classification_metadata.semantic_gate_reason: adversarial refuter (diverse lens, conf 1.00): The patch introduces the `resolveHttpResponse` resolver and adds it to the `impulses.ts` dispatcher. However, the original `httpResponse` shape was meant to be produced by a resolver. In `http-response.ts`, the function `resolveHttpResponse` now produces an `http_response` shape. The key issue is that the resolver returns a `ResolverResult` which has a `shape` field. The current implementation at `src/resolvers/http-response.ts:9` always returns `{ shape: 'http_response', body: 'Invalid pointer type' }` when `pointer.type` is not 'http_response'. This is technically a valid `http_response` shape being returned, but it doesn't represent a 'real' HTTP response as per the gap's intent. More critically, the problem is with the dispatch in `src/routes/impulses.ts` line 393: `return resolveHttpResponse(pointer as { type: "http_response"; url: string; });`. The resolver `resolveHttpResponse` is still producing `http_response` directly, not producing a shape of type `httpResponse` (note the casing difference). Therefore, the system still lacks a producer for the exact shape `httpResponse`. The gap specifically mentions 'httpResponse' (camelCase) and the resolver now produces 'http_response' (snake_case). This is a VIOLATING-LINE-ONLY issue where the name does not match the requested camelCase. [first judge had passed: The patch updates `resolveHttpResponse` to accept a URL from the pointer, and the calling site `impulses.ts` now correctly casts the pointer to provide this URL.]

summary: [narrowed from gap-failure-penalty-survives-a-corrected-specification] A gap's failure penalty is never invalidated when its specification is corrected, so a gap whose spec was WRONG can never be retried once it is right. landabilityScore subtracts min(failed_attempts * 0.1, 0.4) from the rank, and nothing anywhere resets or discounts failed_attempts when the summary, the edit_site or the anchor materially change. OBSERVED TWICE TODAY on the same workstream. First: a gap accumulated 4 attempts against a remediation that the substrate's own adversarial refuters correctly proved insufficient; once the remediation was corrected the gap sat at 0.6 against a competing floor of 0.9 and was never selected again. Second: a gap accumulated 2 attempts failing anchor_not_found because commit 9fd234a shifted its target function from line 774 to 780 and staled its anchor; the anchor was corrected within minutes, but the gap now sat at 0.85, still below 0.9, and went 30 minutes without a retry. In both cases the only way to get the corrected specification tried at all was for the operator to close the gap and re-file it under a new id purely to obtain a clean attempt count. That workaround is indistinguishable from gap-id churn, it discards the gap's real history, and it means the store cannot tell a genuinely unlandable gap from one that was merely mis-specified and has since been fixed. The penalty is measuring the quality of past INSTRUCTIONS while being read as evidence about the TRACTABILITY of the work. Those are different quantities and conflating them makes correction impossible. Invalidate or decay the accumulated penalty when the fields the drafter actually consumes change — summary, edit_site, suspected_real_location and matched_excerpt are the load-bearing ones — for example by storing a hash of those fields alongside the count and zeroing the count when it changes. Do not simply remove the penalty: it correctly buries genuinely unlandable work, which is the behaviour it exists for.

All eight refusals are byte-identical, for the same gap staging src/seed/harness-check-scenario.ts, and all cite the SAME test: 'parity gate'. That test is already on record as the known flaky false-blocker for this gate. TWO COMPOUNDING EFFECTS. First, the gate refuses on tests that are flaky or already failing, attributing them to whatever diff is staged. Second, and worse, a refused gap immediately RETRIES, and because the compose lane is single-occupancy that retry loop monopolises the lane — so every other gap, including the two gaps filed specifically to REPAIR the failing tests, never reaches the gate at all. The system cannot repair the thing that is blocking it, because the blockage consumes the only channel through which the repair could travel. Any fix should address both halves: attribute only tests whose status actually changes between a baseline recomputed on the same tree state, AND back off a gap that has been refused for the same reason more than once so it cannot starve the lane.
classification_metadata.ROOT_CAUSE_FOUND: THE BASELINE SNAPSHOT IS STALE BY 5 TO 8 DAYS AND IS NEVER REFRESHED ON LANDING. Measured 2026-08-26: /workspace/.test-baseline/development-vessel.failnames has mtime 2026-08-18T08:33 and holds 104 entries; /workspace/.test-baseline/development-vessel has mtime 2026-08-21T13:55 and reads '108 1654'. The most recent landed commit, 31c7017, landed at 08:31 on 2026-08-26. So the set the gate calls 'the last landed baseline' predates the last landing by five to eight days. Every test that began failing in that window is absent from the snapshot and is therefore scored as NEWLY FAILING and attributed to whatever diff happens to be staged. Verified directly: the cited 'parity gate' test is NOT in the failnames file, and neither is the node:fetch module error, even though test/resolvers/composition-coverage-report.test.ts has been unrunnable since it was first authored in 631d888. By contrast 'write_proposal writes under' IS in the snapshot and is correctly excluded, which is why the cited count moved from 8 to 6 rather than to 0. The refusal message tells the reader these failures 'will clear once the baseline is refreshed by a green landing', but the file mtimes show the refresh does not happen — landings occurred on 2026-08-26 and the snapshot still dates from 2026-08-18. THE FIX IS THE REFRESH, NOT THE COMPARISON. Write the baseline snapshot on every successful landing, or recompute it on the parent commit of the staged tree at comparison time. Until then this gate blocks every change to this vessel and cannot self-clear, because clearing it requires a green landing and no landing can be green.
classification_metadata.SECOND_ROOT_CAUSE_FLAKY_TEST: TWO INDEPENDENT CAUSES, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS NOW FIXED. Cause one was baseline staleness: the snapshot dated 2026-08-18 omitted 9 tests that fail today, so they were scored as regressions. That snapshot was refreshed from a full clean-tree run at HEAD 31c7017 on 2026-08-26T13:28 (104 fail / 2 errors / 1793 tests, all real failures retained, no gate weakened). Cause two survives and cannot be fixed by any snapshot: src/maintenance/parity-gate.test.ts is NONDETERMINISTIC. Measured by running it three times against the same clean tree at the same commit with an empty git status: run 1 gave 13 pass 0 fail, run 2 gave 13 pass 0 fail, run 3 gave 12 pass 1 fail. A flaky test cannot be represented in a pass/fail baseline: whichever way it lands when the snapshot is taken, the opposite outcome later reads as a status change. This is why refusals resumed within minutes of the refresh, now citing 'parity gate — the safety property > move + body edit of the moved fn FAILs astEquivalent', a test that had PASSED during the baseline run and so is legitimately absent from it. The gate's 'confirmed on a re-run' guard does not help, because a coin-flip test can fail twice in succession. CONSEQUENCE: every landing on this vessel has an independent chance of being blocked at random, from any source, which is precisely the intermittent-refusal pattern already on record for this gate. TWO CANDIDATE REPAIRS, not mutually exclusive: make parity-gate.test.ts deterministic, which is the real fix and is worth doing regardless; and make the gate flake-tolerant by treating a test as newly-failing only when it fails consistently across several runs while the baseline run had it passing consistently, or by maintaining a quarantine list that this test would enter automatically.
classification_metadata.CORRECTED_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08_26_1930: SUPERSEDES the staleness explanation recorded earlier in this gap, which was WRONG on two counts. CORRECTION ONE: the baseline the gate reads is /workspace/post-land-baseline/<vessel>.json, loaded at repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts:1873 where newlyFailing = computeNewlyFailing(baseline, failNow). It is NOT /workspace/.test-baseline/, which is what an earlier operator intervention refreshed; that intervention therefore had no effect on this gate, and any improvement attributed to it was coincidental. CORRECTION TWO: the file is NOT stale. Its mtime is 2026-08-26T08:33:47, written immediately after commit 31c7017 landed at 08:31, so it IS refreshed on landing exactly as the refusal message promises. THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THAT THE CAPTURE IS INCOMPLETE. The post-land baseline holds 25 entries. A full clean run of the suite at the same commit, on a tree with an empty git status, produces 103 distinct failing tests. Roughly 78 genuinely-failing tests are therefore absent from the baseline, and because newlyFailing is failNow minus baseline, every one of them is attributed as a regression to whatever diff happens to be staged. This is why 'DRAFT_SPEC_FROM_GAP_TEMPLATE > write_proposal writes under openspec/changes/...' is cited repeatedly: it fails deterministically on a clean tree — the test asserts the literal {{extract_slug_value}} while the source emits {{extract_slug_text}} — and it is not among the 25. Note the baseline DOES contain 'parity gate', so the flaky-test theory, while independently true, is not what is blocking here. REPAIR: capture the complete failing set post-land rather than a subset. Whatever truncates it — a scoped or partial suite run, a timeout, or a capped result list — must be found, because a baseline that records a quarter of reality converts three quarters of the suite into permanent false regressions and blocks every autonomous landing on this vessel.
classification_metadata.fleet_wide_scope_2026_08_26_2032: THE BASELINE DEFECT IS FLEET-WIDE AND ITS WORST FORM IS AN EMPTY ARRAY. Surveyed /workspace/post-land-baseline/ on 2026-08-26: development-vessel.json is 2638 bytes holding 25 entries against 103 real failures; activity-api.json is 2628 bytes; concept-db has no file at all; and goal-host-vessel.json is TWO BYTES, i.e. the literal empty array []. Under newlyFailing = failNow minus baseline, an empty baseline makes EVERY currently-failing test read as a regression caused by whatever diff is staged, which is the same defect as truncation taken to its limit. A missing file is handled (baseline=null, and the caller fails open), but an EMPTY ARRAY parses successfully and is therefore treated as a legitimate record of 'nothing was failing', which is the most blocking value the field can take. LANDING RATES CORROBORATE THE SCOPE: development-vessel is the only vessel in the fleet to have landed anything on 2026-08-26 (31c7017 at 08:31); goal-host-vessel last landed 08-25 18:08, activity-api 08-25 21:27, metric-collector-vessel 08-21, concept-db 08-18. So this is not one stuck vessel — fleet-wide autonomous landing is close to stopped, and a gate that converts an unpopulated or partial baseline into a universal regression verdict is a sufficient explanation. TWO REPAIRS, BOTH CHEAP: treat an empty array the same as a missing file, i.e. fail open rather than block, since 'no tests were failing at the last landing' is almost never true and is indistinguishable from 'the capture did not run'; and make the post-land capture record the COMPLETE failing set, failing loudly if it cannot, because a partial capture silently converts the remainder of the suite into permanent false regressions.

summary: [narrowed from docs-align-tick-has-no-observed-autonomous-execution] The docs-align detection leg has no observed autonomous execution, so the substrate never sees its own documentation drift unless an operator dispatches the tick by hand. MEASURED 2026-08-26: across the 100 most recent execution traces exactly one carries docs_align, and it is an operator-dispatched walk tagged claude-code-operator; and the gap store had ZERO documentation_drift gaps of any age until that manual dispatch produced the first 23. The machinery is otherwise intact: the rhythm exists as the data-management family whose goal text is run docs_align_tick to assemble the repo docs corpus, scan it against live truth, and file documentation drift gaps, and the tick chains docs_align_scan into docs_align_bridge into substrateGap_write with dry_run defaulting to falsy, which is exactly the chain that produced 23 gaps in 60 seconds when finally invoked. The defect is that nothing invokes it. TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, NEITHER YET DISCRIMINATED, and this gap should not be closed until one is shown to be the cause. FIRST: FAMILY_RESOLVERS at repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/rhythm-conductor-tick.ts:164 maps exactly one family, gap-organizing, to a direct resolver dispatch; every other family including data-management falls to the else branch and is enqueued as a natural-language goal through boredom_enqueue, and the comment immediately above that branch states that this is done instead of enqueuing an NL goal that goal-host cannot walk into an invocation. SECOND: the family may simply never come due under the conductor budget, in which case the enqueue path is never exercised at all. NOT ESTABLISHED, DO NOT ASSUME: that the boredom queue never drains NL goals in general. Boredom is demonstrably live and draining gap-goals, with gap-goal-supply logging candidates and reservations within the same hour. Discriminate by recording whether the conductor ever selects data-management and, if it does, whether the enqueued goal is ever reserved.

[narrowed from recommit-gaps-inherit-a-healthy-category-and-outrank-everything] A failed compose files recommit-<gap.id>-<cls> with a HARDCODED category of systematic_failure (feature-compose.ts:2340). systematic_failure is the healthiest class in /workspace/expectation-calibration.json (6386 attempts / 4334 lands, ~68%), so the recommit gap inherits that land rate, scores landability 1.0, and outranks every fresh gap. Measured over 12h: 73 composeId issued, 2 verdict=FAVORABLE, 3 live-sync rollback, and every pick confined to two targets (route-edit-db8bd146-narrowed on goal-host-vessel/src/goal-intent.reliability-control-5.test.ts and recommit-route-edit-9077062c-typecheck_dangling_reference-narrowed on development-vessel/src/resolvers/http-response.ts), with the runner_up almost always the other member of the same cluster. The existing recommit DEPTH CAP (feature-compose.ts:2333, depth < 2) does not stop this because the source route-edit gap never closes and keeps re-minting fresh depth-1 recommits. This is a grain error: the recommit gap's landability is borrowed from a category whose 68% land rate was earned by unrelated work, while its own lineage has just demonstrably failed. The picker therefore preferentially re-selects exactly the gaps that most recently failed, and the single-occupancy compose lane is consumed by them, starving every other gap in the pool. Same root defect as calibration-counts-killswitch-invocations-as-authoring-failures with the opposite sign. FIX: score a recommit gap against its own lineage (source gap failed_attempts and recommit depth), or give recommit gaps their own calibration key so their real land rate is measured rather than borrowed.

[narrowed from the-hopeless-escalation-asks-a-question-whose-answer-cannot-unseal] When pickMostLandable classifies a gap as hopeless it writes a uiQuestion_write of kind gap_needs_human (gap-to-feature.ts:801) asking a human to redefine the goal, supply missing information, grant access, or drop the gap. That escalation is the designed relief valve for the hard exclusion, and it cannot work, because the exclusion predicate consults nothing the answer could change. hopeless() (gap-to-feature.ts:778-781) reads readCalibration() and only readCalibration(), returning on calib[category].attempts >= 8 && lands === 0. No answer field, operator verdict, disposition, or override is read at the exclusion site. A human can answer all 73 escalated gaps perfectly and every one remains excluded, because the only quantity that unseals a category is a LAND recorded in the calibration file, and a land requires a pick the exclusion prevents. The nearest reader, solicitation_outcome_scan, only reports outcomes for solicitation_ids explicitly supplied to it (solicitation-outcome-scan.ts:32 returns 'no solicitation_ids supplied' otherwise); it is a reporting scan over obsidian interaction episodes, not a path from an answered question back to gap selectability. A question with no read-at-use-time path is an archive. FIX: the exclusion must consult a human disposition alongside the calibration record, so that answering the escalation has the effect the escalation implicitly promises.

[narrowed from a-capacity-refusal-is-counted-as-a-failed-authoring-attempt] feature-compose returns verdict BUSY when the single-occupancy autonomous compose lane is full, and documents at feature-compose.ts:2541 that this is 'BUSY, not REFUSED. Capacity is TRANSIENT — the work is fine, the host is [busy]'. gap-to-feature.ts does not read that distinction: the string BUSY does not occur anywhere in the file, while there are nine bumpFailedAttempts call sites. A gap refused purely because the lane was occupied is therefore penalised as though its authoring had failed.

MEASURED, 2026-08-27 10:58-11:15Z. Gap unseal-documentation-drift-replace-one-line-in-hopeless was picked repeatedly and never composed once: zero fc-plan lines in the window contain its unique anchor signature 'r.attempts >= 8' (the only fc-plan entries in the window targeted a different gap's anchor), while nine 'REFUSING autonomous compose' lines were logged. Over the same window its score fell from 1.26 to 0.96 and its landability from 0.84 to 0.64, a 0.2 drop consistent with failed_attempts moving 0 to 2 under the min(fa*0.1, 0.4) penalty. No authoring attempt occurred, and two failures were recorded.

TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) Selection becomes a function of lane timing rather than gap quality. The busier the lane, the more gaps are penalised for the lane being busy, and penalised gaps sink, so the queue self-selects toward whichever gaps happened to arrive when a slot was free. A gap can be starved indefinitely without ever being attempted. (2) It feeds the permanent seal. bumpFailedAttempts calls updateCalibration(category, false) at gap-to-feature.ts:1970 before it does anything else, so every capacity refusal also advances the CATEGORY counter toward hopeless()'s attempts >= 8 && lands === 0 threshold. This is a third independent source of seal poisoning alongside triage-only routes (calibration-counts-killswitch-invocations-as-authoring-failures) and failed network persists (category-counter-outlives-the-per-gap-counter-on-any-activity-api-blip).

FIX: a BUSY result must not reach bumpFailedAttempts at all. Return the gap to the queue unpenalised, exactly as the producing layer's own comment intends. This is a consuming-layer defect: the producer distinguishes transient capacity from failure and the consumer discards the distinction.

A commit pushed to origin/dev (goal-host f91f8f2) fetched into the in-container clone but NEVER mirrored into the running /vessels copy — the change is durable on origin/dev but not deployed. Restarting goal-host to break the wait only requeues the interrupted dispatches, which re-saturate it, so the deadlock persists.

Independently documented: test/setup-spool-isolation.ts ('spool files were exec_test_1 debris written by test runs'), validation/reports/SEAM_PROBE_BASELINE_2026-08-21.md ('81 of 83 spool files were exec_test_1 debris'), SELF_DEVELOPMENT_WIRING_AUDIT.md, COMPOSITIONALITY_STATE.md. NOT a production config leak (my first framing) and NOT a live test execution (my second) — it is persistent test-debris in the shared spool. FIX: purge the exec_test_1 spool entries and isolate the test spool from the live spool (setup-spool-isolation.ts is the in-test half; the live spool needs the same isolation or a poison-message drop after N failures against an unreachable host). (B) STILL OPEN, not root-caused: intermittent `routedComplete not ok` (LLM completion dispatch failing) breaks the recompute's second-derivation authoring → layer-1 abstention regardless of Option A retry; cause (resolver overload from walk fan-out? resolver health?) undetermined — needs its own investigation.

classification_metadata.premise_correction_2026_08_28: PREMISE CORRECTION - the operator overstated this gap and the correction matters more than the fix. The wire is now complete (92c991d forwards body.metadata.information_yield at the ingest call site; 0772deb landed the consumer check), and the code is correct. But its BEHAVIOURAL effect today is NIL, and the original claim that idle activities 'accumulate strong positive posteriors for doing no work' is NOT SUBSTANTIATED by current data. MEASURED: every activity currently emitting information_yield 'idle' already had a FROZEN thompson_alpha before the fix - exactly one distinct alpha value across the 6 hours preceding it, for llm-api-health-observer-tick, mitosis-tick, detect-poison-producer, detect-execution_error_ribosome_extract, docs-decision-deliver and gap-to-scenario-bridge-tick (the last held 6029.532371760352 across 14500->14613 executions). CAUSE: these are deterministic detector ticks. A sampled idle trace reports resolver_tier 'deterministic' on every task, so tierClass === 'all_deterministic' already set skipVariantUpdate via the pre-existing M4 tier-restricted bandit gate. The alpha=728.887 on docs-decision-deliver at 1495 executions is a HISTORICAL value, frozen since at least 2026-08-25, not ongoing accrual. WHAT THE FIX IS ACTUALLY WORTH: it is defensive and correct for a case that does not currently occur - a PATTERN or LLM tier activity reporting idle yield would have been credited before and is skipped now. It should not be described as fixing an active leak. NOT CLOSING this gap on 'the code landed': there is no consequence test that can currently discriminate, because the population the fix targets is empty. ROOT CAUSE FOUND (updated 2026-08-28, verified live). The list handler's projection is OPT-IN and its default is INVERTED relative to its own documented contract. repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts:732 reads exactly:
    const summaryProjection =
      fieldsParam === 'summary' || detailParam !== 'true';
detailParam is c.req.query('detail'), which is undefined when the caller does not pass it, and undefined !== 'true' is TRUE — so summaryProjection defaults to TRUE and every unadorned caller gets the NARROW projection. The comment immediately above (lines ~718-731) states the opposite and predicts this exact failure: "The DEFAULT projection is left WIDE and unchanged — many autonomous consumers (development-vessel resolvers, boredom-vessel) read metadata, composition_chain, failure_mode, and input/output_impulse_shapes off this list response, so narrowing the default would silently break them." It did.

VERIFIED LIVE in-container against http://127.0.0.1:8080/v2/activities/execution-traces with header 'Authorization: ApiKey <key>':
  ?limit=3            -> rows contain failure_mode_type scalar; NO metadata, NO output_impulse_shapes
  ?limit=3&detail=true -> same rows contain full failure_mode:{type} AND the complete metadata object
The data is present in the table; only the default projection hides it.

CONSEQUENCE: nine development-vessel resolvers read those fields off this endpoint and every read is wrapped in a tolerant catch or continue, so each degrades to a clean healthy zero rather than an error. Confirmed blind: coverage_tick (reachable_learned always 0), trace_outcome_validity_audit (skips 100/100 traces, all 5 rules dead), detector_coverage_scan (uncovered_clusters always 0), posterior_consistency_audit (compares 2656 posteriors against ~35 minutes of traces). Because coverage_tick computes reachable_learned as advertised INTERSECT learned and learned is structurally empty, coverage_progress can never be true and the S1-to-S2 lift gate (three consecutive coverageReports with coverage_progress true) is structurally unreachable.

FIX (one line, one file): at execution-traces.ts:732 change `detailParam !== 'true'` to `detailParam === 'false'` so the wide projection is the default and narrowing stays opt-in via ?fields=summary or ?detail=false, matching the comment. Do NOT change the selectFields branches at :887 — the wide branch already lists failure_mode, metadata, output_impulse_shapes, input_impulse_shapes correctly. Separately the limit clamp at :736 (Math.min(Math.max(limitParam,1),100)) makes every window_hours parameter in the consuming instruments fiction — a 720h audit actually covers ~35 minutes — but that is a second, independent defect and should not be bundled into this edit.

PREDICATE PROVEN LIVE, not merely unblocked: detector_meta_scan invoked with a synthetic snapshot containing one zero-pick detector row returns detectors_known 2, active 1, dormant_count 1, finding_count 1, naming development-vessel:cyclic-flow-scan. Fix landed as commit f34547e on origin/dev (goal-host-vessel): a new src/shaped-policy-store.ts serves the STORED document for both shapes, and both are now advertised in SHAPES. Same contract as bodyHonestyPolicy and walkBudget, which fixed this exact defect class on 2026-08-16 - serve the stored document so behaviour is editable data, serve nothing when none is stored so the consumer keeps its documented literal. CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED: (1) both shapes now appear in the discovery registry, where they were absent from all 385 before; (2) with no file stored each resolves to a structured 404 'no <shape> configured - consumer keeps its literal fallback' rather than having no producer at all; (3) with a document at WORKSPACE_ROOT/policies/<shape>.json each resolves 200 carrying the stored body - extractionPolicy {maxExtractionDepth:7} and pathwayReusePolicy {minSuccessfulExecutions:3,minTotalExecutions:5}; (4) goal-host logged 5 fallback lines in 11:30-11:54 and ZERO since 11:56, against 48 log lines of other activity in the same window proving the vessel is live. That fallback line is emitted ONLY when source === 'fallback-literal'. A TRAP WORTH RECORDING: WORKSPACE_ROOT on this deployment is /workspace/git/super-repo, so the canonical policy directory is /workspace/git/super-repo/policies - NOT /workspace/policies, which also exists and holds a stale divergent set (an older body-honesty-policy.json and llm-model-policy.json). Seeding the wrong directory yields a perfectly honest 404 that is indistinguishable from a broken reader; that is exactly what happened on the first attempt here. walk-budget.ts already documents the same hazard in its own comments. REMAINING, not closed by this change: extractionEligibilityPolicy (ribosome-vessel/src/index.ts:178, ungradableProducers) is the third shape of this family and still has no producer. It needs the same treatment in the ribosome, where its reader lives - the producer belongs with the consumer per law 11, which is why it was not bundled into a goal-host commit.

summary: The mitosis pre-cutover test gate reports failures as INTRODUCED BY THE PATCH when they are artifacts of the filesystem churning underneath a test that scans the live tree, so verified-safe patches are silently refused. OBSERVED 2026-08-28T06:28:54Z: a one-token patch to repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts (detailParam !== 'true' -> detailParam === 'false') applied cleanly via fs_edit at 06:27:26, passed bun run typecheck (mitosis-evaluate static_checks_pass), and received mitosis-cutover gate verdict=FAVORABLE at 06:28:28 — then at 06:28:54 was refused with 'evaluate_refused:tests_failed: 1 failure(s) INTRODUCED by this patch: trace boundary - the write and read agree on key names > THE REGRESSION'. DISPROOF, run three ways: (1) that test file, src/routes/trace-key-agreement.test.ts, EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES the patched file from its scan corpus at the Glob filter `if (f.endsWith('.test.ts') || f.endsWith('/routes/execution-traces.ts')) continue` — it structurally cannot observe this edit; (2) `bun test src/routes/trace-key-agreement.test.ts` on the unpatched /vessels/activity-api tree gives 4 pass / 0 fail; (3) the same command on a clean cp -a copy WITH the patch applied also gives 4 pass / 0 fail. LIKELY MECHANISM: that test Glob-scans the live src/ directory and asserts sources.length > 50 plus corpus content; substrate-pull-sync was mirroring vessels into /vessels during the gate window (06:40:29 '[mirror-to-live] activity-api mirrored (7167628)'), and mitosis staging roots are created and removed concurrently, so the scanned corpus differs between the baseline and patched runs for reasons unrelated to the diff. A gate that attributes an environment-dependent failure to the patch cannot be trusted when it passes either — the same defect class as a verification gate with no call sites. FIX DIRECTION (do not bundle): the gate must distinguish a failure the patch CAUSED from one that also reproduces on the unpatched baseline in the SAME environment — re-run the named failing test on the base tree at refusal time and only attribute it to the patch if the base passes; and quarantine tests that scan the live filesystem from the introduced-failure comparison entirely.

classification_metadata.root_cause: baseline runs on the real tree, patched runs in a symlink overlay; Bun Glob does not traverse symlinks
classification_metadata.mechanism_2026_08_28: MECHANISM ESTABLISHED (was 'environment flake', now exact). buildOverlay() in vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts symlinks every top-level entry of baseRoot into a temp overlay, then materializes REAL directories only along the path of each staged file. Inside a materialized dir, test files are REAL COPIES (deliberate, see the 2026-08-09 comment at line ~375: a symlinked test resolves its relative imports against baseRoot and would test the UNPATCHED source) while every other entry is a SYMLINK. For a patch to src/routes/execution-traces.ts the overlay therefore contains real dirs src/ and src/routes/, whose only REAL files are the test files plus the staged file; all other sources are symlinks. src/routes/trace-key-agreement.test.ts, being a real copy, resolves import.meta.url to the OVERLAY and Globs '**/*.ts' under overlay/src. BUN'S Glob.scan DOES NOT TRAVERSE SYMLINKS - measured directly: 1 visible .ts in a symlinked tree versus 212 via `find -L`. So its corpus is (test files) + (execution-traces.ts), both of which its own filter EXCLUDES, leaving zero sources, and `expect(sources.length).toBeGreaterThan(50)` - the assertion whose comment reads 'guards the scan itself' - fires. It is correctly detecting that it is blind. Meanwhile the BASELINE suite runs against the real baseRoot (212 files) and passes, so the delta reports the difference as INTRODUCED BY THE PATCH. SCOPE: this misfires only for a vessel containing a test that scans the source tree. Fleet census: activity-api 1 such test file, development-vessel 0, goal-host-vessel 0, concept-db 0. So the defect currently makes activity-api un-landable through the autonomous path while leaving the repair site itself landable. FIX DIRECTION: the asymmetry is the bug. Run the BASELINE suite in an overlay built the SAME way - same staged relative paths, base-tree content - so the two runs are structurally identical and differ only in file CONTENT. Any overlay artifact then fails in both runs and the delta correctly reports 0 introduced. Cheaper alternatives (copying all sources, or quarantining tree-scanning tests from the comparison) are strictly worse: the first defeats the cheap-overlay property the design depends on, the second silently drops real coverage. Note baselineSuiteCache (line ~180) is keyed by base root, so the cached baseline must be keyed by overlay shape too or it will reintroduce the same asymmetry.

[])` at vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts:876 - so an overlay artifact fails on BOTH sides and cancels out of the delta. CONSEQUENCE OBSERVED: before the fix, four consecutive refusals citing 'N failure(s) INTRODUCED by this patch' (three on activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts, one on this very file). After the fix: ZERO such refusals, and the first patch evaluated against the new gate LANDED - commit 9ac885c, author 'Substrate Autonomous', on origin/dev, with no operator hands. The cutover's own citation now reads cited_checks=["typecheck","shape-dispatch","bun test (baseline-delta, flake-confirmed)"]: the delta correctly identifies the failure as reproducing on both sides rather than attributing it to the diff. This was closed resolution=already_resolved by Class-3 landed-commit provenance. Two commits reference the gap id: 52452e0 (a destructive fix that landed over a semantic-gate refusal) and de354d1 (the operator revert of it). Net code change across the pair is ZERO and the stored data was never repaired. Provenance counted that a commit exists; it did not ask whether the commit survived or worked.

THE DEFECT IS LIVE AND TAKES ONE QUERY:
  SELECT week, reached, total FROM reach_history  ->  week 2026-08-17 total = 414944
  SELECT count() FROM execution GROUP ALL         ->  19288
The weekly counter claims 21.5x more executions for a single week than have ever existed.

A Class-2 predicate is now declared so provenance can no longer close this. It ABSTAINS rather than measures, because no vessel advertises a reachHistory shape — stated plainly so nobody reads the predicate as a working verifier. This gap will not auto-close until either a shape exposes reach_history or the data is repaired.

NOTE ON THE ORIGINAL FILING: the summary below blames the ADDITIVE upsert. That framing is questionable — the SELECT is watermarked, so totals MUST accumulate; replacing the accumulation is what made 52452e0 destructive. The real defect is the INFLATED HISTORICAL ROWS, which no code change removes and which require a recompute or truncate.

--- original text follows ---
In repos/activity-api/src/services/trace-retention.ts, the rollupReachHistory function folded reach counts into reach_history with an ADDITIVE UPSERT: `reached = (reached ?? 0) + $reached,` and `total = (total ?? 0) + $total,`. Because the bucket UPSERT is additive while the watermark UPSERT is a separate statement issued afterwards, any run whose bucket writes succeed while the watermark write fails or lags re-adds the same rows on the next run, inflating the weekly totals monotonically. Measured 2026-08-28: week 2026-08-17 reported total=414944 against an execution table holding 17116 rows across its entire retained window — 24x more than every execution row that has ever existed in the store, making the week-over-week reach trend unusable. Series was 11/11, 22/33, 1689/7752, 146/414944, 144/4975. PREDICATE ADDED 2026-08-28 (file_path + hardcoded_url): the defect IS the presence of the literal additive expression in the running copy, so its absence there is a measurement that the condition is gone rather than a claim that a commit happened. This is the Class-1 surgical check in gap-to-feature.ts verifyGapCondition — it reads /vessels/<vessel>/... and returns 'present' if the literal is found, 'absent' if it is not. It was missing when this gap was filed, which left the gap structurally unclosable by measurement (see gap prose-only-gaps-are-structurally-unclosable-so-the-ttl-becomes-their-only-exit); supplying it is the filer's job and was my omission.

summary: CORRECTED 2026-08-28: an earlier version of this gap claimed no test-baseline mechanism existed. That was wrong — it exists. The real defect is narrower and worse: the mechanism only ever polices REGRESSIONS and never the absolute level, and it absorbs red state into its own baseline permanently. In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts the post-land suite runs after each promotion (line ~2451), maintains a per-vessel baseline file of failing test ids, and files a substrateGap id post-land-suite-red-<vessel> in category systematic_failure. But the emission is guarded at line 2482 by `if (sb.ran === true && _newlyFailing.length > 0)`, where _newlyFailing is the set-difference against the stored baseline. A vessel whose tests have been failing for months has an empty _newlyFailing set, so nothing is ever filed and it reads as healthy. Worse, the baseline is rewritten unconditionally at line ~2477 with `writeFile(_baseFile, JSON.stringify(_failNow))`, so the current red set becomes the accepted normal on every pass — a one-way ratchet in which failures are absorbed, never surfaced. Measured consequence at origin/dev 17aae9a: `bun test` in development-vessel reports 99 distinct failing tests across 1794 tests / 236 files, including 4 in the suite literally named 'detectors are wired to something that runs them'. Three of those failures dated to c053d77 on 2026-06-12 and had been red for eleven weeks with nothing detecting them (fixed by operator in ce95539). No component anywhere asks whether a landed baseline is green. Repair: add an absolute-level check alongside the delta check — when the post-land suite reports fail > 0 at a landed HEAD, file or refresh a standing gap naming the failing test ids and their count, independent of whether they are newly failing; and stop letting an unexplained rise in the baseline count be written silently. The typecheck analogue for comparison already treats an absolute broken baseline as first-class: repos/boredom-vessel/src/index.ts line 2258 gives any id starting with baseline-typecheck-broken- PRIORITY_WEIGHT_HIGH, and repos/boredom-vessel/src/goal-generation.ts line 131 sorts those ahead of every category weight. Tests deserve the same absolute treatment, not only a delta.

summary:
pickMostLandable in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts ranks gaps that are in the 'pending verification' state at the top of the pool, wins the pick with them, and only then discovers they cannot be composed. The cycle ends without falling through to the next candidate, so the pick is consumed by a no-op.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MAKING THE PENDING BRANCH RE-COMPOSE. The skip at gap-to-feature.ts:2501-2508 is CORRECT AND DELIBERATE. Its comment states the reason: 'Landed once but unmeasured - do NOT re-compose (a second landing manufactures a re-land the close-oracle would score as a false-close). The sweep + human escalation own it. (§12.6 step 1)'. Removing or weakening that guard would manufacture false closes. The bug is upstream of the guard, in RANKING and in the pending state never resolving - not in the guard itself.

Measured over 60 minutes on the live fleet: 59 total picks, 22 of them skipped as pending = 37.3% of picker throughput consumed by no-ops. recommit-route-edit-9077062c-typecheck_dangling_reference-narrowed was picked 11 times and skipped 11 times, a 100% no-op rate, because its category-inherited landability of 1.0 and impact 1.5 give it score 1.5 - the highest in the pool - on every cycle. systematic-failure-universal-tool-fallback-zero consumed 6 more, route-edit-85922d48 consumed 5.

Two distinct repairs, both upstream of the guard:
(1) RANKING: a gap in the pending state is known-unworkable at rank time, so it should be filtered from the selection pool BEFORE scoring, or the picker should continue down the ranked list to the first non-pending candidate instead of returning. Either converts a wasted cycle into a productive one.
(2) STUCK PENDING STATE: recommit-route-edit-9077062c-typecheck_dangling_reference-narrowed has created_at 2026-08-16T16:26:52Z and is still pending-unmeasured as of 2026-08-28T09:22Z - twelve days. The comment says 'the sweep + human escalation own it', but neither has resolved it in twelve days, so the pending state is effectively terminal rather than transient. summary: Most gaps are closed because no detector re-emitted them, not because the condition was fixed, so the close-rate metric measures DETECTOR LIVENESS rather than repair. Measured over an 800-gap sample from the live store: 450 closed, of which 331 carry the literal marker '[expired by gap_lifecycle_scan] ... not re-detected within 336h TTL; detector liveness (upsert-by-id) says this is likely no longer valid' — 74 percent of all closures. Only ~119 closures are attributable to anything other than expiry. The emitter is repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-lifecycle-scan.ts around line 447, which posts substrateGap_write with status 'closed' and classification_metadata.closed_reason 'expired_not_redetected'. The condition itself is never re-checked before closing; the code's own wording concedes the inference is weak ('likely no longer valid'). This matters for law 7, which makes gap close rate the first measure of progress: a close rate computed over this store is ~74 percent an artifact of TTL sweeps. The funnel figures I measured earlier (close_rate 0.693 -> 0.688 -> 0.683 over 2026-08-27) should be read as roughly one quarter resolution and three quarters expiry. It also fails the durability leg (law 7 measure 3) by construction: a persisting condition whose detector stops firing is closed, then re-opens later under a different id, which is exactly 'gaps reappearing wearing different hats'. WORKED EXAMPLE, SELF-CONCEALING: gap 'gap-picker-cannot-detect-its-own-livelock' was substrate_detected on 2026-08-23 having measured 432 picks consumed by the pending-verification no-op. It was closed at 2026-08-28T03:43:44 as expired_not_redetected. The condition was still live: on 2026-08-28 the same livelock was measured at 50 picks in 6 hours against gap recommit-route-edit-9077062c-typecheck_dangling_reference-narrowed. The closure removed the system's own record of a defect that was still running, and the loop is self-concealing because a picker starved by the livelock is less likely to re-run the detector that would re-emit it. FIX: before expiring a gap, re-evaluate its condition predicate where one exists, and where none exists mark the gap 'unverifiable' or hand it to the pending-verify path rather than closing it green. At minimum, report expiry separately from resolution everywhere a close rate is published, so the metric stops overstating repair.

summary:
DO NOT CLOSE THIS AS already_resolved ON SYMPTOM ABSENCE. The observable rate is TRANSIENT and has already gone to zero once while the code defect remained fully intact. Measured 2026-08-28: at 10:05 the rate was a flat 28 requests/minute sustained across 5-, 15- and 30-minute windows (141 / 424 / 848 occurrences of '[oracle-label] NOT consumed'), with 843 of the 848 attributable to ONE execution id, walk-satisfier-3-1787907941577, polled since 09:05 and logged 1266 times in 90 minutes (~1700 activity-api POSTs/hour). By 11:37 that same measurement read 1 occurrence in 15 minutes (~0/min) because that single long-lived dispatch had aged out of the active set. NOTHING WAS FIXED between those two readings. A pick-time condition check that samples the current rate will therefore find the condition 'absent' and close this as already_resolved while the defect is untouched. Verify the CODE PATH is bounded, not the current rate.

THE DEFECT. The poll-time oracle-label consumption block in repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts (~lines 15113-15170) re-fetches the label corpus on every poll, without bound, for any execution that never receives a human label. One sufficiently long-lived dispatch is enough to sustain ~28 requests/minute indefinitely against activity-api.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY BURNING THE LATCH ON MACHINE LABELS. That behaviour is deliberate and documented inline: 'SOURCE-AWARE LATCH: only a HUMAN verdict burns the consumption latch. recordDeterministicLabel mirrors EVERY oracle verdict into the corpus as a deterministic/automated row at verdict time, so a machine label is always present before the operator can speak. Burning the latch on it made the human branch below structurally unreachable - 0 HUMAN reach override lines in 48h against 81 machine consumptions.' Setting learn.oracleLabelWritten on a machine label would re-break the human override path this code was specifically repaired to restore.

The defect is that 'do not latch' was implemented as 'retry unboundedly at poll frequency'. The consumption should stay open to a later human label without re-querying at poll rate forever. Bound it while preserving the human window: exponential per-execution backoff up to a ceiling of minutes; and/or stop re-polling once the dispatch is terminal and older than the window in which a human realistically responds; and/or invert the flow so a human label WRITE notifies the dispatch rather than the dispatch polling for it.

CLOSURE CRITERION: this gap is closed when the re-poll is bounded IN CODE and a long-lived ungraded dispatch no longer sustains a fixed poll-rate query stream - not when the current rate happens to read zero.

summary: The precutover_regression check compares the staged tree's failing tests against a STORED SNAPSHOT from the last green landing, not against a fresh run of the current tree, so once a vessel's tests degrade for unrelated reasons every subsequent cutover is blamed for them and refused - and the refusal prevents the green landing that would refresh the snapshot. SELF-SEALING, and the code says so itself: the refusal message reads 'if these are known-flaky, they will clear once the baseline is refreshed by a green landing', but a green landing must first pass this gate. MECHANISM (vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts, the CUTOVER_PRECHECK_SUITE block ending at the softRefuse near line 1880): `const baseFile = /workspace/post-land-baseline/<vessel>.json; baseline = JSON.parse(readFile(baseFile)); newlyFailing = computeNewlyFailing(baseline, failNow)`. failNow is a real run of the STAGED tree; baseline is a file. MEASURED 2026-08-28: /workspace/post-land-baseline/development-vessel.json was last modified 2026-08-26 08:33 - over two days stale - and records 25 failing tests. At 10:42:22 a cutover was refused with 'precutover_regression: 8 test(s) fail on the staged tree that passed at the last landed baseline, confirmed on a re-run - e.g. (fail) autocomplete-concept-writer: buildConceptWritePointer'. DISPROOF: that test fails on a CLEAN git-HEAD checkout with no patch applied - `bun test test/observers/autocomplete-concept-writer.test.ts` on an unpatched copy gives 7 pass / 2 fail. The staged change was four lines in src/resolvers/orphaned-capability-scan.ts (a boolean guard) and cannot affect buildConceptWritePointer. The gate had already returned verdict=FAVORABLE with cited_checks typecheck, shape-dispatch and bun test (baseline-delta, flake-confirmed) 2 minutes earlier; this second gate then refused and rolled back ('live-sync rollback: no cutover pushed - restored 1/1 live file(s)'). CONSEQUENCE: development-vessel has landed 2 substrate-authored commits in 71.5h. NOTE the confirm-on-re-run guard does not help: a genuinely pre-existing failure reproduces on both runs, so re-running only filters single flakes, not stale-baseline drift. FIX DIRECTION: measure the baseline the same way the comparison side is measured - run the suite once on the UNPATCHED tree at refusal time and attribute a failure to the patch only if it does not reproduce there. This is the same asymmetry, and the same fix, as gap precutover-gate-attributes-environment-flake-to-the-patch (landed as 17aae9a in vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts). Failing that, refresh the stored baseline whenever it is older than the vessel's HEAD commit. DO NOT 'fix' this by setting CUTOVER_PRECHECK_SUITE=0 - that disables a real safety gate wholesale and is env-gated behaviour the learning loop cannot observe.

classification_metadata.close_criteria: CONSEQUENCE TEST: stage a change that cannot affect the cited tests (e.g. a boolean guard in an unrelated resolver) while /workspace/post-land-baseline/<vessel>.json is older than the vessel's HEAD commit. The cutover must either land it, or refuse with a failure set that does NOT reproduce on a clean git-HEAD checkout of the same tree. A refusal naming tests that fail unpatched is a regression of this gap.
classification_metadata.closed_note: CLOSED 2026-08-28, verified by the consequence test recorded on this gap. Fix landed BY HAND as commit cf28f52 on origin/dev (development-vessel): a post-land baseline older than BASELINE_MAX_AGE_MS (24h) is now treated as unusable and routed down the fail-open path the file already had for an unmeasurable baseline (computeNewlyFailing(null, now) === []). The check is NOT disabled - a baseline under 24h is still authoritative - and the repair is self-healing, because the first green landing rewrites the snapshot after which the gate discriminates correctly again. Deliberately NOT fixed via CUTOVER_PRECHECK_SUITE=0, which would disable a real safety gate wholesale and is env-gated behaviour the learning loop cannot observe. CONSEQUENCE OBSERVED: before the fix, development-vessel had landed 2 substrate-authored commits in 71.5 hours and its baseline file had been frozen since 2026-08-26 08:33. Within roughly 15 minutes of the fix going live, TWO substrate-authored commits landed on origin/dev with no operator hands - d7fa981 (route-edit-b7e00c9e) and 90e022c (route-edit-5bf11524) - and precutover_regression refusals since the fix number ZERO. One of those autonomous landings is itself independently verified: the substrate composed and landed the accuracy-predicate tightening in docs-align-scan.ts line 248, changing `(?:\w+\s+)*shape` to `shapes?\b` so the proximity guard requires adjacency. Its acceptance test passes - docs_align_scan with invariants [accuracy] and all 385 live advertised shapes over five shape-heavy documents now returns 0 findings, where before it returned 2 FALSE positives flagging the field names `columns` and `sample` in the sentence 'columns, and sample where the shape is tabular'. CHARACTERISATION CORRECTED TWICE — THE PATTERN IS INTERMITTENT.

24h hourly profile of 'Started activity-api.service' (measured 2026-08-29T04:10Z):
  Aug 28  04:00-13:00   8, 20, 37, 8, 39, 60, 63, 60, 9, 4

Roughly 755 restarts in 24 hours, peaking at 79/hr, in PAIRS (two systemctl restarts racing; the second 'Stopping' 14ms after the first 'Started').

BOTH OF MY EARLIER CHARACTERISATIONS WERE WRONG, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. This record first carried 'symptom_is_transient_do_not_close_on_absence', written after sampling a quiet stretch. I then removed that flag and asserted the storm had run 'continuously for 21 hours' — measured over a window whose trailing 17 minutes were already silent. Neither is true: there is a six-hour zero period in the middle of the day and 20+ minute gaps within active periods. The honest word is INTERMITTENT.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: a quiet sample is not evidence of resolution (the original flag's instinct was right even though its premise was wrong), and an active sample is not evidence of continuity. Any verdict on this gap must cite an hourly profile, not a point measurement.

STILL TRUE AND UNEXPLAINED: systemd reports NRestarts=0 / ActiveState=active throughout, so systemd is not the restarter and an external caller is signalling the unit. self-recovery (recovered_by_restart:0 every tick) and pull-sync (one restart in 90 minutes, and of goal-host) are both eliminated by direct evidence. A 100-second 0.25s-interval process scan failed to catch a caller — the restart pair completes in ~300ms, and no restart occurred during the scan window.

WHY IT CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED: filed separately as restart-attribution-is-wired-for-one-vessel-only-so-every-other-restart-is-unattributed. The breadcrumb at /workspace/restart-requests/activity-api.json is stale (pull-sync, 02:11:12Z) against a 600s freshness window, and no vessel except development-vessel reports its own start attribution.

39 'Started activity-api.service' events in the last 60 minutes; 281 Started/Stopping/Stopped lifecycle events in the last 2 hours. systemd simultaneously reports NRestarts=0, ActiveState=active, SubState=running — the exact false-clean signature this gap was filed on. CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD'S OWN METADATA: it previously carried 'symptom_is_transient_do_not_close_on_absence', written when the storm appeared to stop on its own. That flag was wrong in its premise — the symptom was never transient, it was unobserved. It has now run continuously for ~21 hours. The flag is removed rather than left to justify a future close on a quiet sample.

NRestarts=0 means systemd is NOT the restarter: something external is signalling the unit. That is still unidentified and is the open question.

--- original text follows ---
DO NOT CLOSE THIS AS already_resolved ON SYMPTOM ABSENCE - THE STORM HAS ALREADY STOPPED ONCE WITH THE CAUSE STILL UNIDENTIFIED. Two readings, same day, no code change and no identified fix between them: at 11:17 activity-api had 79 'Started activity-api.service' events in 60 minutes and 61 seconds of uptime; by 16:40 it had ZERO starts in 90 minutes and 3h07m continuous uptime (ExecMainStartTimestamp 13:33:42). The journal covers the whole period (oldest entry Aug 25, 1308 lifetime Started lines), so the zero is real and not a retention artifact. NOBODY FIXED ANYTHING. The restarter was never identified, so a quiet fleet is not evidence the cause is gone - only that it is not currently firing. Verify the CAUSE, not the current rate.

ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT. 79 starts in 60 minutes, restarts arriving in PAIRS every 40-90s (11:14:26, 11:14:27, 11:14:49, 11:14:50, 11:15:42 x2, 11:15:56 x2, 11:16:37, 11:16:38, 11:18:05, 11:18:06, 11:18:59 x2). At 11:16:37 two full stop/start cycles inside one second; at 11:37:21 'Started' immediately followed by 'Stopping'.

MECHANISM ESTABLISHED. The service receives SIGTERM and exits 0: '[Server] SIGTERM received, shutting down gracefully' -> Discovery deregister -> '[Server] Graceful shutdown complete'. Because the exit is clean, Restart=on-failure never fires and NRestarts stays 0. Each start re-runs ExecStartPre init-database.ts ('Migration complete: 214/214'), so the fleet paid a full migration check every ~45 seconds.

WHY EVERY HEALTH CHECK MISSED IT. ActiveState=active and NRestarts=0 BOTH reported clean throughout. NRestarts counts ONLY systemd's own Restart= policy; an external systemctl restart never increments it. The heuristic 'a restart loop reports activating, never failed - ask NRestarts, not is-active' does NOT cover this, because both checks pass. WORKING DISCRIMINATORS: journal 'Started <unit>' count over a window, or ExecMainStartTimestamp freshness vs wall clock.

RESTARTER STILL NOT IDENTIFIED - ELIMINATIONS so the next investigator does not repeat them. NOT self-recovery (healthy:14, recovered_by_restart:0). NOT substrate-pull-sync (6 runs/60m; targets development-vessel; DEFERS restarts while dispatches are in flight). NOT mitosis cutover (8 mitosis-self-restart-* units in the window, ALL development-vessel). NOT file-sync/hot-reload (/vessels/activity-api/src mtime hours stale; no watcher in ps). NOT a systemd trigger (no .path/.timer/.socket for activity-api; Restart= never fired). NOT trace-store-health-check (oneshot reader; itself a victim, failing 'Unable to connect'). NOT perf-canary-resolve (contains `systemctl restart ${restartUnit}` and probes :8080 but logged ZERO activity in the window). NOT a shell-tool invocation (zero systemctl strings, zero shell-resolver activity fleet-wide in 30m). A 60-second tight ps poll for systemctl/vessel-ctl caught nothing while 2 restarts occurred within 3 minutes, so the most likely remaining candidate is a long-running process issuing the restart over systemd's DBUS API without forking a binary.

TIMING CORRELATION WORTH TESTING, NOT ASSERTED. The storm was observed during the window in which compose/cutover activity was repeatedly iterating on repos/activity-api/src/services/trace-retention.ts, and it ceased after that work stopped and the operator reverted commit 52452e0 at ~12:10. That is a co-occurrence, not a demonstrated cause - the compose loop restarting its own target vessel would fit the pair-wise pattern and the dbus hypothesis, but it was NOT confirmed and mitosis-self-restart units were only ever seen for development-vessel. Test it by driving repeated compose/cutover cycles against an activity-api file and watching the start count.

SECONDARY WORK: make restart attribution TOTAL. The restart-attribution detector fired 5x with 'UNATTRIBUTED START - the only breadcrumb is stale (requester=pull-sync ...). Reporting unattributed rather than guessing.' The detector is correct to refuse; only pull-sync writes a breadcrumb. Every restart-capable path must write one.

CLOSURE CRITERION: the restarter is IDENTIFIED and either removed or made to write an attribution breadcrumb - not that the current start count reads zero.

summary:
An operator-corrected gap summary was OVERWRITTEN by shorter machine-derived text, and the adversarial refuters in the semantic gate then reasoned from the overwritten summary and REJECTED A CORRECT FIX while arguing for a change that would destroy data. Metadata survived the overwrite but did not prevent the misdirection, because the refuters quote the summary.

SEQUENCE, all observed 2026-08-28 on gap reach-history-weekly-counter-inflated-beyond-total-executions-ever (target repos/activity-api/src/services/trace-retention.ts, rollupReachHistory):
1. 09:35 operator rewrote the summary (~2600 chars) to state that the additive UPSERT `reached = (reached ?? 0) + $reached,` is CORRECT BY DESIGN - the SELECT reads only rows newer than the stored watermark, so the weekly total must accumulate across runs - and that replacing it with `reached = $reached` would overwrite each week's accumulated total. It named the real mechanisms: non-atomic watermark advance, and no concurrency guard.
2. 09:57 the summary was replaced by a 746-char version derived from the earlier coax dispatch goal, which frames the additive UPSERT as the defect and ends 'Make the weekly fold idempotent so re-scanning a row range cannot double-count'. The explicit do-not-replace guard is GONE from the summary. classification_metadata retained correct_line_do_not_change and rejected_wrong_fix.
3. ~11:29 a compose produced a patch that wrapped the bucket UPSERTs and the watermark UPSERT in a SINGLE TRANSACTION - the atomicity half of the prescribed repair.
4. The semantic gate refused it, refuters 2/2 (conf 0.95, 0.90): 'The patch retains the additive UPSERT logic ... The bucket counters continue to be incremented rather than replaced, so the gap remains unaddressed' and 'the issue isn't about atomicity across a crash, but about the *logic* of the additive update'. The second lens quotes the summary directly: 'The core issue of the GAP is that any run whose bucket writes suc(ceed)...'.

THE REFUSAL'S STATED REASON IS WRONG AND POINTS AT A HARMFUL CHANGE. 'Incremented rather than replaced' is an argument for `reached = $reached`, which discards prior accumulation - the exact change an earlier drafter proposed at 07:47 and which was refused then. The gate is now arguing FOR the change a previous gate refused.

BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The transaction patch is INCOMPLETE, not wrong: it addresses the non-atomic watermark advance but not the missing concurrency guard (three overlapping rollupReachHistory starts were observed inside two minutes on a 30-minute interval). So a refusal may be defensible on COMPLETENESS grounds. What is defective is the stated REASON: the refuters rejected it for retaining additivity, not for missing the lease. A gate that refuses for the wrong reason will accept the wrong patch when one is offered, and its reasons are fed back as compose lessons.

TWO REPAIRS. (1) Stop machine-derived text from overwriting an operator-authored summary, or merge rather than replace; an operator correction is the highest-quality information the gap carries and it was silently discarded 22 minutes after being written. (2) Make the semantic gate read classification_metadata as authoritative where it conflicts with summary prose - fields like correct_line_do_not_change and rejected_wrong_fix exist precisely to constrain the drafter and the refuters, and here they were present, correct, and ignored.

summary: The UI panel store is IN-MEMORY ONLY, so every outstanding human escalation is destroyed by a vessel restart. repos/stateful-ui-vessel/src/store.ts states it directly: 'No persistence yet - substrate restart clears all stores.' MEASURED 2026-08-28: /health on stateful-ui-vessel :8270 reported 194 panels; after a single vessel-ctl restart it reported 0. gap-to-feature.ts posts a uiQuestion_write panel ('Gap needs a human decision') whenever hopeless() excludes a gap, and docs-decision-solicit.ts posts through the same passthrough - 2020 escalation log lines across 81 distinct gaps were recorded in a 71.5h window. Any of those a human had not yet answered are gone, with no record that the question was ever asked. This bounds the value of the uiQuestion READ shape landed as 6dc8107: a reader is necessary but not sufficient while the questions themselves are ephemeral. It also means the escalation path cannot satisfy its own purpose - hopeless() escalates precisely the gaps that need a slow human decision, and slow decisions are exactly the ones that will not survive to be answered. FIX DIRECTION: persist panels and feedback to the container volume (the same durability tier as /workspace/state/*.json which the boredom selector already uses) and rehydrate on boot. Keep the in-memory map as the hot path; write through on upsertPanel and recordFeedback. NOTE the fleet currently runs TWO vessels advertising this vocabulary - stateful-ui-vessel at :8270 holds the live panels, while human-surface-vessel (which its own config says 'replaces' stateful-ui) runs from /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/human-surface-vessel; whichever survives the migration needs the persistence.

A naive `if (since < 2000) return;` throttle - the idiom used by persistMomentum in boredom-vessel - silently loses the LAST write of any burst, which is the one most likely to matter for an escalation. Every path is failure-tolerant: a store write cannot break a resolve, and a missing or corrupt file starts empty exactly as before. Only panels and feedback are persisted; observations, events, asserts and attachments are telemetry and stay in memory. STILL OPEN at the far end of this channel, tracked on uiquestion-has-no-read-shape's closure note: nothing carries a human ANSWER back to the asking gap. uiFeedback records answers and gap-to-feature.ts has no consumer for them, so question -> decision -> gap disposition remains broken at the last link even though the question now survives and can be read.

The gap describes a situation where categories with `>= 8 attempts, 0 lands` are incorrectly hard-excluded, leading to self-sealing behavior because `updateCalibration` is never called. The proposed fix, particularly `REPLACEMENT 3` (lines 857-858: `const scoredGaps = actionableGaps.length ? actionableGaps : hopelessGaps;`), aims to include `hopelessGaps` as a fallback. However, this change only makes `hopelessGaps` selectable when `actionableGaps` is *empty*. The core issue is that `updateCalibration` is tied to gap *closure*. By making `hopelessGaps` a last resort, these gaps will still only be picked when no other 'actionable' gaps exist. If the system *can* pick an actionable gap, it will, and the hopeless gap remains unpicked and thus never closes, never calls `updateCalibration` to potentially escape the hopeless state. This doesn't genuinely fix the self-sealing mechanism on an executing path; it merely defers it, meaning the condition for `lands === 0` will likely persist for these categories even when they *could* theoretically be landed if prioritized differently. TWO HARMS: corpus pollution (a consumer treating the log as an operator-verdict corpus reads dispatch text as human feedback -- and since 421052c it IS a live read surface, because solicitation_outcome_scan matches human answers there by panel_id), and FALSE REACH (a walk satisfying itself by writing to a feedback channel books a reach for doing nothing -- the beta-pump class). summary:
The fc-coverage check in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts (~3610-3628) decides whether a target is tested by trying exactly two candidate paths - a sibling `<name>.test.ts` and `<repo>/src/... -> <repo>/test/...` with `.test.ts` - and requires an EXACT basename match. Any test file named `<name>-<suffix>.test.ts` is invisible to it, so a resolver split across several focused suites is reported as having NO TEST FILE.

MEASURED 2026-08-28 over development-vessel's 246 resolvers: 173 have an exact-name test the detector sees, 70 are genuinely untested, and 3 are MISREPORTED as untested while carrying suffixed suites:
  feature-compose.ts   - 5 test files (adversarial-quorum, architecture-gate, rollback-verify, semantic-gate, truncation)
  gap-to-feature.ts    - 6 test files
  memory-note.ts       - 1 test file

THE MISS IS NOT RANDOM - IT IS SELECTION BIAS. A resolver acquires suffixed test files precisely BECAUSE it is large and heavily tested enough to need more than one suite. So the detector fails exactly on the best-covered files, and those two files are the compose engine and the gap picker/closer - the two most load-bearing resolvers in the self-development loop, and the two most frequently edited by the substrate itself.

WHY IT MATTERS. The warning is load-bearing, not cosmetic: it is the signal that a FAVORABLE verdict means 'the diff was READ, never RUN', and it cites d96e2ae (an unconditional self-call that landed and hung the vessel). Firing it falsely on the vessel's best-tested resolver devalues it - an operator or an activity that learns to discount the warning will also discount it on the 70 files where it is true. The check's own comment says its purpose is to 'stop the weakness being invisible'; a false positive here makes the real weakness harder to see, not easier.

CONFIRMED CONSEQUENCE: this false warning has already been believed and propagated. An operator record dated 2026-08-27 states that fc-coverage warns gap-to-feature.ts has NO TEST, and used that to argue an inverted-boolean bug would go uncaught because 'every gate below READS the diff; only a test RUNS it'. gap-to-feature.ts has six test files. The premise was the detector's error, believed and written down as fact.

FIX DIRECTION: after the two exact candidates fail, glob the sibling test directory for `<basename>-*.test.ts` and treat a non-empty result as covered. Keep the existing candidates first so the common case costs no extra I/O. Do NOT widen this to a substring match - `gap-to-feature` must not be satisfied by an unrelated `gap-to-feature-bridge` suite; anchor the glob on the exact basename followed by a hyphen.

summary: [narrowed from mitosis-cutover-lands-a-stale-base-patch-as-a-silent-revert] An autonomous cutover REVERTED a verified fix three minutes after it landed, and nothing in the landing path noticed. Sequence, all on 2026-08-28: 421052c pushed to origin/dev at 22:58 (repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/solicitation-outcome-scan.ts, +44 lines, verified by consequence against live surfaces). At 23:01:26 the autonomous loop landed 510b6df, titled 'apply solicitation-outcome-scan-reads-a-surface-the-answers-never-reach-compose-report via mitosis cutover' -- for the SAME gap -- with stat '1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 44 deletions(-)'. It deleted exactly the fix it was named for. ROOT CAUSE, from the commit's own trailer: 'Base SHA at staging: 4e87aba4ab11', a base that PREDATES 421052c. The compose staged its patch against a stale tree; vessel_mitosis_cutover then applied that stale CONTENT on top of the real current HEAD. A patch that is a harmless no-op against its own base becomes a 44-line DELETION against a newer one. NOTHING COMPARED THE STAGING BASE TO HEAD AT CUTOVER TIME. This is not specific to an operator commit -- any commit landing between staging and cutover is silently reverted the same way, including the substrate's own autonomous commits, which makes it a self-inflicted regression generator. WHAT WORKED, and should not be changed: the close-oracle detected the fix was gone and REOPENED the gap ('event-driven gap-compose pickup triggered by ... (reopened)'). Detection is fine; the defect is upstream. SECOND, SEPARABLE OBSERVATION: the re-compose that followed produced a patch inserting the identical answeredPanels check TWICE, which the semantic gate caught (adversarial refuters agreed 2/2, conf 0.90/1.00) -- the gate is working, but the composer re-reading an already-fixed file and re-applying its own change is the thrash this stale-base bug creates. FIX DIRECTION: at cutover, compare the recorded staging base SHA against the current HEAD of the target branch; if HEAD has moved, either rebase the staged patch onto HEAD and re-verify, or REFUSE the cutover as stale. A cheap sufficient guard: refuse when the staged diff DELETES lines the staging base did not contain. Restored by fe52076 (revert of 510b6df).

summary:
⚠ PARTLY REFUTED 2026-08-29 — DO NOT CITE THE HEADLINE NUMBER AS A COMPOSER-CAPABILITY MEASUREMENT.

Re-testing docs-align-scan.ts after the per-test-timeout confound was removed showed SEVEN consecutive composes reaching verdict FAVORABLE - the drafter authored patches the gates approved - and every one was refused at cutover with 'staged content drifted in the tree the commit lands in'. Those are LANDING-PATH failures, not authoring failures, and this gap attributed them to the drafter. Root cause filed as the-freshness-gate-checks-the-runtime-tree-but-the-commit-lands-in-the-push-clone.

The confound I flagged in the original text (concurrent sessions) turned out to be the mechanism, not background noise: three other sessions landing commits moved the push clone out from under each staged base. I named the confound and still led with the capability claim.

WHAT SURVIVES: the run-3 false refutation (a correct patch destroyed by a self-retracted refuter) and the run-5 TS1109 on a verbatim array-literal replacement are still real and unexplained by drift - the TS1109 came from the drafter, before any cutover. So a drafting weakness is still evidenced; its SIZE is not, and 1-of-5 is not the measurement of it.

TO ACTUALLY MEASURE: re-run the 2026-08-26 harness on a quiet fleet with no concurrent composing sessions, and separate FAVORABLE-then-refused from gate-rejected-draft in the tally. Those are different failures and this gap conflated them.

--- original text follows ---
Five operator-dispatched, single-file edit goals on 2026-08-28 evening produced ZERO landings. Every failure was caught by a gate - nothing inert or wrong reached the tree - but the composer could not author a correct patch for any of them, including ones whose full replacement text was supplied verbatim.

THE RUNS (target, size, framing, terminal failure):
1. selection-entropy.ts (139L, described edits): LANDED as e15911b. The one success.
2. selection-entropy.ts (139L, dead-code removal): semantic_reject - 'does not address the actual gap as described'. CORRECT refusal; the goal was a cosmetic edit routed through a gap's identity.
3. fossil-rank-report.ts (27L, described helper): TS1109 syntax error, then 'wired stub, not a functional implementation', then a CORRECT patch (verify.ok, typecheck clean, shape-dispatch OK, judge PASSED) destroyed by a 2/2 refuter quorum in which one refuter retracted itself mid-reason.
4. feature-compose.ts (5127L, literal code, unique anchors, dedicated test): no land in ~55min. Consistent with the known large-file timeout class.
5. docs-align-scan.ts (378L, literal code, unique anchors, dedicated test, favourable size): TS1109 'Expression expected' at line 130 - which is the SIMPLEST of the two edits, a seven-line array-literal replacement adding one element.

WHY RUN 5 IS THE LOAD-BEARING DATUM. It removes every operator-side explanation. The target is in the size class that lands, it has an exact-name test file, both anchors were verified unique against the live tree by grep -c, the surrounding scope was confirmed, and the replacement text was given in full rather than described. The drafter still emitted syntactically invalid output on an array literal. There is no more transcribed form of the instruction available, so the remaining variable is the composer, not the specification.

CONTRAST WITH THE 2026-08-26 BASELINE of 90% structural (45 correct / 2 inert / 3 duplicate over 50). Tonight is 1 landing in 5 attempts on the same vessel. n=5 is small and these targets were chosen for difficulty rather than sampled, so this is NOT a clean re-measurement of that baseline - but a 4-for-4 failure run that includes a fully-transcribed edit to a small, tested file is not explained by target difficulty alone and should be re-measured against the 08-26 harness.

CONFOUND TO CHECK FIRST: commit 7ed1bf8 ('raise the per-test timeout - bun's 5s default was a load sensor') landed during this window. A per-test timeout acting as a load sensor makes verify outcomes a function of machine load, and several of these runs were concurrent with three other Claude sessions composing against the same vessel. Re-run the harness on a quiet fleet before treating the regression as real.

WHAT IS NOT AT FAULT: the gates. Six distinct refusal classes fired correctly across these runs - no_unique_anchor, comment-only diff, wired stub, TS2451, TS1109, and 'does not address the gap as described'. The one bad outcome was a FALSE rejection (run 3), filed separately as a-self-retracted-refutation-still-counts-toward-the-adversarial-quorum. Do not respond to this gap by loosening any gate.

A substrateGap that declares no Class-2 measurement predicate (classification_metadata.evidence_resolve or verify_shape) is closed by verifyGapCondition on LANDED-COMMIT PROVENANCE alone (gap-to-feature.ts:1250, 'Class 3 (sync): a substrate-authored commit referencing this gap id already exists'), writing resolution: "already_resolved" at :2572/:2651. Provenance cannot observe a DATA condition, so any gap describing corrupted or wrong stored data closes false.

PROVEN FALSE CLOSE, 2026-08-29. Gap reach-history-weekly-counter-inflated-beyond-total-executions-ever (and its -narrowed child) were closed resolution=already_resolved at 00:32 and 00:40. The defect is still fully present and is trivially measurable right now:
  SELECT week, reached, total FROM reach_history  ->  week 2026-08-17 total = 414944
  SELECT count() FROM execution GROUP ALL         ->  19288
The weekly counter claims 21.5x more executions for a single week than have EVER existed in the store. That is the exact condition the gap was filed on, unchanged.

WHY IT CLOSED: two commits reference the gap id - 52452e0 (a fix that landed over a semantic-gate refusal and was destructive) and de354d1 (the operator revert of it). Class-3 provenance counts a commit that exists; it does not ask whether that commit is still in HEAD or whether it worked. A REVERTED FIX STILL SATISFIES PROVENANCE. Net code change across the pair is zero, the data was never repaired, and the gap reads closed.

THE GUARD EXISTS BUT DOES NOT COVER THIS. The comment at gap-to-feature.ts:1231-1233 states 'MEASUREMENT BEFORE PROVENANCE ... do NOT let the sync landed-commit provenance short-circuit a measurable gap' - but it is conditioned on hasClass2Predicate, so it only protects gaps that already declare a predicate. A gap with no predicate gets provenance-only closure, which the pending-sweep elsewhere in this same file explicitly calls out as 'PROVENANCE, not resolution'. The two branches disagree about whether provenance may close a gap.

DATA GAPS ARE THE WORST CASE because no code change can ever fix them: the inflated rows are history. A code-provenance oracle will report 'absent' the moment anyone touches the named file, regardless of whether the stored data was repaired. Repairing this one requires recomputing or truncating reach_history, which nobody did and which no commit implies.

FIX DIRECTION: (1) when a gap declares no Class-2 predicate, provenance should yield 'unknown' (abstain, stay open) rather than 'absent' - the same asymmetry the sweep already applies to the landed_commit close-oracle, which must earn trust and never accrues it from a commit count. (2) Class-3 provenance must ignore a commit that has been reverted, or that is not an ancestor of the current HEAD; shaIsAncestorOfAnyClone/shaWasRevertedInAnyClone already exist in this file for exactly that purpose and are used by the pending sweep but not by Class 3.

OPERATOR CONSEQUENCE: gaps filed without evidence_resolve/verify_shape are closeable without ever being measured. Seventeen gaps were filed this session without predicates.
