summary:
[narrowed from restart-attribution-is-wired-for-one-vessel-only-so-every-other-restart-is-unattributed] EDIT SITE AND FIX DIRECTION CORRECTED 2026-08-29 — both were prescribed before checking.

1. EDIT SITE. I recorded repos/development-vessel/src/index.ts. That is the one site ALREADY wired; changing it cannot make activity-api report anything. Covering the vessel that actually storms means editing repos/activity-api/src/index.ts (1025 lines, no test file for it).

2. FIX DIRECTION. I wrote 'hoist the same startup block into the shared vessel bootstrap'. THERE IS NO SHARED VESSEL BOOTSTRAP. packages/ contains design-tokens, interaction-conformance, shape-dispatch-check, test-helpers and vessel-discovery-client — none of them a bootstrap. And restart-attribution.ts lives inside development-vessel/src, so activity-api cannot import it across repo boundaries. The real options are (a) promote the module into packages/ and import it from both, which is a cross-repo change, or (b) duplicate the ~15-line telemetry block into activity-api's own entry point. Neither is the two-line edit I implied.

3. THE ORIGINAL SCOPING WAS DELIBERATE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The comment at the existing call site explains why it targets development-vessel specifically: 'every restart of THIS vessel discards in-flight composes for the whole fleet once the drain deadline passes.' It was written to hunt restarts of the compose host. Extending it to activity-api is a genuine coverage extension, but the gap should not read as though someone forgot.

--- original text follows ---
The restart-attribution mechanism (repos/development-vessel/src/restart-attribution.ts) is wired at exactly ONE call site — development-vessel/src/index.ts:282 — and that site hardcodes its own vessel name:

    const raw = await readFile(breadcrumbPath("development-vessel"), "utf8").catch(() => "");
    console.log(describeStart(raw ? parseBreadcrumb(raw) : null, Date.now()));

So exactly one vessel reports whether its own start was attributed. Every other vessel starts silently. repos/activity-api/src contains no reference to breadcrumb, restart-attribution or unattributed at all.

THE MODULE'S OWN STATED PURPOSE IS THE THING THAT IS NOT HAPPENING: 'AN UNATTRIBUTED RESTART IS THE SIGNAL ... no breadcrumb is an UNATTRIBUTED restart. Counting those tells us the unknown.' Nothing counts them, because only one vessel looks, and it looks only at itself.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, 2026-08-29T04:00Z. activity-api restarts ~39 times per hour (39 'Started' events in 60 minutes; 281 lifecycle events in 2 hours), continuously for 21+ hours, in PAIRS: two systemctl restarts racing, the second 'Stopping' arriving 14ms after the first 'Started' (03:45:21.468 Started -> 03:45:21.483 Stopping). systemd reports NRestarts=0, ActiveState=active, SubState=running throughout — systemd is not the restarter, so an external caller is signalling the unit.

THE CALLER CANNOT BE IDENTIFIED, and that is the point. /workspace/restart-requests/activity-api.json holds {"requester":"pull-sync","reason":"converged to origin/dev","at":"2026-08-29T02:11:12Z"} — stale by 1h34m against a 600s freshness window (RESTART_BREADCRUMB_FRESH_MS). Every restart since is unattributed and nothing records that fact. Candidates eliminated by direct evidence: self-recovery (reports recovered_by_restart:0, healthy:14 on every tick) and pull-sync (its only restart in 90 minutes was goal-host-vessel at 02:44).

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHER-LEVERAGE GAP: the restart storm itself has been open ~21 hours and is undiagnosable precisely because attribution has 1-of-N coverage. Extending the existing call site to every vessel converts an unattributable storm into a named requester — or, if no requester ever writes a breadcrumb, into a counted unattributed-restart signal, which is exactly what the module was built to produce.

FIX DIRECTION: read the vessel's own name rather than a literal — the value is already available at that site — and hoist the same startup block into the shared vessel bootstrap so every unit reports its start attribution. Do NOT make it fail-closed; the block is deliberately telemetry-only and wrapped in a swallowing try/catch so an unreadable breadcrumb can never prevent a boot.

NOTE ON A WRONG FIRST READING: I first concluded this module had NO production caller, because `rg 'from ".*restart-attribution"'` missed a dynamic `await import("./restart-attribution.js")`. A static-import grep does not see a dynamic import; the defect is coverage, not dead code.

I am providing missing information for this gap. Here is the fact, with verbatim anchors.

FILE: repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-health-tick.ts

DEFECT, on this exact line (currently 351):
    : (total_pairs === 0 ? false : pairs_above_floor / total_pairs >= confidenceRatioThreshold);

A bare ratio with a zero-guard but NO MINIMUM-SAMPLE FLOOR, over variant pairs seen in a 3600s window. Measured on the same unchanged system 4h apart: 2/17 = 0.12 FAIL, then 2/4 = 0.50 PASS. THE NUMERATOR NEVER MOVED (2 both times); the denominator collapsed. Degenerate case: 1/1 = a confident PASS on ONE observation. Since CLAUDE.md defines S1->S2 lift as three consecutive coverage_progress=true AND overall_passing=true, an IDLE substrate manufactures lift.

FIX, using the idiom already in this same file. Three lines above:
    const confidence_passing = !corpus_complete
      ? null
and the comment at 345-348 says: 'When the registry corpus could not be fully read, confidence + stability are UNMEASURED (null), never a confident pass/fail. A null dimension makes overall_passing null ("couldn't measure this tick"), which resets the lift streak honestly instead of falsely signalling a regression.' A THIN SAMPLE IS OWED THE SAME HONESTY.

Add a minimum-sample floor that yields null, not false. Follow the existing threshold-read pattern at lines 117-118 (const confidenceFloor = pointer.confidence_floor ?? 10;) by adding const confidenceMinPairs = pointer.confidence_min_pairs ?? 8; and make the predicate return null when total_pairs < confidenceMinPairs. Surface total_pairs and that floor in posterior_confidence so the verdict is legible.

DO NOT lower confidenceRatioThreshold, and DO NOT return false on a thin sample: false reads as a measured regression and asserts the opposite of the truth, which is that the tick could not measure. null is correct and this file already treats it that way.

summary: [narrowed from lift-gate-confidence-term-passes-when-activity-drops] THE S1->S2 LIFT GATE PASSES WHEN THE SUBSTRATE DOES LESS WORK. Measured twice on the same unchanged system, 4 hours apart, with no learning intervention between: at 01:11Z posterior_confidence was total_pairs=17, pairs_above_floor=2, median alpha+beta=3 -> confidence_passing FALSE -> overall_passing FALSE. At 05:00Z it was total_pairs=4, pairs_above_floor=2, median alpha+beta=17 -> confidence_passing TRUE -> overall_passing TRUE. THE NUMERATOR NEVER MOVED: 2 pairs above the floor in both readings. The gate flipped because the DENOMINATOR COLLAPSED from 17 to 4. ROOT CAUSE, substrate-health-tick.ts:351: confidence_passing = total_pairs === 0 ? false : pairs_above_floor / total_pairs >= confidenceRatioThreshold (default 0.25, floor 10). It is a bare RATIO with a zero-guard but NO MINIMUM-SAMPLE REQUIREMENT, computed over variant pairs observed in a lookback_window_seconds of 3600. Fewer distinct (state, activity) pairs exercised in the last hour = smaller denominator = higher ratio = gate passes. The degenerate case is total_pairs=1 with that single pair above floor: 1/1 = 1.0, a confident PASS on ONE observation. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A METRIC BUG: this is the architecture's own definition of readiness to advance a stage. development-vessel CLAUDE.md defines lift as three consecutive coverage_progress=true AND health_verdict.overall_passing=true. A quiet period therefore manufactures lift. The system can certify itself ready to advance BY BEING IDLE, which inverts the intent -- confidence is supposed to mean 'the posteriors are well-sampled', and a shrinking sample is the opposite of that. SUBSTRATE_AS_MDP.md 12.6 names this class explicitly: a gameable reward converges on the wrong objective. FIX DIRECTION: require a minimum total_pairs before the ratio is meaningful and return null (UNMEASURED) below it -- the file already has the right idiom, since !corpus_complete yields null and the comment says a null dimension 'makes overall_passing null (couldn't measure this tick), which resets the lift streak honestly instead of falsely signalling a regression'. The same honesty is owed to a thin sample. Consider also reporting the absolute pairs_above_floor count as a gate term, since it is the quantity that actually reflects accumulated evidence. VERIFY BY CONSEQUENCE: with the sample floor in place, a quiet hour yields overall_passing=null rather than true, and the 2-pairs-above-floor reading cannot produce a pass at any denominator. FOUND by re-measuring the same metrics 4h apart while investigating why the gate had flipped without any learning improvement.

FIXED AUTONOMOUSLY BY THE SUBSTRATE — commit abbfa4c, author Substrate Autonomous, on origin/dev. The patch is exactly the specified one-line change:
  -    ? await Bun.file(`${repoPath}/${headRef.trim().slice(5)}`).text()
  +    ? await Bun.file(`${repoPath}/.git/${headRef.trim().slice(5)}`).text()
Semantic gate addresses:true; drift check exempted; committed and pushed with no operator hands on the patch.

⚠ MY ORACLE WAS WRONG, AND THE GAP IS NOT FULLY CLOSED. I wrote 'test/resolvers/git-status.test.ts must pass after the change'. It cannot pass: /workspace/goal-host-vessel/.git/HEAD reads 'ref: refs/heads/master', but .git/refs/heads/ is EMPTY and there is no packed-refs file — the fixture is an UNBORN repository with no commits, so no ref file exists at any path. The resolver's `.git/` omission was a real defect and is now correctly fixed; the test fails for a SECOND, independent reason that I mis-specified as the same one.

REMAINING WORK (separate from the landed fix): the test needs a real fixture. Either point GOAL_HOST_VESSEL_REPO at a repository that has commits, or create a temporary repo in the test and assert against it. Additionally the resolver reads only LOOSE refs — a repository whose refs are packed (.git/packed-refs, which is the normal state after gc) will still fail, so a complete resolver would fall back to packed-refs or shell out to `git rev-parse HEAD`.

--- original text follows ---
resolveGitStatus (repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/git-status.ts, 14 lines) drops the `.git/` path segment when resolving a symbolic HEAD, so it can never return a commit hash for any repository whose HEAD is a ref — which is every repository on a branch.

    const repoPath = process.env.GOAL_HOST_VESSEL_REPO ?? "/workspace/goal-host-vessel";
    const result = await fetch(`file://${repoPath}/.git/HEAD`, ...);       // correct: reads .git/HEAD
    const commitHash = headRef.trim().startsWith("ref: ")
      ? await Bun.file(`${repoPath}/${headRef.trim().slice(5)}`).text()    // WRONG: no .git/
      : headRef.trim();

.git/HEAD contains a line of the form `ref: refs/heads/<branch>`. The ref is relative to the .git DIRECTORY, not to the repository root, so it must be read from `${repoPath}/.git/refs/heads/<branch>`. The first fetch gets this right and the second read does not.

MEASURED: test/resolvers/git-status.test.ts fails with
    ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/workspace/goal-host-vessel/refs/heads/master'
Note the missing `.git` between the repo path and `refs/`. The detached-HEAD branch (a bare sha in HEAD) is unaffected and already correct, which is why this survived: it only fails on a branch.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE: insert `.git/` before the ref path, so the read becomes
    await Bun.file(`${repoPath}/.git/${headRef.trim().slice(5)}`).text()
Change nothing else. The env override, the fetch of .git/HEAD, the detached-HEAD branch, the returned shape and the error branch are all correct as they stand.

ORACLE: test/resolvers/git-status.test.ts currently fails and must pass. It asserts the result has shape "gitStatus" and a string `commitHash`.

summary:
STATUS CORRECTED TO REJECTED 2026-08-29. The retraction was written into this summary but the status was left 'open', so the composer kept picking it and authoring against a premise I had already shown to be false. Caught by the new feature_compose execution traces, which listed live composes against this gap id — the first thing those traces surfaced was my own wasted work.

Read the retraction below before reopening: the ORIGINAL claim does not hold.

⚠ REFUTED 2026-08-29T09:16Z — THE CENTRAL CLAIM OF THIS GAP IS FALSE. Do not act on it.

Staging handles test files correctly. With instrumentation in place (b9117b1) a test-only compose logged:
  [fc-stage] vessel=development-vessel vBase=/workspace/git/compose/fc-mte5un46-u932es/development-vessel
            isolated=true edited=[.../test/resolvers/orphaned-capability-scan.test.ts] created=[]
            changedRel=["test/resolvers/orphaned-capability-scan.test.ts"]
and the staging directory development-vessel-mitosis-fc-2026-08-29T09-15-57-852Z was created containing that test file WITH the patch applied. changedRel is populated; nothing filters test paths; there is no isolation mismatch.

WHY THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Every earlier compose failed BEFORE the staging block — the reachability dead-code rejection (fixed by 31dbc81), an op-budget overflow from a 7-op gap against a budget of 4, and a create_file refusal where the drafter tried to overwrite the 5745-byte file with a 1396-byte rewrite. Staging was never reached on any of them. 'No mitosis dir has ever contained a test file' was therefore a CONSEQUENCE of upstream failures, not evidence of a filter. I read an absence as a mechanism and built a root cause on it, including a confident negative result about path derivation that was answering a question nobody needed asked.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND USEFUL: the earlier 'copy mitosis -> host_repo: 1 file(s)' followed by an EMPTY `git diff --name-only HEAD --` and a failed commit really did happen, on a run whose mitosis_root pointed at the PREVIOUS compose's directory (the 07:35 git-status one, which held only src/resolvers/git-status.ts). A cutover invoked against a stale mitosis_root copies files already at HEAD and then fails with an empty commit error. THAT is the real defect worth pursuing, and it is narrower than what this gap originally claimed.

--- superseded text follows ---
NEGATIVE RESULT — PATH DERIVATION IS NOT THE CAUSE. Do not re-investigate it.

opAbs (feature-compose.ts:2702) computes the write target as ws?.rootFor(vessel) where vessel is the UNPREFIXED name, and vesselRoot (2701) is called from the staging loop (~4891) which strips 'repos/' before calling it. Both therefore key rootFor on the same string, and changedRel's startsWith(vBase + '/') should match an edited path. Statically this path is consistent, so the mismatch is NOT in how the absolute path is derived.

What remains: worktree LIFECYCLE. The likely candidate is ws.rootFor resolving to a different root — or the isolated worktree being reclaimed — between the apply step and the staging loop, so staging reads a tree that never received the edit. That is a runtime-ordering question and cannot be settled by reading; instrument both sites to log the absolute path and the resolved root, run one test-file compose, and compare.

--- previous text follows ---
ROOT CAUSE REFINED — IT IS AN ISOLATION MISMATCH, NOT A src/-ONLY FILTER.

Do NOT patch the changedRel filter at feature-compose.ts:4892. It has no src/ restriction, and vesselDirOf (line 344) matches ^repos/<vessel>/ with no path-segment restriction either, so neither excludes test files.

What the evidence shows instead: the edits are applied to one tree and staged from another.
  1. The patch WAS applied and staged in the push clone — observed directly as
     'M test/resolvers/orphaned-capability-scan.test.ts' with the correct three-edit diff.
  2. The isolated compose worktrees do NOT contain it: /workspace/git/compose/fc-mte2581n-6a9dtk and
     fc-mtdzzn88-he10wa both hold the test file with the fix absent.
  3. Mitosis staging copies from vBase = vesselRoot(v) = ws?.rootFor(v) — the ISOLATED WORKTREE —
     so it captured the UNPATCHED file.
  4. The cutover then runs `git reset --hard origin/dev` BEFORE copying, which DESTROYS the real
     staged edits in the clone, and copies the unpatched staged file over the top.
  5. copyTree uses copyFile, which throws ENOENT on a missing source; no error was raised, so a file
     genuinely was copied — it was simply the wrong version. That is why the log reads
     'copy mitosis -> host_repo: 1 file(s)' and the very next `git diff --name-only HEAD --` is EMPTY.

CONTRAST THAT EXPLAINS WHY SOURCE FIXES LAND: for src/resolvers/git-status.ts the mitosis dir development-vessel-mitosis-fc-2026-08-29T07-35-14-856Z DID contain the patched file, and the identical cutover sequence committed it as abbfa4c. So the sequence is sound; the staging SOURCE is what differs.

⚠ DIAGNOSE BEFORE PATCHING. I could not establish from static reading WHY the edit reached the clone rather than the worktree for this compose. Instrument the apply step to log the absolute path it writes and compare it against ws.rootFor(vessel) at staging time; fix the mismatch that shows up. Guessing at a fix in the landing path is precisely how the escalation lane caused harm earlier today.

--- original text follows ---
A test-only compose passes every gate, applies its edits, and then commits NOTHING: the cutover resets to HEAD, copies from a mitosis staging directory that does not contain the test file, finds no diff, and fails at `git commit`.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 on gap orphaned-capability-scan-first-test-asserts-on-a-captured-read. The compose report shows every gate green — semantic_gate.addresses true ("corrects the test to look for the substrateGap_write instead of the earlier READ substrateGap"), verify ok with 0 errors, rolled_back false, 3 edit ops applied ok — and the cutover operation log ends:
    ok    git reset --hard origin/dev        HEAD is now at 31dbc81
    ok    git clean -fd                      untracked dropped
    ok    copy mitosis -> host_repo          1 file(s)
    ok    git diff --name-only HEAD --       (EMPTY)
    ok    git add -- test/resolvers/orphaned-capability-scan.test.ts
    FAIL  git commit                         detail: "git commit failed: " (empty error)
    ok    git reset -q HEAD -- ...           unstaged after commit_failed
The diff is empty immediately after the copy, so the file copied in already matched HEAD — the staged copy did not carry the patch. Overall verdict UNFAVORABLE with no refusal_reason, because nothing refused; the commit simply had nothing to commit.

NO MITOSIS DIRECTORY WAS CREATED FOR THIS COMPOSE. The newest is development-vessel-mitosis-fc-2026-08-29T07-35-14-856Z, from the PREVIOUS (git-status) compose, and it contains exactly one file: src/resolvers/git-status.ts. The cutover therefore copied a stale directory whose contents already matched HEAD.

AND NO MITOSIS DIRECTORY HAS EVER CONTAINED A TEST FILE. Every one of the six most recent staging dirs holds exactly one .ts file and zero files under test/. That matches the population statistic: 3 of 783 substrate-authored commits over 60 days touched only test files (0.4%).

WHERE TO LOOK: feature-compose.ts ~4892 builds
    const changedRel = [...created, ...edited].filter((p) => p.startsWith(`${vBase}/`))
and skips staging entirely when changedRel is empty (`if (changedRel.length === 0) continue;`). There is no src/-only filter in that expression, so the exclusion is upstream: either the test file's applied path does not sit under vBase as computed, or it never enters `edited`. Confirm which before patching — the filter is not where it looks like it is.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: 31dbc81 removed the reachability hard-fail that used to reject test-only patches, and this gap is the very next blocker behind it. development-vessel has ~68 failing tests; a red suite forces every cutover to diff newly-failing against a baseline, machinery that has already failed twice. The substrate cannot green its own suite while test edits never reach staging.

[narrowed from escalation-disposition-parser-rejects-its-own-verb-names] parseDisposition rejects the CANONICAL FORM OF ITS OWN VERB NAMES. Measured 2026-08-29: an operator answered a needs-human escalation beginning 'PROVIDE_INFORMATION.' and the executor returned outcome='unparsed' and correctly made no change. The regex in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/escalation-disposition-apply.ts requires whitespace between the words -- /\bprovide[sd]?\s+(missing\s+)?info(rmation)?\b/ -- so the underscored literal 'provide_information' does not match. The same applies to 'grant_access'. THE FOUR VERB NAMES THE SYSTEM ITSELF USES ARE drop / redefine / provide_information / grant_access, and those underscored identifiers are the most natural thing for a human to type when told to pick one: they appear as the verb keys in the disposition table and in every gap record this executor writes. So the parser fails on exactly the input its own vocabulary invites. CONSEQUENCE: the answer is silently a no-op. The gap stays sealed, the escalation stays outstanding, and the human is not told their answer was unusable -- the outcome is recorded in the report but nothing surfaces back to the panel. This is a small regex fix with an outsized effect, because the escalation channel is the ONLY designed escape from the hopeless() category seal (see openspec/changes/2026-08-28-escalation-disposition-executor/proposal.md), so a verb that cannot be parsed is a seal that cannot be opened. FIX: accept the underscored and hyphenated forms of all four verbs, i.e. allow [\s_-]+ wherever the current patterns require \s+, and add the bare literals provide_information / grant_access. KEEP the existing ordering (most-specific first) and KEEP returning null on no match -- the no-op on an unrecognised answer is correct and deliberate; the defect is only which strings are recognised. ADDITIONALLY, consider reporting 'unparsed' back to the panel so the human learns their answer did not take. VERIFY BY CONSEQUENCE: an answer whose first token is PROVIDE_INFORMATION yields verb=provide_information and outcome=applied.

createAuthenticatedClient() in activity-api and concept-db (repos/activity-api/src/db/surreal.ts, repos/concept-db/src/db/surreal.ts) called connect() before use()/authenticate() with no try/catch. Any auth-handshake failure (identity-vessel unreachable, JWT issues -- both observed live) leaked the already-open SurrealDB socket forever, since the caller's try/finally around queryWithAuth never started. Confirmed as the root cause of an unbounded SurrealDB connection growth (28->64+) driving a container CPU/thermal emergency (Tctl 100C) on 2026-08-29. Patched in both vessels (wrap connect/use/authenticate in try/catch, close() on failure, rethrow) and verified live -- connection count plateaus under load instead of climbing. NOT YET CHECKED: whether other vessels built from the same TypeScript vessel template (identity-vessel showed the same high-connection-count symptom) share this exact pattern in their own createAuthenticatedClient.

concept-db's resolve-island upkeep activity runs: SELECT * FROM concept WHERE relevance > 0.3 AND (SELECT count() FROM concept_edge WHERE from_concept = concept.id OR to_concept = concept.id GROUP ALL)[0].count == 0 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10. The relevance filter matches 60,800 of 63,611 concept rows (nearly the whole table), and SurrealDB evaluates the correlated concept_edge subquery for every matching row BEFORE the ORDER BY/LIMIT 10 is applied -- tens of thousands of subquery evaluations per cycle against a 22,312-row concept_edge table. This times out ('The operation timed out') and re-fires every UPKEEP_INTERVAL_MS (default 300000ms/5min) via the upkeep scheduler, contributing sustained SurrealDB CPU/IO load. Observed as part of a 2026-08-29 thermal emergency (Tctl 100C). Emergency mitigation: stopped concept-db's upkeep scheduler live via POST /upkeep/scheduler/stop (confirmed running:false) -- this is NOT a code fix and the scheduler is currently OFF, meaning split-long-concept, adjust-priority-relevance, prune-irrelevant-neighbors, decay-stale-relevance, and prune-per-execution-concepts are also not running. Needs: rewrite resolve-island's query to bound the candidate set (e.g. pre-filter to a small recent/unchecked window, or track a checked-at watermark) before the correlated subquery, then re-enable the scheduler.

  - verifyPatchAddressesGap — the LLM judge plus adversarial refuters, i.e. 'does this diff actually address the gap'

summary:
CLOSED 2026-08-29 by development-vessel 8af0f94. The gap's own stated blocker turned out to be wrong, and the real one was a dropped HTTP request.

THE RECORDED BLOCKER WAS: 'resolver-emitted SUMMARY traces cannot be extracted (completed=0; the census is executor-only, ExecutionRecordSchema has no task field)'. That is not what was stopping this. The feedback path was already built and already correct:
  vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts:465-480 POSTs /v2/activities/execution-traces/reach with { execution_id, reached: true, completion_shapes: ["cutoverApplied"] } — the same grader goal-host uses — AFTER the commit exists and the push has been attempted. Its comment is explicit that reached:true is honest 'here and only here', and that a compose which merely reached FAVORABLE must stay ungraded lest the ribosome be fed the hollow executions law 4 warns about. The schema limitation is precisely why the verdict goes to that dedicated endpoint instead of riding along on the POST.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT: emitLandingTrace was a SYNCHRONOUS function doing `void fetch(...)`. The resolver returned its cutoverApplied body immediately and the request was abandoned when the handler finished, so the landing trace never reached the store — and the reach grader chained off that same promise, so the verdict went nowhere either. MEASURED: a real landing (commit b857661, gap route-edit-d71ecda6) went through the git_aware path while the store held ZERO vessel_mitosis_cutover executions across the most recent 400.

I NEARLY FIXED THE WRONG THING: 7 cutoverApplied return sites exist and only 2 call the emitter, which looks like missing coverage. Enumerating all seven first showed the other 5 are already-applied no-ops and log listings — not landings. Both real landing paths already called it. Coverage was correct; the request was dropped in flight. (The file's own header warns it got this exact instrumentation question wrong twice.)

FIX: emitLandingTrace is now async and awaited at both landing sites, so the emission and its chained reach-grade complete before the resolver returns. Every failure path still swallows, so emission can never affect a completed landing; awaiting only bounds the return by the 5s timeout already declared. The endpoint read also moved to env() so an empty METABOB_ENDPOINT cannot silently POST to a relative path.

THE WALK JOIN IS NOW POSSIBLE WITH NO SCHEMA CHANGE, which was the gap's substance: the landing trace carries metadata.gap_id = 'route-edit-<goalhash>' and the originating walk's goal_hash is that same hash (verified: gap_id route-edit-e0cfd390 against walk goal_hash e0cfd390). A consumer can join on it today. It also carries linked_to_gap, which the cutover already computes as FALSE for route-edit-* ids — the substrate self-reporting the very linkage weakness this gap named.

VERIFIED: tsc --noEmit clean; cutover-adjacent suites 41 pass / 0 fail. REMAINING WATCH ITEM, stated plainly rather than hidden in a closure: confirm a vessel_mitosis_cutover row with reached:true appears in the store after the NEXT landing. If it does not, the defect is downstream of the await and this should be reopened with that evidence.

EXPERIMENT 1 — single file, multiple ops (trace exec_1788052485529_xepsp7bpe3a, gap route-edit-e0cfd390): op_count 2, ops_applied 2, and the report's applied[] lists BOTH edits with ok:true, repaired:false — one at line 43, one spanning lines 2-3. Nothing dropped.

EXPERIMENT 2 — TWO files, run deliberately against my own revised oracle, which said the single-file case was already demonstrated and must not be re-used as evidence. Dispatched a goal naming docs-align-tick.ts AND perf-canary-resolve.ts. The planner emitted ops for BOTH:
  [fc-plan] ops: [ edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/docs-align-tick.ts,
                   edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/perf-canary-resolve.ts ]
and the gate pipeline then evaluated BOTH, one second apart:
  02:57:16 [fc-coverage] TARGET HAS NO TEST FILE: …/docs-align-tick.ts
  02:57:17 [fc-coverage] TARGET HAS NO TEST FILE: …/perf-canary-resolve.ts
The second file is neither dropped at planning nor lost before the gates.

'SILENTLY' IS REFUTED BY AN EXISTING GATE — feature-compose.ts:4593, the target-touched floor:
  'target-touched floor: WITHHELD FAVORABLE — intended target(s) <targets> absent from applied set [<applied>]'
It withholds the FAVORABLE verdict AND prints both lists, so a target that fails to be touched cannot pass unnoticed. Observed firing live during these runs on an unrelated compose (light-dispatch-vessel/src/index.ts). A dropped target is now a withheld verdict with a named discrepancy — the opposite of silent.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS TRACKED ELSEWHERE: a compose can still end UNFAVORABLE and roll back. That is the verify path, and its real defect this session was a 30s shell watchdog killing the typecheck (local-tools e4d604c + development-vessel c37aab5), not op loss. Do not mine those rollbacks as evidence for this gap.

IF IT RECURS: the discriminating evidence is applied[] vs op_count in the compose report, plus the presence or absence of a target-touched-floor line. A report showing ops_applied < op_count with NO withheld-verdict line would be a genuine instance; nothing observed here matched that.

Observed on substrate-live 2026-08-29 23:26:45; the unit had been sitting in `failed` ever since. So a momentary store hiccup was rendered indistinguishable from 'credit stopped flowing' — the loudest possible false alarm from the fleet's own health detector, and precisely what the file's own comments warn against ('reporting it as one would make the probe cry wolf').

THE FIX needed no new vocabulary: `null` is already this file's word for 'unreadable', both call sites map it to INCONCLUSIVE + exit 2, and the unit ALREADY declares SuccessExitStatus=0 2. Catching routes an unreachable store to the verdict the probe already reserves for 'I could not measure', matching publish()'s tolerance directly below.

  PROBE_CONTAINER=nonexistent-container METABOB_API_KEY=x \
    bun scripts/substrate/learning-liveness-probe.ts; echo $?   # expect 2, never 1

A function's header comment states the OPPOSITE of what the code 20 lines below it does, on a question that governs learning credit. MEASURED 2026-08-29 at 81eab2d in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/concept-usage-record.ts. The header comment (~lines 44-46) reads: 'A placeholder concept_id means the upstream extract failed — skip the write entirely; a placeholder/empty trace_id gets a unique synthesized fallback so each usage event still keys distinctly.' The code at ~lines 67-79 does the exact opposite for trace_id: it returns early with `skipped: true, recorded: false, reason: 'unbound/placeholder trace_id — skipped usage write (no synthetic credit)'`, and its own inline comment explains the reversal: 'No real trace attribution — do NOT synthesize a usage row. Synthetic autonomous_backfill_* rows inflated concept relevance (usage credit must come only from a real execution trace that loaded the concept).' So the synthesized-fallback policy was deliberately REMOVED and the header was never updated. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO: (1) it is a live misinformation hazard — anything reading this file to decide behaviour (a drafter building a patch, an operator, a future reader) sees an authoritative-sounding statement that synthetic trace_ids are minted, which is false and is the precise behaviour that was inflating concept relevance; law 8 says the fix for a wrong output is making the load-bearing fact available at the moment of use, and here the file volunteers the WRONG fact first; (2) the tests believed the header, not the code — test/resolvers/concept-usage-record.test.ts asserted `String(sentBody.trace_id).toContain('autonomous_backfill_')` and failed, and a reader trusting the comment would 'fix' the resolver back toward synthesizing, re-introducing credit inflation. The test was inverted in 81eab2d to assert the real policy (no write, nothing reaches concept-db); the stale comment remains and is the last thing still asserting the removed behaviour. REPAIR: rewrite the header comment so it describes the current policy for BOTH branches — placeholder/empty concept_id skips (benign no-op, returned as the declared success shape because structuredError made goal-host's proxy throw and failed whole composed activities), and placeholder/empty trace_id ALSO skips with no synthesized fallback, because usage credit must come only from a real execution trace. Comment-only change, no behaviour change. ORACLE: no occurrence of 'synthesized fallback' or 'gets a unique' survives in the file describing trace_id handling, and `bun test test/resolvers/concept-usage-record.test.ts` stays 8 pass/0 fail. DETECTOR WORTH MINTING (the more valuable half): this class — a comment describing behaviour the adjacent code contradicts — has now been observed at least twice, here and in gap-to-feature.ts's hopeless() where the code contradicts its own comment about attempts. Both were found by a human reading the file, not by any gate. A checker that flags policy verbs in comments ('synthesizes', 'skips', 'returns') whose adjacent block does the opposite is hard in general, but a cheap high-value approximation is: when a code path returns a literal reason string, assert that string's key terms are not negated by the enclosing comment block. CONTEXT: deliberately NOT hand-patched — src/ is gated, and this session declined to hand-patch src/config.ts for the same reason.

summary: RESOLVED in fbbfd9b. ROOT CAUSE (solved, not merely narrowed): fetchWithRetry DELIBERATELY suppresses trace-store reads while a maintenance lease is active - http-retry.ts defines TRACE_STORE_READ_PATTERNS matching /v2/activities/execution-traces, isMaintenanceLeaseActive() reads the lease file, and the answer is memoised for 5s in a module-level leaseCheckCache. maintenance-lease.test.ts left a LIVE lease file behind, so every later suite reading execution traces silently received NOTHING. coverage_tick reported trace_count 0, reachable_learned 0 and coverage_progress false - indistinguishable from a broken detector when the read had been skipped exactly as designed. THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT was instrumenting the victim's own fetch MOCK to log the URLs it received: under pollution the execution-traces mock was NEVER CALLED (templates were). 'the mock returned nothing' and 'the mock was never asked' are indistinguishable from the assertion, and only the second was true. FIX: afterAll (not afterEach) releasing the lease plus __resetMaintenanceLeaseCacheForTests(). The file's comment correctly ruled out afterEach - the acquire/status/conflict/renew/release/re-acquire lifecycle is the point - but that argument covers BETWEEN CASES, never the FILE. Clearing the memo matters independently: the cache answers 'active' for up to 5s after the file is gone, so releasing the file alone leaves a shorter, flakier version of the same bug. VERIFIED: maintenance-lease + coverage-tick 2 fail -> 21 pass / 0 fail; full suite 64 -> 57 fail (1802 pass), and BOTH trace-store-reading victims cleared (coverage-tick and generative-frontier-gap-tick). The victim needed NO changes - it was never broken. GENERALISABLE LESSON: a test that leaves behind state which PRODUCTION CODE deliberately reads (leases, feature flags, circuit breakers, maintenance modes) is far more dangerous than a leaked mock, because the suppression is CORRECT behaviour - nothing looks broken, the downstream suite just receives a legitimate empty answer. Search for designed global-state READERS, not only for globalThis.* assignments. METHOD: found by baseline-gated ddmin over 224 files (224->1) after an earlier plain bisection wrongly blamed a 14-file combination; halving is unsound when the trigger may be a set, and that run was at a commit whose victim set had since moved.

summary: git_status IGNORES its cwd argument and hardcodes ANOTHER VESSEL's repository. repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/git-status.ts:4 reads `const repoPath = process.env.GOAL_HOST_VESSEL_REPO ?? "/workspace/goal-host-vessel";` and then opens `${repoPath}/.git/HEAD` and `${repoPath}/.git/<ref>`. The pointer accepts `cwd` and the resolver never uses it, so a caller asking for the git status OF A GIVEN DIRECTORY silently receives the goal-host vessel's status instead - or an error when that path does not exist. This is 'a field that accepts your data is not a field that means it'. MEASURED at 5b41234 by printing the CLI's own stderr: `bun run cli call-resolver git_status --data '{"cwd":"<repo>"}'` exits 1 with: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/workspace/goal-host-vessel/.git/refs/heads/master'. Two independent problems in that one line: the path points at a vessel that is not the caller and does not exist at that location in this container, and the ref resolves to 'master' while these repositories use 'dev'. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE RED TEST: (1) a resolver that silently answers about a DIFFERENT repository than the one asked about is a correctness hazard for anything that branches on git state - it will confidently report clean/dirty or a branch name belonging to someone else; (2) test/cli.test.ts is one of only three files in a verified 3-file interaction that makes gap-to-feature-admission fail, and FAILING FILES HAVE ALREADY BEEN PROVEN TO ACT AS POLLUTERS in this suite (fixing the analogous layout defect in detectors-are-scheduled.test.ts dissolved a different 3-file interaction, 5 failures -> 0). So repairing this is likely to clear victim failures elsewhere, not just its own. REPAIR: honour the pointer - use `pointer.cwd` (falling back to process.cwd()) as repoPath, and resolve the CURRENT HEAD ref rather than assuming master. If the resolver is genuinely meant to report only the goal-host vessel, then it is misnamed and must not accept a cwd it discards - rename it and drop the field, so the contract stops lying. Note the `??` on the env var has the empty-string hazard filed separately as empty-string-env-vars-defeat-nullish-coalescing-endpoint-defaults. ORACLE: `call-resolver git_status --data '{"cwd":"<any git repo>"}'` exits 0 and reports THAT repo's branch; and it must report a DIFFERENT branch for two different repos passed in - prove it reads the argument rather than merely stopping to error.

summary:
CLOSED 2026-08-29 by ee525e7, and the ORACLE THIS GAP SET WAS MET: the test passes with its original TWO-action script unchanged. The extra consumption was removed rather than papered over by padding the script.

ROOT CAUSE: discoverFallbackModels (patch-with-tools.ts:302, called from resolvePatchWithTools:714 BEFORE the ReAct loop) POSTs { type: "llmModelPolicy" } to the SAME producer URL a completion uses. The test harness matched on the URL alone, so that pre-loop model discovery consumed llmActions[0]. Turn 1 then received the script's SECOND entry ('done'), and every later turn got it too because the index is clamped once the script is exhausted - producing 'LLM declared done 2x without making any edit' while the scripted first action was a call_tool the loop never saw.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, since reading the code had already sent me down two wrong paths: I instrumented the stub to record every /llm request with its body keys and a stack. Call #1 carried ONLY { type } - no prompt, no model, no task_type - and its stack named discoverFallbackModels. Calls #2 and #3 were the real turns. That single capture settled it.

THE HARNESS WAS MISALIGNED FOR EVERY CASE IN THE FILE, not just this one; the siblings survived only because their second scripted entry happens to be a usable action. Discriminating on body.type realigns all of them.

NOT A RESOLVER DEFECT: the pre-loop model discovery is legitimate and its own short timeout is deliberate. Nothing in the shipping path was changed.

VERIFIED: patch-with-tools.test.ts 5/5, with the log now showing 'turn 1: action=call_tool tool=fs_write' followed by the write and a verified-green terminal. Full suite at ee525e7 is 1875 pass / 0 fail / 0 timeouts, reproduced twice consecutively.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 21:39:40 live. The compose pipeline discards a CORRECT, VERIFIED-UNIQUE anchor because it is far from a heuristically located region, and substitutes an arbitrary anchor in its place. Verbatim log line: '[fc-anchor-region] planned anchor for repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts is unique but 3103 lines from the located region (line 30) - re-deriving from the offered anchors instead'. Eight seconds later: '[fc-anchor-choice] re-derivation picked anchor [0] from the verified list for repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts'. THE DRAFTER WAS RIGHT AND THE PIPELINE OVERRODE IT. The planned op was {kind:edit, path:repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, old:'    if (isNonAttemptComposeResult(cb)) {'} - the exact line, correct leading indentation, unique in the file, and the correct edit site for the requested change. The log itself concedes the anchor 'is unique' in the same sentence in which it rejects it. WHY THIS IS A MECHANISM DEFECT, NOT A TUNING ISSUE: region proximity is useful for DISAMBIGUATING among several candidate matches. It is not evidence about a UNIQUE match. A unique anchor has exactly one interpretation, so distance from a guessed region cannot make it wrong - it can only make the REGION wrong. As built, the rule makes an entire legitimate class of change inexpressible: any edit in one file whose declaration site and use site are far apart. That is an extremely common shape (declare a constant or a Map at the top of the module, use it 3000 lines down) and it is precisely the shape of the change that was being attempted. REPRO: dispatch an edit goal whose text mentions BOTH a declaration near the top of a large file AND the distant use site. The grounding centres the region on the declaration (here line 30, where GAP_COMPOSE_COOLDOWN_MS and gapComposeLastAttemptAt are declared), and then the region check vetoes the correct anchor at the use site (line 3133). The mention of the declaration site in the goal text is what steers the region; that is how to reproduce it deterministically. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: this is the second of two consecutive failures to land a one-line change (attempt 1 failed by anchor confabulation; attempt 3 produced the right anchor and had it vetoed here), and it is the failure that forced an operator hand-edit under the two-strike rule. Closing THIS gap is what would have let the system land that fix itself. FIX DIRECTION: a verified-unique planned anchor must be ACCEPTED. Region proximity should rank ambiguous candidates and must never veto a unique one. If a distance signal is still wanted for a unique anchor, it should be logged as an observation, not acted on. summary: MEASURED 2026-08-29 live, end to end. The escalation escape valve's provide_information verb grants the gap a selection exemption and then throws the information away. escalation-disposition-apply.ts writes human_disposition, human_disposition_answer, human_disposition_record_id, human_disposition_at, human_exemption_attempts_remaining and resets failed_attempts — and NEVER PARSES THE ANSWER. So the gap becomes selectable but stays exactly as ungrounded as it was, which means it can be picked forever and never composed. PROOF, one gap, both halves observed: gap concept-usage-record-header-comment-contradicts-its-own-code-on-synthetic-credit was answered on 2026-08-29T19:01:43Z with an answer whose literal text reads 'EDIT_SITE (the gap has none, which is why it cannot be grounded or composed): repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/concept-usage-record.ts'. Its complete classification_metadata key set three hours later is exactly: approach_decisions, failed_attempts, human_disposition, human_disposition_answer, human_disposition_at, human_disposition_record_id, human_exemption_attempts_remaining, human_exemption_granted_at. There is NO edit_site, NO file_path, NO change_site, NO suspected_real_location. Every approach_decision the picker recorded for it carries edit_site:'' and every pick logs target:'(no-target)'. It has been selected more than twenty times across three hours at the TOP score (1.5938, tied_at_top 1), has spent ZERO of its three exemption attempts, and has never produced a single fc-plan, fc-scope or fc-anchors line. WHY THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING DEFECT: the category seal's only designed escape is a human decision, and the resolver's own header cites the escalation body that asks the human to 'redefine the goal, provide missing information, grant access, or drop it'. Three of those four verbs are answerable with words alone. provide_information is not: information that is not written into the fields the compose path READS has not been provided to the system, only to the log. Law 8 names this exactly — the fix for a wrong or absent output is making the load-bearing fact available AS AN IMPULSE AT THE MOMENT OF USE — and here the fact was supplied by a human, stored verbatim, and left where no consumer looks. The valve therefore reports success at every step and cannot close a gap: disposition applied=1, exemption granted, gap re-opened, picked at top score, refused for grounding forever. NOTE THIS IS NOT THE CAPACITY DEFECT. Capacity (BUSY) and the cooldown burn (fixed in be891f3) both delayed this gap; neither explains it. With those cleared, other gaps re-pick every 12-16s while this one still cannot compose, because it has nothing to compose against. FIX DIRECTION: on provide_information, extract the actionable fields from the answer and write them into classification_metadata where localizeGap and the grounding gate read them — at minimum edit_site, since a gap with target '(no-target)' cannot be grounded. A labelled form (a line matching /^EDIT_SITE:\s*(\S+)/mi) is enough and is what an operator already writes unprompted; anything unparsed must stay in human_disposition_answer as it does today. VERIFY AT THE CONSUMING LAYER: the test is not that a field was written, it is that the next pick of that gap logs a real target instead of '(no-target)' and reaches fc-scope. DO NOT let an unparsed answer silently grant the exemption while leaving the gap ungrounded — that is today's behaviour and it is indistinguishable, from every report the system emits, from success.

summary: Edit repos/concept-db/scripts/apply-schema.ts: the schema applier is structurally incapable of reporting failure, so schema drift is undetectable. Line 86 does content.split(';'), which shreds any DEFINE FUNCTION body containing semicolons. Lines 99-106 catch every statement error and only console.error unless the message contains 'already exists', then continue. Line 110 prints the per-file success tick and line 136 prints 'Schema applied successfully' UNCONDITIONALLY, even when every statement failed. The verification block at lines 121-134 enumerates only table NAMES beginning with 'concept'; it never checks indexes, analyzers or functions, so nothing it could plausibly get wrong is within scope of its own verification. Verified on the live DB 2026-08-29: fn::island_concepts, defined in sql/upkeep/002-upkeep-views.surql:21, is absent from INFO FOR DB, so the resolve-island upkeep activity is structurally dead, and the apply log still printed success. Make the applier split on real statement boundaries rather than raw semicolons, exit non-zero on any non-'already exists' error, and verify functions, indexes and analyzers rather than table names alone.

Edit repos/concept-db/src/upkeep/activities.ts: the concept store can never delete anything, so it grows without bound (63,952 concepts on 2026-08-29). Exactly one upkeep activity deletes a concept, prune-per-execution-concepts at line 305, and its candidate query at line 309 requires times_loaded = 0. But times_loaded is incremented on retrieval - see src/resolvers/concept.ts:254, and the vessel's own health template at src/upkeep/pipeline-health-template.json:35 asserts this as intended behaviour by reading a concept before and after issuing a search request and requiring that times_loaded incremented. The same field is also the Bayesian relevance denominator, relevance = (times_succeeded + 1) / (times_loaded + 2) per src/resolvers/usage.ts:110. One field is therefore serving two jobs that are in direct conflict: it must increment on every retrieval for relevance to work, which makes times_loaded = 0 unreachable for any concept the system has ever surfaced. Measured decomposition of the candidate query: 506 rows match source_type impulse_activity_pattern, 260 also match the content pattern, 29 also have times_loaded = 0, and the full conjunction returns 0 - empty by construction, not by accident. Separate the prune predicate from the relevance counter: prune on usefulness such as loads that only ever produced neutral outcomes, low relevance, and age, rather than on never-having-been-touched.

Edit repos/concept-db/src/index.ts: the /health endpoint reports upkeep.enabled from an environment variable alone, so it no longer reflects whether the scheduler is actually running. Two substrate-authored mitosis-cutover commits (120d9d1 and acb7a5a, both applying the same one-line change, neither recording a rationale) replaced the expression process.env.DENSE_BACKFILL_ENABLED === 'true' ? status.enabled : false with process.env.DENSE_BACKFILL_ENABLED === 'true', dropping the status.enabled term. Health now reports enabled true whenever the env var is set, even if the upkeep scheduler is stopped or dead. This is the dominant defect class in this substrate, a success signal that stops tracking the thing it reports, and it is especially costly here because upkeep is independently known to be degraded: /upkeep/status shows totalTrials 0 for all six activities, so health is now structurally unable to surface that. summary: development-vessel:mitosis-tick fires roughly 390 times an hour (195 measured in 30 minutes) and each evaluation runs a full bun test via runCheck in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-evaluate.ts, plus a second suite for the baseline. Measured on substrate-live 2026-08-30: about 29 suites running concurrently on 14 CPUs, with the 1-minute load average between 41 and 57 for over half an hour and no downward trend. Two spawners contribute: 18 of the concurrent processes carried pull-sync's `timeout 240 bun test` gate signature and 13 were bare mitosis-evaluate spawns. The saturation is what made vessel /health take 9.5 seconds, made substrateGap_write time out so this gap could not be filed at the time, and made walks fail on HTTP 500 fetch failed The operation was aborted rather than on reasoning. It also corrupts measurement: the identical search probe read 326ms and 8192ms ten minutes apart, and several apparent query failures turned out to be pure load artifacts. Two mitigations have landed (0fd7487 kills the process group on timeout so a timed-out check no longer orphans its tree, and 3e687d2 defers starting a suite when load exceeds 3x the CPU count, reporting it through the existing inconclusive timed_out channel). Neither addresses the underlying cadence. The remaining question is a design decision: whether ~390 evaluations per hour, each running the full suite up to twice, is the intended rate, or whether the tick should be paced by a rhythm impulse that reads current conditions.

Edit repos/concept-db/src/index.ts: the /health endpoint reports upkeep.enabled from an environment variable alone, so it no longer reflects whether the scheduler is actually running. Two substrate-authored mitosis-cutover commits, 120d9d1 and acb7a5a, both applying the same one-line change and neither recording a rationale, replaced the expression process.env.DENSE_BACKFILL_ENABLED === 'true' ? status.enabled : false with process.env.DENSE_BACKFILL_ENABLED === 'true', dropping the status.enabled term. Health now reports enabled true whenever the env var is set, even if the upkeep scheduler is stopped or dead. This is the dominant defect class in this substrate, a success signal that stops tracking the thing it reports, and it is especially costly here because upkeep is independently known to be degraded: /upkeep/status shows totalTrials 0 for all six activities, so health is now structurally unable to surface that. Restore the conjunction so the field reports actual scheduler state gated by the env var.

provide_feedback refuses to write a ground-truth label when a dispatch has no selectedTemplateId, returning: cannot write a label - missing selectedTemplateId (no template/satisfier was recorded). Observed 2026-08-29 on dispatch 44acaa4a-6bfd-4a91-a264-3a6f66a8d9f0, a goal that failed as goal-seek:no-trace before any template was selected. The consequence is that the oracle corpus is structurally blind to the substrate's EARLIEST and most informative failures. A goal that dies before selection is precisely the case where an operator verdict carries the most information - it says the walk never got started and why - yet that verdict cannot be recorded, while a goal that selects a template and then produces a hollow result CAN be graded. The corpus therefore over-represents late failures and cannot represent early ones at all, which biases any future reach-gate recalibration trained on it. Allow a label to be written with a null or sentinel template when the dispatch record carries a goal and an execution id, so that pre-selection failures enter the corpus rather than being silently dropped. The verdict for the observed dispatch was recorded only in operator memory: the walk reasoned correctly with target inference at confidence 0.9 and died on infrastructure, specifically an unquoted ampersand in a synthesized curl command, now fixed in goal-host-vessel 99d6305.

REPRODUCED by Codex integration pilot 2026-09-10: dispatch ac2dc732-c089-4a43-a92f-aebc4ad6d3fb (dependency-order goal; independent expected [A,B,C]) terminated failed with no selectedTemplateId and no answerBody. MCP provide_feedback returned the same missing-selectedTemplateId refusal. Preserve this dispatch-level negative label without inventing an activity identity. This is operator-supplied evidence, not autonomous discovery.

Edit repos/local-tools-vessel/src/index.ts: the vessel that executes arbitrary shell commands on behalf of the whole fleet keeps no record of what it ran, so the substrate cannot attribute its own resource consumption. Its journal over a ten minute window contained only [gc-tick] lines. Measured consequence on 2026-08-30: substrate-live sat at loadavg 41 to 57 on 14 CPUs, and the dominant consumers were about 13 concurrent `timeout 240 bun test` command pairs. Attributing them by /proc/<pid>/cgroup showed system.slice/local-tools-vessel.service, so they were shell commands dispatched through this vessel rather than spawned by mitosis evaluation or by pull-sync's own gate loop. Which caller composed and dispatched those command strings could not be determined, because neither the sh() helper at line 103 nor the second spawn site at line 280 logs the command, its caller, or its duration. The two spawn sites already wrap commands in groupBounded for timeout safety, so a log line at the same point costs nothing extra. Emit at minimum the command string (truncated), the originating trace or dispatch id if present in the request, the exit code and the duration, so that a future investigation can answer 'what is running on this box and who asked for it' without process forensics. Note for whoever fixes this: attribute by cgroup, not by cwd or ppid - the observed processes had cwd under development-vessel's clone while their cgroup correctly identified local-tools-vessel, and that mismatch produced two wrong root-cause attributions before it was caught.

PROVEN BY CONTROL, not inferred. Commit b857661 measured 1895 pass / 0 fail earlier today. RE-RUNNING THE SAME COMMIT later, with several composes in flight, gives 1890 pass / 5 fail — exactly these five. Same tree, same bun, same in-container path; only fleet load differed. The five also pass in isolation (4/4 and 28/0) and together with their neighbours (55/0).

WHY IT MATTERS: pull-sync's pre-cutover gate reads a red test as a regression INTRODUCED by the patch under test, so these silently block unrelated landings whenever the substrate is busy — which is precisely when it is trying to land things. It also cost real diagnostic time here: I attributed them to my own cutover change and only cleared it by re-running the previously-green baseline.

ORACLE: run the full suite twice at ONE commit while at least two composes are in flight. The failing set must be identical, and must not contain these five.

LIKELY DIRECTION (unverified): the spawned check returns non-zero or fails to start under CPU contention and the assertion reads that as a substantive verdict — the same 'could not ask vs answered no' class as goal-host f5c4052, development-vessel c7dbf97 and local-tools e4d604c. Check what staticEvaluate does with a non-zero/absent exit before changing any assertion.

summary: REJECTED 2026-08-30 - FALSE POSITIVE, verified against the wrong file. The claim was that substrateGap_write returns action:created/updated while the row never reaches gaps.json. The verification read /workspace/gaps/gaps.json (row count 2670, mtime 2026-08-30T06:09:58Z). That is NOT the live store. development-vessel runs with WORKSPACE_ROOT=/workspace/git/super-repo and substrate-gap.ts stores at WORKSPACE_ROOT/gaps/gaps.json, i.e. /workspace/git/super-repo/gaps/gaps.json (mtime 2026-08-30T08:05:22Z, live). The two are separate regular files, not symlinks. DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE: this gap's own probe id write-path-live-test-probe appears 3 times in the LIVE store and 0 times in the stale one; the second cited write gap-to-feature-narrowing-guard-b appears 6 times in the live store. Both writes persisted exactly as reported. The write path is not defective. NOTE, and the reason this is worth recording rather than deleting: the substrate's own codebase already documents the trap - boredom-vessel/src/index.ts carries the comment that /workspace/gaps/gaps.json is a copy frozen 2026-08-08. A detector reading that path will keep manufacturing this same false positive, and at ~1.7 composes/hour a false gap does real damage: it consumes scarce repair budget, and a fix applied to a working write path would BREAK it. The durable fix is that anything reading the gap store must resolve WORKSPACE_ROOT rather than hardcode /workspace/gaps.

summary: The substrate has no activity or check that counts ppid=1 orphaned processes grouped by cgroup/systemd unit. This class of defect (a spawned child surviving its own tracked lifecycle, becoming an untracked orphan) caused a real thermal emergency 2026-08-30 -- 14 orphaned bun test processes were invisible to a concurrency governor that correctly tracked its own slot bookkeeping. A periodic check (count ppid=1 processes per unit's cgroup, alert or auto-reap above a threshold) would have caught this class without an operator manually walking /proc. This is a law-6 followon: 'what activity would detect this class without me.'

adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.92, 0.95): The patch only kills descendant processes on timeout, not on normal command completion. The tree‑walk `__killtree` is invoked solely inside the watchdog:

```
if kill -0 "$__cpid" 2>/dev/null; then
  __killtree "$__cpid" -9 &
fi
```

If the command finishes before the watchdog fires, no call to `__killtree` occurs, leaving any child processes (e.g., `bun test` workers or `bun --watch` descendants) orphaned. After normal exit the script only cleans up PID files and exits:

```
wait "$__cpid"
__status=$?
kill "$__wpid" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f ${commandPidFile} ${watchdogPidFile}
exit "$__status"
```

Thus the fix does not guarantee the full descendant tree is terminated on all execution paths, leaving the original gap unaddressed for non‑timeout exits. fi
```

If the command finishes before the watchdog fires, no call to `__killtree` occurs, leaving any child processes (e.g., `bun test` workers or `bun --watch` descendants) orphaned. After normal exit the script only cleans up PID files and exits:

```
wait "$__cpid"
__status=$?
kill "$__wpid" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f ${commandPidFile} ${watchdogPidFile}
exit "$__status"

adversarial refuters agreed 2/2 (conf 0.92, 0.95): The patch only kills descendant processes on timeout, not on normal command completion. The tree‑walk `__killtree` is invoked solely inside the watchdog:

```
if kill -0 "$__cpid" 2>/dev/null; then
  __killtree "$__cpid" -9 &
fi
```

If the command finishes before the watchdog fires, no call to `__killtree` occurs, leaving any child processes (e.g., `bun test` workers or `bun --watch` descendants) orphaned. After normal exit the script only cleans up PID files and exits:

```
wait "$__cpid"
__status=$?
kill "$__wpid" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f ${commandPidFile} ${watchdogPidFile}
exit "$__status"
```

Thus the fix does not guarantee the full descendant tree is terminated on all execution paths, leaving the original gap unaddressed for non‑timeout exits. summary: CLAUDE.md states the floor contract: 'Given any arbitrary task, the substrate must at worst match what a ReAct-style agent (reason -> act -> observe, looped) would do... the walk with tool-enabled fallback IS the ReAct loop, with the difference that every step lands in a trace.' Measured 2026-09-01, the edit path does not meet that floor and structurally cannot, because it routes AROUND the walk. goal-host logs 'EARLY EDIT-INTENT DETECTED (pre-walk, names <file>) - routing to feature_compose', so an edit goal never enters the walk that the contract names as its guarantee. It lands in feature_compose, whose drafter is a SINGLE-SHOT LLM call over pre-assembled static grounding (grounding_len ~55000, region:null on every fc-plan observed). MEASUREMENT: on two goals dispatched this session against files an operator-driven ReAct loop edited correctly in 1-2 attempts, the compose lane took 2 attempts and failed (route-edit-f823889a), and 2 attempts and landed a HOLLOW change (route-edit-c9ad6782, which named shape 'failurePatternReport' -- not among the 390 advertised shapes -- and so resolved to nothing while passing typecheck, the semantic gate, the adversarial refuters, and cutover). Per-attempt success across the lane is 1.6%. THE DECOMPOSITION IS NOT LATENCY: a compose runs 5-13 minutes, comparable to a human-driven edit including tests. It is success-rate x inter-attempt amnesia. The drafter cannot call a tool mid-draft -- it guessed the shape name twice because it could not ask the registry, a question registry_query answers in one call -- and it carries only failure_lessons (last 5, reasons sliced to 200 chars) between attempts, versus full context. ~60 attempts at 1.6% separated by cooldown/backoff/queue, versus 1-2 attempts with continuity, produces days-versus-minutes with no other ingredient. Model tier is NOT the explanation: the drafter runs claude-sonnet-5 / claude-haiku-4-5, which would resolve a registry name if it could ask.

summary: REJECTED 2026-09-02 — the mechanism this gap asserts does not exist. Traced to the source. There is NO credit asymmetry. applyOutcomeToPosteriors has exactly two call sites (activities.ts:2438, goal-paths.ts:762). The high-volume one passes a synthetic tag ['dispatcher_used:goal-host'] which forces classifyReach -> 'ungraded', and posterior-update.ts:1002-1004 gives an ungraded outcome {alphaDelta 0, betaDelta 0} — neither credited NOR blamed, in both directions. Its own comment states the intent: 'Honest-reach floor: goal-host does not (yet) emit a reach verdict on this body, so an exit-status completion is UNGRADED, not credit... Remove once goal-host emits reach tags on this path.' So thompson_alpha sitting at the 1.00 prior on a template with 48 successful_executions is not suppression — it is 48 UNGRADED completions. successful_executions counts caller-reported exit status (activities.ts:2239, success_delta = validated.success ? 1 : 0); alpha/beta move only on graded REACHES. Two different questions, and the system is correctly refusing to answer the second using the first — the same discipline that keeps landed_commit at 0 closes / 772 false_closes rather than closing on provenance. FOUR MECHANISMS WERE PROPOSED FOR THIS ANOMALY IN ONE SESSION AND ALL FOUR WERE WRONG: chain-credit asymmetry; a stored success_rate of 0 corrupting reconstruction; ribosome-extracted pathways outperforming seeded ones 3x; and Thompson suppressing minted pathways. The '66% success' figure behind the third was exit-status completions, not reaches, so it never supported the claim. Each died on contact with the code, and the trace that killed the last should have been the FIRST step rather than the fifth. THE REAL FINDING IS NARROWER AND IS FILED SEPARATELY: goal-host emits no reach verdict on the execution body, so the majority of executions are unlearnable-from by design, capping the learning rate at the fraction of work carrying a reach tag.

summary: THE CEILING CONTRACT IS CURRENTLY UNFALSIFIABLE FROM THE STORE, and that is the finding. Measured over goal_execution_paths: repeated tasks (total_executions>1) succeed at 17.8% (2,173 paths / 15,602 execs) vs first-time tasks at 20.5% (7,227 paths / 7,227 execs); and within the repeated population the rate DECLINES MONOTONICALLY with repetition — >=2:17.8%, >=3:17.7%, >=5:17.4%, >=10:16.7%, >=20:15.2%. That curve is consistent with 'learning does not compound' AND EQUALLY with RETRY SELECTION: a goal that succeeds on attempt 1 keeps total_executions=1 and stops, while a goal that keeps failing is retried and accumulates executions, so high-N paths are enriched for hard-or-impossible goals BY CONSTRUCTION. Aggregates cannot separate the two.

classification_metadata.closure_blocker: The store AGGREGATES per goal+path (total_executions / successful_executions) and keeps no per-execution ordering, so no query over it can distinguish learning from retry selection. Falsifying the ceiling contract needs a WITHIN-GOAL TEMPORAL comparison: for a given goal+path, did the success rate of its LATER executions exceed its EARLIER ones? That data lives in the execution traces (executed_at + reached per row), not in goal_execution_paths — the join is the missing reader.
classification_metadata.OPERATOR_CORRECTION: I first reported this as 'the ceiling contract is measurably NOT met'. That claim does not survive the retry-selection confound and is WITHDRAWN. What is established is weaker and still useful: NO LEARNING ADVANTAGE IS VISIBLE in the aggregate, and the aggregate cannot in principle show one. Do not quote 17.8% vs 20.5% as refutation of the architecture.

SCHEMA:252: read successful_executions/total_executions, never the aliased success_count, which is stale on any row with >1 execution.
classification_metadata.why_it_matters: The ceiling claim — 'a task the system has done before should run over the pathway it learned, cheaper faster and more reliable' — is the justification for tracing every step. It has never been evaluated in either direction, and tonight's attempt shows the reason is structural: the table designed to record pathway reuse cannot answer the question, because it discards execution order. That is the same shape as every other defect found today — the information exists (executed_at and reached are on the trace rows) and does not arrive where the decision is made.
classification_metadata.detection_question_law6: Build the within-goal temporal comparison as a resolvable shape: for each goal_hash with >=N executions, split its traces at the median timestamp and compare reach rate of the later half against the earlier half. Positive delta = the pathway is compounding; zero or negative = it is not; and unlike the aggregate, retry selection cannot fake it because both halves come from the SAME goal.
CAVEATS_STATED_BEFORE_ANYONE_QUOTES_THIS: successful_executions is the per-goal reach accumulator (SCHEMA:10 'whether it reached its target, accumulating per-goal alpha/beta'), so this is a reach comparison — but it inherits any defect in reach grading, including the half-implemented downgrade fixed only hours earlier in 7dabe62. Rows written before that fix carry the old rule.

SELECTION EFFECT NOT CONTROLLED: goals that get repeated may be systematically harder than one-shot goals, which would depress the repeated bucket independently of learning. This measurement does not separate them and must not be quoted as proof that reuse is harmful — only that no advantage is visible.

Law 5 specifies boredom as condition-driven SELECTION ('when idle, select what to do from current conditions folded into selection weights'); a named target-template dispatch is a static call, not a weight. summary: FALSIFIER CHECKED AND RESOLVED — the gap stands as a MISSING-IDENTIFIER gap, not a lookup gap. I wrote the falsifier 'if some existing field already carries activity-api goal_hash into the commit or the compose report, this is a lookup gap'; checked it, and it does not. The commit builder at development-vessel/src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts:2209-2215 emits exactly: 'substrate-authored: apply <proposalId> via mitosis cutover' plus trailers Gap/Proposal/Mitosis/Base SHA at staging. No goal_text, no activity-api goal_hash. STRONGER CONFIRMATION FROM THE SYSTEM ITSELF: vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts:471 computes linked_to_gap as `gapId.length > 0 && gapId !== 'unknown-gap' && !gapId.startsWith('route-edit-')` -- the substrate EXPLICITLY classifies route-edit-* provenance as NOT a gap linkage, because it is a synthetic id derived from goal-host's local FNV-1a hash rather than a real gap. Measured consequence: 229 of the route-edit commits landed on origin/dev in 30 days are self-classified linked_to_gap=false. The system is honest about its own attribution hole; nothing closes it. ORIGINAL FINDING UNCHANGED: goal-host-vessel/src/goal-target-inference.ts:28 goalHashOf() is FNV-1a 32-bit over NFC/lowercase/whitespace-collapsed text -> 8 hex chars, and appears in commit subjects as route-edit-<hash> and in executionIds as feature_compose:rejected:<hash>; activity-api/src/routes/goal-paths.ts:176 hashGoal() is md5(normalizeGoal(goal)) truncated to 16 hex -> goal_execution_paths.goal_hash. Different algorithms, different lengths, no transform relates them. The goal-host comment at goal-target-inference.ts:36 states the split is intentional and notes activity-api keys its posteriors from goal_text independently, so the LEARNING LOOP IS NOT BROKEN -- recordGoalPath posts goal_text and activity-api hashes it itself. What is broken is EXTERNAL ATTRIBUTION: given a landed commit, nothing can find the goal row, its walk tier, its posterior, or its reach verdict. This blocked the measurement it was attempted for (quantifying how often a dispatch graded reached=false actually landed on origin -- n=2 verified individually, no rate computable). My attempted 8-char-prefix join of 196 landed hashes against 9416 goal_execution_paths rows returned 0 matches, but a NEGATIVE CONTROL of 196 random 8-hex prefixes ALSO returned 0, so that result is uninformative and is retracted as evidence. NOTE the positive architectural finding alongside this: the cutover REFUSES to land without provenance (structuredError cutover_refused_missing_provenance at :2206 -- 'every landing must carry gap_id and proposal_id; pass adhoc: true only for consciously unattributed operator work'). The discipline exists; the identifier it carries is just the wrong one for joining to learning state. FIX DIRECTION (not applied, needs a decision because it touches the mitosis commit path that all autonomous landing depends on): add activity-api's goal_hash, or the goal_text, as an additional commit trailer beside Gap/Proposal.

ROOT CAUSE beneath the false-negative reach verdicts, and it is NOT simply 'the verdict is read too early'. The compose report is a SINGLE MUTABLE FILE keyed on goal hash at /workspace/proposals/route-edit-<goalHashOf(goal)>-compose-report.json. When an early compose attempt LANDS a commit and a later retry is rolled back, the retry OVERWRITES the file, so the only surviving record says the work failed. Measured on both of tonight's dispatches: (a) route-edit-03f9a89c -- commit 82b030e landed on origin/dev at 04:39:57, report file mtime 04:56:16, SIXTEEN MINUTES LATER, containing verdict=UNFAVORABLE ok=false op_count=1 rolled_back=true cutovers=[] ; (b) route-edit-98efdb48 -- commit edd2e44 landed at 04:28:01, report mtime 04:28:27, containing verdict=UNFAVORABLE ok=false op_count=3 rolled_back=true cutovers=[]. In both cases cutovers is EMPTY while the commit is provably on origin/dev. CONSEQUENCE: goal-host ALREADY CONTAINS the correct reconciler for this at src/index.ts:15968 -- it reads the compose report, extracts result.new_git_sha from report.cutovers, and grades reached:true only when a real sha exists, with an explicit comment refusing to grade a staged-but-not-landed edit because that 'manufactures a hollow green'. That logic is right and it is unreachable in practice for two reasons: it is gated on the dispatch having been INTERRUPTED (status still 'running' at restart), and even when it runs it requires report.verdict === 'FAVORABLE' and a non-empty cutovers array -- both of which the retry has already erased. So the substrate has the correct reader and has destroyed the evidence it reads. NOTE the semantic_gate reason recorded for 03f9a89c is itself downstream of this: 'The patch changes the behavior of a different part of the code that does not fix the original issue with the safeCount function' -- the adversarial refuters were judging a REDUNDANT re-application against a file that the earlier attempt had already fixed, so their rejection was locally reasonable and the rollback was correct. The defect is that the retry then overwrote the record of the success. FIX DISPATCHED for the verdict half (dd46c830-55d4-4d55-a302-f67970a6a0ac): consult git for a commit matching route-edit-<hash> on origin/dev before returning reached:false, rather than trusting the clobbered report. THE EVIDENCE-DESTRUCTION HALF IS NOT FIXED: the report writer should not clobber a report whose cutovers recorded a landing -- version it, append, or refuse to overwrite a landed record. FALSIFIER: if some attempt-scoped copy of the report is retained elsewhere (a per-attempt suffix or an archived proposals directory), then the evidence is not destroyed and only the READER needs to look in the right place.

In repos/activity-api/src/routes/execution-traces.ts, the GET '/selection-outcomes' route returns HTTP 500 on every single call and has never once served a response. Its `selectionsQuery` reads `FROM thompson_selection_log AS sel`, and SurrealDB does not support table aliases, so the statement fails to parse with "Unexpected token `AS`, expected Eof". The alias is also referenced in the WHERE conditions built above it as `sel.activity_id`, `sel.selected_at`, and in the `ORDER BY sel.selected_at DESC`. Remove the table alias from this one route: change the FROM clause to `FROM thompson_selection_log`, drop the `sel.` prefix from the three condition strings that build `selectionConditions`, and change the ORDER BY to `ORDER BY selected_at DESC`. The bare column names are correct because there is only one table in the statement. Do not restructure the handler otherwise — the two-fetch pattern it already uses (read selections, then read the execution table by correlation_id, then join in memory) is the same JOIN-free shape that commit 471febb established for the sibling route GET '/selection-calibration', which works today. Verify by curling the route and getting HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 500; an empty result array is the expected and correct outcome, because this route reads the legacy recommend-driven selection path that migration 202 superseded with universal per-execution capture.

summary: In repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts, the edit-intent escalation return block grades a goal `reached: false` even when the edit has already landed on origin/dev. The block returns an object containing `selectedTemplateId: "feature_compose"`, `reached: false`, and `executionId: `feature_compose:rejected:${goalHashOf(goal as string)}``, immediately after the tap line that ends `— returning the compose failure`. Before that return, add a last-chance landing check. Compute `const h = goalHashOf(goal as string);` and, for the vessel repo named by the edit file, spawn git in the checkout that tracks origin/dev — the path convention is `/workspace/git/vessels/<vessel>`, as the comment near line 1850 states — using `Bun.spawn` exactly like the existing call at line 10907 does. Run `git log origin/dev -1 --format=%H --grep=route-edit-<h>` and, if it prints a non-empty 40-character sha, return `reached: true` with `status: "completed"`, `executionId: `feature_compose:${sha}``, and a goalReachReason naming the sha as landing evidence; otherwise fall through to the existing `reached: false` return unchanged. This is the same evidence bar the function already applies a few lines earlier, where a landed sha from patch_with_tools is graded `reached:true` — it is a timing fix, not a change to what counts as a reach.
