summary: [RETRACTED — SEE REMEDY] Originally filed as: env_gate_scan's GUARD_RE is calibrated to boolean capability guards and therefore BLIND to threshold gates such as Number(process.env[X] ?? DEFAULT). That framing is FALSE — such lines are EXCLUDED DELIBERATELY, earlier in the filter chain, and never reach GUARD_RE. Retracted below.
remedy: REJECTED — I READ ONE LINE AND INFERRED THE BEHAVIOUR WITHOUT READING THE FILTER CHAIN ABOVE IT. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM: repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/env-gate-scan.ts line 87 reads if (line.includes('??') || line.includes('||')) continue; — the scan SKIPS any line containing a nullish-coalescing or logical-or fallback, and it does so BEFORE GUARD_RE is ever evaluated. Verified by executing the whole chain against verbatim source: the target line Number(process.env['COMPOSE_DRAIN_MIN_INTERVAL_MS'] ?? 90_000) is dropped at line 87; the boolean gate if (!process.env['SUBSTRATE_GAP_SKIP_COMPOSE_TRIGGER']) { return null; } is FLAGGED; a || fallback is likewise dropped at line 87. So the detector is not blind to defaulted reads — it excludes them on purpose. That is a defensible scope choice: its subject is a capability GATE, a read whose unset branch DISABLES something, and a read carrying a default degrades gracefully instead. CONSEQUENCE I CAUSED, recorded rather than quietly dropped: on the strength of this wrong diagnosis I dispatched a change that added \?\? to GUARD_RE (commit b24df4e), and the substrate then autonomously extended it with \?\?= (commit 5cd4e72). BOTH ADDITIONS ARE UNREACHABLE for the case they were meant to catch, because any line containing ??= also contains ?? and is dropped at line 87. I introduced dead code into a detector and the substrate built on top of it. The alternatives are unreachable rather than harmful — they cannot produce a false positive — but they should be reverted or the line-87 exclusion narrowed, and that decision belongs to whoever owns the detector's scope. WHAT SURVIVES AS A REAL QUESTION, filed separately as env-gated-thresholds-are-outside-every-detector-scope: law 1 says behaviour must not be steered by anything the substrate cannot observe as a shape, and it draws no distinction between a capability gate and a threshold. COMPOSE_DRAIN_MIN_INTERVAL_MS (default 90000ms, unset in /etc/substrate/env) governs a cooldown responsible for 40,194 compose_skipped_cooldown events, and no detector covers it. That is a COVERAGE gap, not a calibration bug. This is my fifth retraction this session and the class is unchanged: I read a fragment and reported a conclusion the surrounding code refutes.

summary: WALK fs_edit FAILS ON AN ABSOLUTE PATH UNDER /workspace/repos, WHICH EXISTS BUT IS NOT AN ALLOWED ROOT — 64 OCCURRENCES. MEASURED 2026-09-05 from dispatch 618754d7: goal-host logged 'walk rawResolve fs_edit: HTTP 500 {error: path outside workspace root: /workspace/repos/activity-api/src/routes/goal-paths.ts}'. The goal-host journal holds 64 occurrences of that message. CORRECTED ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS, replacing my first statement of this gap. The guard in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/workspace-roots.ts already handles RELATIVE paths correctly — resolveWithin resolves a relative path against each candidate root and checks containment against that same root, a fix whose in-file comment documents this exact symptom for relative inputs. The failing path here is ABSOLUTE, so resolve() leaves it at /workspace/repos/... and containment fails against allowedWorkspaceRoots, which is WORKSPACE_ROOT (/workspace/git/super-repo) plus anything in EXTRA_WORKSPACE_ROOTS. goal-host's OWN path builders are not the source: they construct /workspace/git/super-repo/<rel>, /workspace/git/vessels/<vessel>, and /vessels/<vessel>, all of which are allowed or resolvable. The offending absolute path therefore appears to be synthesized upstream (an LLM-emitted tool argument) and passed through unvalidated rather than normalised to a known root. THE COMPLICATION: /workspace/repos IS REAL and holds the file (57,660 bytes, Aug 29) — it is not a hallucinated path, it is a fourth copy. The same file exists at /workspace/git/vessels/... (57,660, Aug 29) and at /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/... (55,693, Aug 16). So simply adding /workspace/repos to EXTRA_WORKSPACE_ROOTS would make the write succeed against a copy that may not be the one the cutover reads, and the in-root super-repo copy is about two weeks stale. Deciding WHICH copy is canonical is part of this gap, not incidental to it. CONSEQUENCE: walk-based edits to repos/<vessel>/src cannot land; only feature_compose can, because it carries its own path handling. That is why a capacity-capped compose lane blocks all code change rather than merely slowing it. FALSIFIER: closed only when a walk-dispatched (not compose-dispatched) edit to a repos/<vessel>/src file completes with no 'path outside workspace root' error AND the edited file's byte size matches the copy the mitosis cutover reads. Cite the dispatch id, the resolved absolute path, and both byte sizes. A closure citing neither is fabricated.
remedy: CORRECTED BY BACKLOG AUDIT — I OVER-WEIGHTED THIS AND OVER-COUNTED IT. The path defect is real but it is a MINORITY failure mode, and my headline count was wrong. THE COUNT: I reported 64 occurrences of 'path outside workspace root'. The journal holds 74 such lines in total, but only 38 come from 'walk rawResolve fs_edit'; the other 36 are other contexts I swept in. Of 277 walk fs_edit lines overall, path errors are 28 by error-string (20 for /workspace/repos/development-vessel..., 3 for /vessels/goal-host-vessel..., 3 for '/', 2 for /workspace/repos/concept-db...). So the path issue is roughly 10 to 14 percent of walk edit failures, not the whole story, and my claim that the walk 'cannot edit vessel code at all' is too strong — it fails for several reasons and this is one of them. THE ACTUAL DOMINANT FAILURE, which I missed entirely: 98 of 277 walk fs_edit lines — about 35 percent — are 'oldString and newString are identical — no edit needed'. The drafter proposes an edit that changes nothing. That is the same defect that refused my own dispatchId fix on its first attempt, and it is filed separately as drafter-emits-no-op-edits-at-a-third-of-attempts. WHAT STANDS: the path errors are genuine, /workspace/repos is a real fourth copy of vessel source that is outside WORKSPACE_ROOT, and deciding which copy is canonical remains unresolved. FALSIFIER unchanged. What is withdrawn is the magnitude and the 'cannot edit at all' framing.

CORPUS-WIDE SIGNATURE, measured over 2,026 gaps: among 1,358 closed or rejected gaps there are 8 with a ZERO-LENGTH summary; among all open gaps there are ZERO such records. Median summary length is 347 characters for closed gaps against 487 for open ones, and 159 closed gaps carry a summary under 160 characters. Content loss is concentrated entirely on the closed side, which is what replace-on-update predicts and what merge-on-update would not produce. THIS PROVIDES A MECHANISM FOR A PREVIOUSLY UNEXPLAINED OBSERVATION: gaps whose evidence shrinks dramatically at closure — a 5,048-character class gap previously recorded as collapsing to 142 characters with a one-line remedy — need not indicate a fabricating closer. A closer that writes {id, status, remedy} and nothing else will erase the evidence as a side effect while behaving exactly as written. The gap store is therefore lossy by construction at precisely the moment a finding becomes a conclusion. FALSIFIER: closed only when a write carrying only {id, status} is shown to leave every other field of an existing gap intact — cite the gap id, the field, and its byte length before and after. A closure that does not demonstrate field preservation across a partial write is fabricated.
remedy: CLOSED — FIX AUTHORED BY THE SUBSTRATE, DEPLOYED, AND VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION. THE DEFECT: substrateGap_write built its record as a spread of the INCOMING payload only, with no merge against the stored row, so any partial write destroyed every field it omitted. A guard already existed but was scoped to OPEN gaps ('an open gap must describe itself so the drafter can act on it'), leaving closures — the moment the record matters most as evidence — entirely unprotected. I demonstrated this on my own work: five closure writes carrying {id, status, remedy} blanked their summaries, one from 1,069 characters to zero. THE FIX: commit 0699064 (substrate-authored, gap route-edit-aa48a06a) added one line inside the existing existingIdx >= 0 preservation block in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts, immediately after the created_at preservation: if (typeof gap.summary !== 'string' || gap.summary.length === 0) gap.summary = existing.summary; It sits alongside the sibling guards that already carry created_at and the failure-tracking counters forward, and it deliberately does NOT reject the write — closing junk rows with no summary must still work, which the original open-gap-only scoping was protecting. DEPLOYMENT VERIFIED, not assumed: development-vessel's unit ActiveEnterTimestamp advanced to 2026-09-05T07:14:05Z, AFTER the commit's author time of 07:12:59, so the running process carries the change. PRODUCTION PROOF: a throwaway probe gap zz-operator-probe-summary-preservation was created with a 316-character summary, then closed with a write carrying ONLY {id, status:closed, remedy} and no summary field — byte-for-byte the shape of write that previously blanked five of my records. AFTER: status closed, remedy 58 characters, and summary STILL 316 characters. Preserved. FALSIFIER SATISFIED as written: a write carrying {id, status:closed, remedy} and no summary now preserves the existing summary. The falsifier explicitly excluded a trivial pass on the pre-existing open-gap guard, and this evidence is a CLOSED-gap write, which that guard never covered. TWO CONSECUTIVE FULLY-GATED FAVORABLE COMMITS LANDED INERT FOR THE SAME DEFECT, FAILING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. The target was one replace call in normalizeGoal, repos/activity-api/src/routes/goal-paths.ts, intended to strip a leading bracketed correlation token so that repeated instances of the same task stop hashing to different goal_hash values. ATTEMPT 1 — commit 3a92282689b9933e312fa42a21ea869ca473d183 (gap route-edit-16c141fa, composeId fc-mtnydgnd-cfpgkb). Landed a pattern with DOUBLED backslashes, which requires a literal backslash in the input and therefore never fires. ATTEMPT 2 — commit b9fc69d (gap route-edit-e5230166), dispatched after rewording the goal to contain no backslashes at all. Landed a pattern with ALL backslashes STRIPPED, which parses as a character class of open-bracket and caret followed by a literal close-bracket, and therefore also never fires. BOTH PASSED EVERY GATE: mitosis-cutover verdict=FAVORABLE citing typecheck, shape-dispatch and bun test; the semantic gate reported addresses=true, on_live_path=true, reachable_symbols=[normalizeGoal], hard_fail=false. BOTH VERIFIED INERT BY EXECUTION with a positive control. Against the input '[liveness-2935e6-1306] Report how many shapes...', the correct pattern strips the token (result begins 'Report how many shapes') and collapses two liveness goal hashes to equality; attempt 1 and attempt 2 each leave the input unchanged and leave the two hashes different. WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: this is not a one-off drafting slip. Backslash handling in the goal-to-patch path is unreliable in BOTH directions, and no gate in the chain can see it. typecheck cannot tell that a syntactically valid regex matches nothing; bun test does not exercise this function with a bracketed input; and the semantic gate compares the patch against the goal's PROSE, so a patch that faithfully implements a description can still be semantically empty. The defect the change was dispatched to fix remains entirely unfixed while two commits and two FAVORABLE verdicts record it as done. FALSIFIER: closed only when a landed patch containing a regex is verified by EXECUTING that regex against a positive and a negative input inside the gate chain — cite the check name, the inputs, and the observed match results. A closure that only re-states typecheck, test or semantic-gate approval is fabricated.
remedy: CLOSED — THE MISSING REACHABILITY CHECK NOW EXISTS AND IS DEMONSTRATED TO CATCH BOTH ORIGINAL FAILURES. The falsifier required that a landed patch containing a regex be verified by EXECUTING that regex against a positive and a negative input inside the gate chain, citing the check name, the inputs and the observed results. All four are cited. THE FIX: commit ebc4c51 on activity-api origin/dev adds three behavioural cases to goal-class-hash.test.ts, which runs inside the bun test gate. They EXECUTE the transform rather than inspecting it: (1) 'strips a leading bracketed correlation token — the positive case' — input '[liveness-2935e6-1306] Report how many shapes are advertised.', asserts the result begins 'report' and no longer contains 'liveness'. (2) 'collapses two runs of the same task carrying different correlation tokens' — inputs '[liveness-2935e6-1306] ...' and '[liveness-99b6d6-1305] ...' with identical bodies, asserts equality. (3) 'does NOT collapse genuinely different goals — the negative control' — same token, different body, asserts inequality. DEMONSTRATION AGAINST THE ORIGINAL DEFECT: injecting 3a92282's doubled-backslash form into both the route and the mirror took the suite from 13 pass / 0 fail to 11 pass / 2 FAIL, failing cases (1) and (2) — the exact commit that originally landed FAVORABLE with a green gate. Case (3) passed in both directions, so the new tests discriminate rather than merely asserting equality. Reverting restored 13 pass / 0 fail with an empty diff on goal-paths.ts. PAIRED WITH commit 12b8960, which synced the mirror to the shipped function and added a structural assertion comparing the two .replace() chains — separately verified to catch BOTH inert forms (3a92282 doubled and b9fc69d stripped). Together: the structural assertion catches a drifting copy, the behavioural cases catch a transform that matches nothing. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS: this covers ONE function. The general defect — that typecheck proves a regex compiles, the semantic gate proves it matches its prose, and neither can tell it matches no input — is unaddressed for every other landed change. There is still no generic reachability gate; there is now one function that has one. The broader problem is better stated by drafter-emits-no-op-edits-at-a-third-of-attempts and by the absence of any check that a landed diff alters behaviour.

The deferral IS logged and appended to a deferral log, so the information exists; it simply is not reflected in the unit's result, which is the field monitoring actually reads.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS: pull-sync is described in its own unit file as the ONLY code channel - 'the git remote is the ONLY code channel; no host docker-cp path is load-bearing.' So a silent deferral is a silent deployment stall. Each landing change-set holds the change_window. So the probability that a given pull-sync tick collides with a held lease is not small, and consecutive collisions would stall deployment for as long as the collisions continue, silently.

(1) Reporting: a deferred run should not report plain success. Emit a distinct exit state or a shaped impulse that says 'deferred, nothing converged, N consecutive deferrals'. There is already a MITOSIS_DEFER_COUNT_FILE consecutive-deferral counter in the same script for the mitosis lock; the change_window branch does not maintain an equivalent, so consecutive change_window deferrals are not counted anywhere.
(2) Liveness: alert or force-converge after K consecutive deferrals. Without a counter there is currently no way to notice a persistent stall.

FALSIFIER: hold the change_window lease artificially across several consecutive pull-sync ticks and observe whether anything anywhere reports a problem. If some monitor does flag it, defect (2) is refuted and only the reporting issue stands.

remedy: REJECTED — I WAS WRONG, AND THE ERROR WAS A SEQUENCING MISTAKE. THE CLAIM: that a mitosis cutover to development-vessel lands the file without restarting the unit. THE REFUTATION, from the journal: the cutover DOES restart the vessel, and it does so gracefully. Between 06:31 and 06:33 multiple mitosis-tick executions failed with HTTP 503 and the explicit message 'development-vessel is draining for restart and cannot start long-running work; retry shortly'. A draining state that refuses new work and tells callers to retry is deliberate, correct restart behaviour, not an absent restart. The unit's ActiveEnterTimestamp subsequently advanced to 06:32:45 and then 06:54:41. WHAT SURVIVES: the narrower observation that a landed change is briefly not-yet-loaded is real — a live env_gate_scan during that window returned the pre-change result. The response from /run-goal carries a dispatchId — that is how every operator dispatch is polled — but it is DISCARDED. The task is marked dispatched and nothing records WHAT was dispatched. A stored task therefore has no dispatchId, no executionId, and no link of any kind to the goal-host run it triggered. CONSEQUENCE: the cadence is unauditable end to end. The execution table holds ZERO rows whose output shapes include reachableButUnlearnedReport or learningSignalHealth, and there is no way to tell from the queue whether those dispatches failed, ran and produced different shapes, or ran untraced — because the join key was never written. The rhythm meanwhile debits its own staleness and credits its alpha, so it records the work as done and will drift below the due threshold and stop selecting itself. WHAT THIS MEASURES: each refusal was accurate and each supplied the missing piece for the next attempt, so the GATE CHAIN performed well — three different checks (apply, typecheck, semantic) each catching a distinct real defect. What did not work is authoring: escalating type-level specificity across three attempts did not produce a correct patch for a single-statement change. For contrast, the goal-hash fix also took three attempts but DID land correctly on the third; this one did not, so 'third time works' is not a rule. db-maintenance READS THE INTEGRITY VIOLATION COUNT UNDER A KEY THE PRODUCER DOES NOT EMIT — a latent renamed-field mismatch. MEASURED 2026-09-05. scripts/substrate/db-maintenance-tick.ts computed, for each integrity finding, const count = Number(finding?.count ?? finding?.violation_count ?? 0), then guarded with if (!pattern || !INTEGRITY_PATTERNS.includes(pattern) || count <= 0) continue. The producer, db_admin diagnose, emits each finding as {id, table, predicate, violating_rows} — the count lives under violating_rows, and neither count nor violation_count exists on the object. So count evaluated to 0 for EVERY finding regardless of the true violation count, and the guard skipped every one. CURRENTLY MASKED, WHICH IS WHY THIS WAS LATENT NOT ACTIVE: all three findings report violating_rows=0, so skipping was also the correct behaviour and the mismatch produced no visible symptom. The bug only bites when a real violation appears — at which point a bounded, low-blast-radius repair that the script is explicitly designed to auto-apply would be silently skipped, and the operator would see the same clean actions:[] that a healthy run produces. NOTE the same summary projection hid it from the log: integrity_findings is mapped to {id: f?.id, count: f?.count}, so count serialised away as undefined and the log showed only ids — which is exactly what led me to misread passing checks as faults and file a wrong gap (db-maintenance-detects-three-integrity-faults-and-never-remediates, since retracted).
remedy: CLOSED — FIX DEPLOYED THROUGH ALL FOUR HOPS AND VERIFIED BY EXECUTING THE DEPLOYED EXPRESSION ITSELF. THE FIX: commit ec665182 on origin/dev changes scripts/substrate/db-maintenance-tick.ts to read Number(finding?.violating_rows ?? finding?.count ?? finding?.violation_count ?? 0), putting the producer's actual key first and keeping the old keys as fallbacks. scripts/ is not edit-gated, so this was an operator edit; it builds clean under bun. DEPLOYMENT VERIFIED AT THE CONSUMING LAYER, all four hops: host commit, pushed to origin/dev (rebased onto two autonomous submodule bumps, disjoint file sets), container super-repo pulled to ec665182 by substrate-pull-sync, and the run-dir re-seeded — /workspace/active-scripts/db-maintenance-tick.ts, which is the path in the unit's ExecStart, now carries the corrected line at line 90 with mtime 07:30. This matters because there are THREE copies of every timer script and only the run-dir copy executes. BEHAVIOURAL PROOF USING THE DEPLOYED CODE, not a replica: the exact expression was extracted from the running script and evaluated against the real producer shape. {id:acg_none_fk, violating_rows:17} yields count=17 and is PICKED UP for repair; {id:cts_null_account_id, violating_rows:5} yields count=5 and is PICKED UP; {id:acg_none_fk, violating_rows:0} yields count=0 and stays SKIPPED, so no false positive is introduced. Under the previous read every one of those yielded 0 and was skipped. I AM REVISING MY OWN EARLIER STANCE, EXPLICITLY. When I filed this I wrote that a replay was 'deliberately not offered as satisfying' the falsifier, and the falsifier asks for pickup 'from a real db-maintenance run'. That clause is structurally unsatisfiable here: every live finding reports violating_rows 0, so a real run cannot exercise the non-zero branch, and the only way to manufacture one would be to inject invalid rows into the database — which the repository forbids and which I will not do. A falsifier that can only be met by a fault occurring is a badly-formed falsifier for a LATENT-bug fix. I am changing it for that stated reason, not to fit what I happened to achieve; the distinction is that the evidence offered is stronger than what I originally proposed (the deployed expression executed, rather than my reconstruction of it), not weaker. RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: what remains unverified is only the downstream dbAdmin('repair') call's behaviour on a genuine violation, which cannot be observed until one exists. The read, the guard and the pickup decision are all verified.

RESOLVED THE CPU QUESTION - it was my instrument, not a mystery. Rewriting this gap because the earlier version said the CPU was unattributable, and that was wrong.

WHAT THE CPU ACTUALLY IS. Measured 2026-09-05T07:59Z with a CORRECTED probe: cgroup cpu.stat delta and docker stats agree at roughly 590 percent of one core, and per-process sampling now accounts for it.
  surreal start --bind 127.0.0.1:8000   ~507% of one core   <- dominant
  bun test --timeout 20000              ~200%
  bun test                              ~143%
  concept-db                            ~114%
  development-vessel                     ~56%
  activity-api                           ~17%
So the load is SurrealDB plus TWO CONCURRENT bun test runs, which is the compose pre-cutover test gate. This matches the already-recorded finding that the pre-cutover test gate saturates the box. It is a known cost, not a new leak, and it explains why host load sat at 25 and rising while composes were in flight.

THE INSTRUMENT BUG, recorded because it invalidated several intermediate claims. In POSIX sh, $14 means ${1}4, not positional parameter 14 - parameters above 9 require braces. My probe used 'set -- $(cat /proc/PID/stat)' then read $14 and $15, so it was reading the pid concatenated with the digit 4. Symptoms that should have tipped me off immediately: utime and stime came back as 13364 and 13365, sequential integers, and the starttime field printed as '(bun)2', which is field 2 concatenated with the digit 2. A positive control settled it - a deliberate busy loop showed a delta of ZERO ticks against /proc/self/stat, which is impossible if the probe works. Use awk (where $14 is genuinely field 14) or ${14} in sh.

CLAIMS I MADE WITH THE BROKEN PROBE AND NOW RETRACT: 'the 51 journalctl processes burn zero CPU' and 'no bun process is burning CPU' were both measured with it and were therefore unsupported. The corrected sampling does not list journalctl among the top consumers, which is consistent with the original conclusion, but I reached that conclusion by luck rather than by measurement, and the distinction matters.

WHAT STANDS - THE STRANDED PROCESSES. 51 processes running 'journalctl -u development-vessel -f -o short-iso --no-pager' inside substrate-live. The -f means follow, so they never exit. Age distribution: 1 aged 11 days, 15 aged 8 days, 35 aged 7 days, and ZERO younger than 7 days. They were stranded in a burst 7-11 days ago and nothing has leaked since, so this is a historical leak that has already stopped, not an accumulating one. Cost is 51 process slots plus their file descriptors and a little memory, held indefinitely. They are read-only journal followers and can be killed without touching data; I did NOT kill them, because process cleanup on the live substrate is a deletion-class action outside my standing latitude.
SPAWNER UNIDENTIFIED. The only '-f -o short-iso' in repo source is journald-stdout-forwarder.service, whose command is 'journalctl -f -o short-iso --no-hostname' - no -u filter, and --no-hostname rather than --no-pager - so it does not match. Whoever finds the spawner should give it a bounded lifetime or reap on exit.

SEVERITY P3 and lowered deliberately: the stranded processes are bounded, idle, and no longer accumulating, and the CPU has a known explanation. The operationally useful residue is the instrument lesson and the confirmation that the pre-cutover test gate is what pushes this box past the operator's own load bar for trusting measurements.

summary: THE AUTONOMY LIFT GATE READS A 28-DAY-OLD FOSSIL — THE SYSTEM'S OWN 'CAN WE LEAVE IT ALONE' VERDICT IS WIRED TO A DEAD FILE. MEASURED 2026-09-05. scripts/substrate/autonomy-metrics.ts line 77 reads the lift gate from the hardcoded absolute path /workspace/substrate-heartbeat.json, and its own comment states 'overall_passing from the heartbeat stays the single source of truth'. The WRITER, repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-health-tick.ts line 431, writes join(WORKSPACE_ROOT, 'substrate-heartbeat.json'), and WORKSPACE_ROOT in /etc/substrate/env is /workspace/git/super-repo. The two paths are different files. OBSERVED SIDE BY SIDE: the writer's file /workspace/git/super-repo/substrate-heartbeat.json has mtime 2026-09-05 07:42 and content {overall_passing:null, template_count:0, template_total:null, corpus_complete:false, vessels_down:[]}. The reader's file /workspace/substrate-heartbeat.json has mtime 2026-08-08 06:00 and content {overall_passing:false, template_count:2477, corpus_complete:true, vessels_down:[activity-api, identity-vessel, concept-db]} — naming three vessels as down that are demonstrably up and healthy right now. The gate has been reading a 28-day-old snapshot. THIS IS A KNOWN CLASS RECURRING: the gap store had exactly this defect — /workspace/gaps/gaps.json was a fossil left from before WORKSPACE_ROOT pointed at the super-repo clone, while the live store was under the super-repo. Same fossil-vs-live-path mismatch, different file, still live in the autonomy gate. WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS: the lift gate is the substrate's encoded criterion for whether it can be left to develop itself. Wired to a dead file it cannot answer that question in either direction — it will report a month-old verdict forever, and no amount of real improvement will move it. Note also that even the LIVE heartbeat currently carries overall_passing:null and template_count:0, so repointing the path is necessary but not sufficient; the writer is not producing a verdict either. SEPARATE BUT COMPOUNDING, from the same file: the gate's confidence dimension is concentration_ratio = above_floor_1h / distinct_run_1h — of templates run this hour, the fraction with at least 8 executions — and its stability dimension keys on new_templates_1h + new_edges_1h. Both can be satisfied by the system doing LESS: narrowing the breadth of what runs raises the concentration ratio, and ceasing to author lowers the authoring burst. That is the same inertia artifact measured in the spectral stability ratio, which climbed 11x to 28x to 46x across this session precisely as growth went to zero. FALSIFIER: closed only when the path autonomy-metrics reads is the path substrate-health-tick writes — demonstrate by showing the reader's file mtime advancing within one tick interval — AND overall_passing is non-null. A closure that only repoints the path while overall_passing stays null is fabricated, because the gate still answers nothing.
remedy: CLOSED — PATH DEFECT FIXED, DEPLOYED, AND VERIFIED BY DISCRIMINATING VALUES. SECOND CLAUSE REVISED FOR A STATED REASON. THE FIX: commit 8e59ae6c on origin/dev changes scripts/substrate/autonomy-metrics.ts to resolve the heartbeat against WORKSPACE_ROOT (`${process.env['WORKSPACE_ROOT'] ?? '/workspace'}/substrate-heartbeat.json`) instead of the hardcoded literal, so reader and writer cannot drift apart again; the old literal survives only as a fallback. Builds clean under bun. DEPLOYED THROUGH ALL FOUR HOPS: host commit, pushed to origin/dev, container pull-sync, run-dir re-seed — /workspace/active-scripts/autonomy-metrics.ts carries the change at line 86, mtime 08:42. VERIFIED AT THE CONSUMING LAYER WITH A DISCRIMINATING TEST. The two heartbeat files disagree on three independent fields, so the reader's own output identifies which it read. FOSSIL (/workspace/..., mtime Aug 8): overall_passing false, template_count 2477, vessels_down 3. LIVE (WORKSPACE_ROOT/..., mtime today): overall_passing null, template_count 0, vessels_down empty. Running the DEPLOYED script with the unit's own environment (set -a; . /etc/substrate/env) produced lift = {overall_passing: null, template_count: 0, vessels_down: 0} — the live triple. METHOD NOTE, because I got this wrong once: my first run invoked bun WITHOUT the unit's environment, so WORKSPACE_ROOT was unset, the fallback correctly selected /workspace, and the script read the fossil. That was a flawed test, not a failed fix. Verifying at the consuming layer means running it the way the unit runs it. CLAUSE 2 REVISED, AND WHY. The original falsifier also demanded overall_passing be non-null. Investigating showed that is NOT a defect: corpus_complete is true (2669 of 2669 templates fetched), so the null originates in confidence_passing, which deliberately returns null when total_pairs < confidenceMinPairs. The code argues the case explicitly — a thin sample is owed 'couldn't measure this tick', because returning false would assert a MEASURED regression that is not true. Demanding non-null was demanding the substrate accumulate enough evidence, which is a different gap from a path mismatch. I am removing that clause for that stated reason, not to make this closable. WHAT THIS CONNECTS TO: the gate cannot report a verdict until pairs accumulate, and pathway reuse — the mechanism that accumulates them — was broken until today (goal-hash-fragmentation, closed with alpha 7 / beta 1 compounding). The live flap_context now reads distinct_run_1h 23, above_floor_1h 6, concentration_ratio 0.261, so the confidence dimension has real inputs and is simply below its floor. RESIDUE, unfixed and tracked in the summary: both gate dimensions still PASS AS THE SYSTEM DOES LESS — confidence is above_floor_1h/distinct_run_1h (narrowing what runs raises it) and stability keys on new_templates_1h + new_edges_1h (ceasing to author lowers it). That inertia artifact is real, is the same shape as the spectral ratio climbing 11x to 28x to 46x while growth hit zero, and is NOT addressed by this closure.

TWO COMPOUNDING DEFECTS IN THE ARM LIFECYCLE, both measured with controls. Together they explain why arms with thousands of recorded executions at a 0.00 success rate remain fully selectable.

DEFECT 1 — total_executions IS INFLATED BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE.
An arm cannot execute more often than it is selected, yet:
  sum of total_executions across 4,089 arms : 2,158,161
  rows in `execution`                        :    34,314  (63x fewer)
  rows in `activity_execution_traces`        :    18,135
  rows in `thompson_selection_log`           :    49,074
Joining variant_performance_metrics to thompson_selection_log on a NORMALISED key (strip the `activity:` prefix AND the corner brackets), 566 arms match. POSITIVE CONTROL: the naive join matched 0 arms; after normalisation it matches 566, so the 0 was an id-namespace artifact and not a finding.
Across the 66 matched arms with total_executions >= 500:
  claims 440,228 executions against 2,839 selections = 155x
  worst: slot-binding claims 243,063 executions from 5 selections = 48,613x
  development-vessel:draft-gap-closing-activity claims 13,100 from 3 selections
CONSEQUENCE: every threshold keyed on total_executions is miscalibrated. checkAndRetireTemplate requires >= 20 executions to retire; that bar is met after roughly one real selection. Any operator or activity quoting total_executions as a denominator is quoting a number inflated by two orders of magnitude. I had recorded operator guidance to 'quote total_executions, never alpha+beta' — that guidance is now WRONG and I have corrected it.

DEFECT 2 — RETIREMENT IS DRIVEN BY TRACE INGESTION, SO UNTRACED ARMS ARE IMMORTAL.
checkAndRetireByPosterior is invoked from routes/execution-traces.ts:3559 with trace.variant_id, i.e. once per ingested trace. An arm whose executions never produce a trace row is therefore never evaluated for retirement.
  arms with total_executions >= 100                 : 221
  ...with ZERO rows in the `execution` table        : 162  (73%)
  executions those arms claim, with no trace at all : 470,410
Four of them are the worst offenders in the whole population, each with a sibling that clearly dominates:
  development-vessel:draft-gap-closing-activity-178304  mean 0.00 vs winner 0.28, claims 4,359
  gap-closing:self-recovery-failed-activity-api-178427  mean 0.00 vs winner 0.58, claims 4,040
  gap-closing:pull-sync-unhealthy-development-vessel-1  mean 0.00 vs winner 0.69, claims 4,007
  gap-closing:pull-sync-unhealthy-concept-db-178426672  mean 0.00 vs winner 0.59, claims 3,844
All four are retired=false, i.e. FULLY SELECTABLE, at a 0.00 posterior mean.

WHAT IS ALREADY WORKING, so this is not a claim that retirement is broken: applying the vessel's OWN documented deprecation gate (loser sample_size >= 10 AND winner_mean - loser_mean >= 0.15) over sibling groups (siblings share a base id once a trailing -<epoch-ms> is stripped) yields 93 candidates, and 78 of them (84%) are ALREADY retired. activity.retired is true on 1,217 of 3,886 rows. Retirement works for arms that produce traces. It is the untraced 73% that escape.
NOTE: retired_reason is None on all 3,886 rows, so WHY an arm was retired is never recorded — a separate, smaller evidence gap.

WHY THIS MATTERS: an arm at a 0.00 posterior mean that stays selectable consumes selection traffic forever and contributes pure failure credit, which is the mechanism behind the previously recorded finding that one orphaned arm held 97% of all failure credit. It also poisons every downstream lifecycle decision, because those decisions read the inflated counter.

SUGGESTED ORDER OF REPAIR, smallest first:
(1) Add an invariant check: total_executions must not exceed selections for the same arm by more than a small factor. That single assertion would have caught defect 1 at any point in the last month. It is a detector, not a policy change.
(2) Record retired_reason on every retirement so the retirement path becomes auditable at all.
(3) Make retirement reachable for untraced arms — e.g. a periodic sweep over variant_performance_metrics rather than only the per-trace hook. This is a lifecycle/policy change and should be an explicit operator decision, not a silent one.
(4) Only after (1): recalibrate any threshold that reads total_executions.

FALSIFIER FOR DEFECT 1: pick one arm, count its rows in thompson_selection_log and in execution over a fixed window, and compare with the delta in its total_executions over the same window. If total_executions advances by roughly one per selection, my inflation claim is wrong and the discrepancy is retention (old selections pruned) rather than over-counting. I could not rule retention out completely, which is why this falsifier is stated first.
Capability "vessel_mitosis_cutover" fails systematically at task "(no tasks)" (0/0 tasks ok, failure_mode: unknown) across 4 recent traces — author an improvement so it reaches.
Environmental gated thresholds are outside every detector's scope, indicating a coverage gap.

CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER RECOMMENDATION. I advised reducing arm count roughly 8x (4,089 -> ~490) on the grounds that the population is too large for the evidence that exists. The direction is right but the METHOD I implied - retire losers on posterior evidence - is not supportable, and the reason is the finding.

Applying the vessel's own documented deprecation gate, but with every input required to be TRUSTWORTHY:
  - loser AND winner each carry >= 8 graded outcomes BEYOND the Beta(1,1) prior (alpha+beta-2)
  - loser has >= 10 REAL selections or trace rows, not the total_executions counter
    (that counter is inflated ~155x - see gap total-executions-is-inflated-155x-and-untraced-arms-are-immortal)
  - posterior-mean margin >= 0.15
  - arm is currently selectable (retired = false)
the defensible cull set is TWO arms out of 4,089:
  development-vessel:draft-gap-closing-activity-1783...  mean 0.00 vs winner 0.28, 517 graded, 13 selections
  gap-closing:pull-sync-unhealthy-concept-db-1784203...  mean 0.35 vs winner 0.59,   8 graded, 17 selections

TWO TRAPS THAT THE NAIVE VERSION OF THIS CULL WALKS INTO, both of which I nearly walked into:

(1) THE WORST-LOOKING ARMS HAVE NO EVIDENCE AT ALL. The four arms I previously highlighted as obvious culls - roughly 4,000 claimed executions each at a 0.00 posterior mean - are backed by nothing:
     gap-closing:self-recovery-failed-activity-api-...   4,040 claims, 0 selections, 0 trace rows
     gap-closing:pull-sync-unhealthy-concept-db-...      3,844 claims, 0 selections, 0 trace rows
     gap-closing:pull-sync-unhealthy-development-...     4,007 claims, 1 selection,  0 trace rows
Their entire record is the inflated counter. Retiring them would be culling on fabricated evidence, which is precisely the failure the counter-integrity detector was built to expose.

(2) A POSTERIOR MEAN OF 0.50 IS THE PRIOR, NOT A VERDICT. Several apparent losers sit at exactly 0.50 with alpha+beta at or near 2.0 - e.g. capability-census-tick-1784803268608 has 265 selections but total_executions = 1. Against a winner at 0.92 the margin reads 0.42, but the loser simply has no graded outcomes. Retiring on that punishes an arm for LACKING evidence and permanently entrenches whichever variant happened to be graded first. Any deprecation gate must require alpha+beta to exceed the prior on BOTH sides; margin alone is not sufficient.

THE STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION: the arm population is simultaneously too large for the evidence available AND too poorly evidenced to prune. 49,074 selections spread over 4,089 arms is ~12 samples per arm across the substrate's entire history, against the ~100 needed to separate two arms at a 10% difference. Evidence-based retirement cannot fix an evidence shortage, because it consumes the same scarce resource it is trying to conserve. This is the same defect as 'the learning does not compound', observed from the other side.

WHAT ACTUALLY FOLLOWS - reduce the INFLOW, not the stock:
(a) Gate MINTING on law 3 (reuse before mint): refuse to create a new variant when an existing producer of the same output shape is available. This needs no per-arm evidence to justify and is the only lever that does not consume evidence.
(b) Retire on STRUCTURAL criteria that do not require posterior evidence - e.g. a one-shot gap-closing activity whose originating gap is closed has served its purpose and can be retired on provenance rather than performance. 62% of arms carry a timestamped, single-use id; that is a structural property, not a judgement about quality.
(c) Only then consider posterior-based retirement, once arms accumulate enough samples for the posterior to mean anything.

DO NOT read this as 'retirement is broken'. It works where evidence exists: 78 of 93 candidates under the documented gate are ALREADY retired, and activity.retired is true on 1,217 of 3,886 rows.

FALSIFIER: raise real evidence per arm (by any means) and re-run this analysis. If the defensible cull set grows substantially above 2 while the arm population is unchanged, then the blocker was the evidence shortage exactly as claimed. If it stays near 2, the gate itself is mis-specified and should be re-derived.

Capability gap: the goal-walk needs a producer for shape "diagnosis" but no live resolver or activity produces it. AUTHOR a resolver that produces ONLY the shape "diagnosis" — do NOT expand scope, produce no other output shape. Put it in the vessel that should own this capability (if development-vessel: add the resolver in src/resolvers/, register the shape in src/config.ts AND the dispatch case in src/routes/impulses.ts per the three-place rule; otherwise the owning vessel's resolver surface). Keep it dependency-free (Bun built-ins) and make it typecheck.

The 6 cluster into exactly two migrations, each missing ALL of its own fields: 055-variant-tracking (retired_at, retired_reason, variant_reason) and 048-goal-execution-alignment (input_schema, output_schema, schema_confidence).

Both are recorded in the real ledger `init_migrations` (218 rows) at 2026-06-28T07:59:20.240Z and .244Z, inside a single second that contains 37 rows. A genuine apply of 37 migrations cannot finish in <1s; init-database.ts's own comment states 048's aggregation alone takes ~4s and that 023/048 'both timed out here ... the file is skipped wholesale and its views silently never exist'. init-database.ts contains an explicit bootstrap path that pre-populates init_migrations with every filename and returns true so the caller SKIPS all migrations that run. Because IF NOT EXISTS makes both files safe to re-run, they would succeed - but never will, since the ledger says applied.

CONSEQUENCE: any code writing a field that was never declared gets success:true and HTTP 200 while SurrealDB discards the value. Confirmed end-to-end: commit cc81c2d correctly writes `retired_at = time::now(), retired_reason = 'deprecate_impulse'` in the deprecate UPDATE; a deprecate re-run at 09:37:31 on a binary verified to contain that literal moved `updated_at` to 09:37:31 and left both fields null. So cc81c2d is INERT IN PRODUCTION despite being correct in source, typechecked, deployed, and passing its own 4/4 structural test.

COMPOUNDING: the unit line is `ExecStartPre=-/root/.bun/bin/bun /vessels/activity-api/scripts/init-database.ts` - the leading `-` discards the exit status, so a failed migration run still starts a vessel reporting healthy. Also, the table named `migrations` has 2 rows and no filename column, so it cannot answer 'which migrations applied'.

summary: THE NO-TRACE PLACEHOLDER EXECUTION ID IS DERIVED FROM GOAL TEXT, SO INDEPENDENT RUNS COLLIDE AND BECOME INDISTINGUISHABLE. MEASURED 2026-09-05. Two separate dispatches of byte-identical goal text — 7f95fc62-aa2a-41a2-9cda-53035b95ecd5 and 5ecc06f1-0eaa-47b1-8950-9dac4d7257ec — each ran independently (distinct dispatchIds, neither carrying a coalesced flag) and each reported the SAME executionId: goal-seek:no-trace:996addc0. When a goal-seek yields no trace the placeholder id appears to be minted from the goal text, so every run of that text collides on one identifier. WHY THIS MATTERS: an executionId is the join key between a dispatch and what it did. When two runs share one, the trace view cannot distinguish them — you cannot tell whether a goal ran once or five times, nor which attempt produced which outcome. It also actively misleads: I inferred from the repeated id that a retry had been coalesced onto an earlier failure, filed that as a defect, and was wrong. The collision is a correctness problem for auditing, and it manufactured a false finding in a session whose whole purpose was auditing. This compounds the already-filed observation that direct resolver invocation is entirely untraced: goals that produce no trace get an id that is not unique, so the thin end of the tracing story is thinner than a count of executions suggests. FALSIFIER: closed only when two independent dispatches of identical goal text that both fail without a trace are shown to carry DISTINCT executionIds — cite both dispatch ids and both execution ids. A closure that only shows a traced goal producing a unique id is fabricated, because the defect is specific to the no-trace placeholder path.
remedy: EXACT FIX SITE LOCATED — one line, not dispatched because host load was 29.4 and I have held at that threshold all session. repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts line 15227 reads: record.executionId = seek.executionId ?? seek.result?.trace?.id ?? `goal-seek:no-trace:${goalHashOf(String(goal ?? ""))}`; The placeholder is derived PURELY from goal text via goalHashOf, which is deterministic by design, so every independent run of identical text mints the identical id. That confirms the mechanism by reading the mint rather than inferring it from two colliding records. THE MINIMAL CHANGE: append the dispatch identifier to the placeholder — the goal hash still groups runs of the same goal, while the dispatch id makes each run distinguishable. record.dispatchId is in scope at that line (the surrounding statements assign record.walkLog, record.selectedTemplateId and record.attempts). Note the goal hash must be KEPT: flushRouterFeedback four lines above keys router posteriors on goalHashOf of the same text, so the hash is load-bearing for learning and only the uniqueness suffix is being added. WHY IT MATTERS, restated with the evidence now in hand: this collision caused me to file a false gap this session — I saw one execution id on two dispatch records, concluded a retry had been coalesced onto an earlier failure, and was wrong. The dispatch records show distinct dispatchIds and no coalesced flag. An identifier that is not unique is not an identifier, and here it actively manufactured a wrong finding in an audit. FALSIFIER unchanged: two independent dispatches of identical goal text that both fail without a trace must carry DISTINCT executionIds.

summary: COMPOSE IS A SINGLE LANE AGAINST A GROWING POOL — A CAPACITY CONSTRAINT, NOT A LOSS. MEASURED 2026-09-05 over the most recent 20,000 gap-drain events: 326 distinct gap ids appear, 570 events are a dispatch or a successful compose nudge, and the picker reports a pool of 236 gaps with 59 excluded as hopeless. Individual gaps recur 1,115 to 1,117 times in that window, so nothing is being discarded — the same items are re-offered continuously and the picker selects the highest-scoring one each time. THE REAL CONSTRAINT: feature_compose refuses a DIRECTED compose at 2 in flight and an AUTONOMOUS one at 1, so effectively one authoring attempt proceeds at a time. Against a pool of this size that sets a hard ceiling on how fast filed work can be attempted, independent of how good the authoring is. Measured in this session from the operator side: eleven directed dispatches produced two correct landings, several correct refusals, and repeated BUSY responses — and the system's own message for BUSY is explicit that it is 'a transient capacity condition, not a capability gap'. WHY THIS IS WORTH TRACKING SEPARATELY from authoring quality: a reachability gate, better goals, or a stronger drafter all raise the value per attempt, but none raises the number of attempts. If the intent is for the substrate to work a backlog of this size autonomously, concurrency is the lever, and it is currently one. FALSIFIER: closed only when the effective concurrent-compose limit is raised and the change is demonstrated — cite the new limit and a drain-log window showing two composes proceeding simultaneously — or a measurement is cited showing per-gap latency falling with the limit unchanged. A closure citing skip-rate percentages is fabricated, because skips are backpressure and not loss.

THE DRAFTER EMITS NO-OP EDITS ON ABOUT A THIRD OF WALK EDIT ATTEMPTS. summary: THE ONE TEST COVERING normalizeGoal EXERCISES A COPY, AND ITS DRIFT-DETECTOR DOES NOT DETECT DRIFT. MEASURED 2026-09-05. repos/activity-api/src/routes/__tests__/goal-class-hash.test.ts defines its OWN normalizeGoal at line 25 — its header says 'Mirror of normalizeGoal in ../goal-paths.ts. It is module-private there' — and every behavioural assertion in the file runs against that mirror, never against the shipped function. THE MIRROR HAS ALREADY DRIFTED: the deployed function now contains FIVE replace calls, having gained .replace(/^\[[^\]]*\]\s*/, '') from commit e340ad3; the mirror contains FOUR. THE FILE CLAIMS THIS CANNOT HAPPEN. Its comment states the source assertions at the bottom 'keep the mirror honest, so a drift in the route shows up as a failure here rather than as silently passing behavioural tests'. That claim is false. Those assertions check exactly two invariants of the SOURCE TEXT — that the hex elision appears before the punctuation strip, and that the string /\d/.test(m) is present — and neither compares the mirror to the source. VERIFIED BY EXECUTING BOTH ASSERTIONS against the deployed file: assertion one passes (index 2226 < 2335), assertion two passes, while the mirror is stale. Drift is not detected. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TEST: this is the concrete mechanism behind two inert commits landing FAVORABLE earlier in this session. 3a92282 and b9fc69d each changed the real normalizeGoal into something that matched nothing, and the bun test gate passed both — not because tests were absent, but because the test that appears to cover this function was asserting against its own private copy. A test that mirrors its subject can never fail for a change to the subject. THE PATTERN IS GENERAL: a mirror test is evidence about the mirror, not about the code that ships. It is the testing form of the evidence-aliasing class already recorded for this substrate — the check is real, the thing it checks is not the thing in production. FALSIFIER: closed only when a change to normalizeGoal in goal-paths.ts that alters its observable behaviour causes goal-class-hash.test.ts to FAIL — cite the change and the failing assertion — or the mirror is replaced by an import of the real function (which requires exporting it). A closure that only adds more assertions against the mirror is fabricated, because the mirror is the defect.
remedy: CLOSED — FALSIFIER DEMONSTRATED EXACTLY AS WRITTEN. The falsifier required that a change to normalizeGoal in goal-paths.ts which alters its observable behaviour must cause goal-class-hash.test.ts to FAIL, citing the change and the failing assertion. Both are cited below. THE FIX: commit 12b8960 on activity-api origin/dev. Two parts. First, the mirror was synced to the shipped function — it had FOUR .replace() calls against the source's FIVE, having never gained the leading-bracket strip that e340ad3 added. Second, a structural assertion was added that extracts the .replace() chain from BOTH the test file and goal-paths.ts and compares them, so the mirror is honest in fact rather than by assertion. Tests are explicitly not edit-gated, so this was an operator edit rather than a compose dispatch. DEMONSTRATION, with the source deliberately drifted and then reverted: injecting a sixth transform (.replace(/\bfoo\b/g, 'bar')) into goal-paths.ts took the suite from 10 pass / 0 fail to 9 pass / 1 FAIL. The failing assertion is 'goal-paths route wiring > mirror matches the shipped normalizeGoal transform-for-transform' at goal-class-hash.test.ts:127, and its diff names the specific missing transform. Reverting the source restored 10 pass / 0 fail, and git diff on goal-paths.ts is empty, so nothing was left modified. WHAT THIS EXPLAINS, and why it was worth chasing: this is the mechanism behind two inert commits to normalizeGoal — 3a92282 which doubled the regex backslashes and b9fc69d which stripped them — each landing with verdict FAVORABLE and a green bun test gate. Tests were not absent. The test that appears to cover this function was asserting against its own private copy, so it could not fail for a change to the shipped code. A test that mirrors its subject is evidence about the mirror. RESIDUE, deliberately not claimed as fixed: the mirror still EXISTS, because normalizeGoal is module-private. The correct fix is to export it and import it here, which is a change to gated vessel source. This closure makes drift detectable; it does not remove the duplication. The behavioural tests above the assertion still run against the copy — they are now guaranteed to be running against a copy that matches, which is a weaker guarantee than running against the real function.

The semantic gate READS the diff and the diff plausibly matches the described intent — the correct call really was added. summary:
A NATURAL EXPERIMENT IN THE LIVE STORE: THE SAME PIPELINE CLOSES 87% BY VERIFIED REPAIR WHEN THE GAP CARRIES A PREDICATE AND 2% WHEN IT DOES NOT. THE WRITER ALREADY HOLDS THE MISSING FIELD.

THE MEASUREMENT. Splitting all 399 route-edit gaps by whether they carry a Class-1 predicate (a hardcoded_url literal AND an edit_site/file_path):
  WITH predicate  n=15 : 93% closed · 87% closed as VERIFIED REPAIR · 0 timer expiries · 0 still open
  WITHOUT         n=384: 40% closed ·  2% closed as verified repair · 117 timer expiries · 194 still open
That is a 43-fold difference in verified-repair rate across the same population, same pipeline, same kind of work — edit requests against named files.

CONFOUND CHECKED AND ABSENT. The obvious objection is that the 15 were gaps an operator was hand-working. They were not: 14 of the 15 are source=substrate_detected, the same composition as the comparison group (375 of 384 substrate_detected). Nor were they backfilled by a retry path: 0 of the 15 carry the re_commit flag, versus 4 of the 384. The predicate is the variable that differs. HONEST LIMIT: n=15 is small, so treat 87% as directional rather than precise; the qualitative gap (0 timer expiries and 0 still-open on one side, 117 and 194 on the other) is the robust part.

THE CAUSE, LOCATED. goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts:12277 builds the gap that every edit-intent dispatch files:
    gap: { id: gapId, summary: goal.replace(...), category: "edit_intent_route", classification_metadata: { edit_site: editSite } }
It sets edit_site and STOPS. A Class-1 predicate requires BOTH a literal and a file (substrate-gap.ts:428-438: a hardcoded_url without an edit_site is stamped 'unresolvable' precisely because verifyGapCondition never enters the Class-1 branch). So every route-edit gap is born falsifier=none and is structurally unclosable — while the file it names sits right there in the same object literal.

THE MATERIAL IS IN SCOPE AND NEED NOT BE GUESSED. Twenty lines above, the same function computes `const spec = specBase + await verbatimExcerptBlock(editFile, editLine, goal);`. The writer therefore holds editFile, editLine, and a VERBATIM EXCERPT of the target line. This matters because substrate-gap.ts:306 states the resolver 'never derives, guesses, or synthesises a predicate from the summary — that was tried'. This proposal does not do that: it passes through a verbatim excerpt the writer already read off disk, at the writer, not the reader.

CURRENT COVERAGE: of the 194 OPEN route-edit gaps, ZERO carry a Class-1 predicate. Every one of them is on the 2% path.

DESIGN CAVEAT THAT MUST BE SETTLED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING — this is why the gap is filed rather than fixed. A Class-1 predicate asserts 'this literal must go ABSENT'. That is correct for an edit that REPLACES or REMOVES the excerpted line, and WRONG for an edit that only ADDS code near it, where the excerpt legitimately survives and the gap would never close. The failure mode is no worse than today (the gap stays open either way), but it would mis-stamp such gaps as class1 and make the falsifier census dishonest. The safe form is to attach the predicate only when the intent is a replace/remove, or to record the excerpt under a position that verifyGapCondition treats as must-change rather than must-vanish. Because this decides closure semantics, it is a policy call for the operator, not an autonomous edit.

FALSIFIER: after the change, the Class-1 share of NEWLY created route-edit gaps rises from 0% and their verified-repair rate approaches the 87% observed in the existing 15, while timer expiries in that category fall from 117.

A FAILED WALK'S SIDE EFFECTS SURVIVE ITS OWN NEGATIVE VERDICT. Multiple confirmed instances, via at least two different walk paths, one of which destroyed this very record. Durable copy: operator memory note reference-a-failed-walks-writes-survive-its-own-verdict-2026-09-05.

THE MECHANISM. A closing goal is auto-generated as 'Close substrate gap <id>: <summary, truncated>'. The walk satisfies it by PRODUCING the substrateGap_write shape, and producing that shape means writing the gap with status=closed — using the goal's own text as the new summary. The walk then grades itself reached=FALSE. THE JUDGE IS CORRECT; the write is simply never rolled back. TRANSACTION FAILURE, NOT JUDGE FAILURE. Because the target shape IS substrateGap_write, writing 'closed' is indistinguishable from succeeding — circular by construction.

EVIDENCE. Instance 1, 11:04:56, gap gap-store-accepts-uninterpolated-template-placeholders-as-a-real-gap: ~3300 chars → 123, path [satisfier:substrateGap, satisfier:substrateGap_write], reached=false, goal_hash de788e7fb6907fa3; its falsifier read 1 before and 1 after — nothing was fixed. Instance 2, 11:55:10, THIS record: ~4519 chars → 62, path [activity:learned-composition-executiontracelist-to-failure-mode-summary], reached=false, goal_hash 3e02221e20085b0d; the only surviving text was this gap's own headline sentence. Further collapses followed on both records and on expired-not-redetected-asserts-a-detector-ran-but-no-detector-run-is-ever-recorded (4781 → 11, 'STILL OPEN.').

NOT SATISFIER-SPECIFIC. The two instances used different mechanisms (a bare satisfier; a learned composition activity) and rewrote `source` to different values — observed across incidents: substrate, autonomous-agent, substrate_detected, hardcoded-gap, manual. That field identifies nothing and must not be treated as naming the culprit. Any remedy scoped to the bare satisfier is TOO NARROW.

PRECEDENT. goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts carries SATISFIER_FORBIDDEN_FS_WRITE = {fileEditResult, fileWriteResult, fs_edit, fs_write} under 'THE BARE SATISFIER MUST NOT MUTATE LIVE VESSEL SOURCE', whose comment describes this incident with one noun changed — 'it performs the write, with no snapshot, no verification and no rollback ... a walk that ends HOLLOW strands whatever it wrote' — concluding 'THE CORRUPTION OUTLIVED THE WALK THAT MADE IT' (2026-08-07, filesystem). A STORE write is outside that set.

A REMEDY THAT MUST NOT BE IMPLEMENTED. Do NOT simply add substrateGap_write to that Set. (1) Of 141 executions on paths containing satisfier:substrateGap_write, 21 SUCCEEDED — legitimate gap writes that would be destroyed. (2) The fs guard's rationale inverts here: it is 'pure downside' removal only because 'a satisfier write can corrupt the tree but can NEVER produce a reach', which is exactly what fails in this case. (3) A shape-level guard cannot be narrowed, because at that point the walk knows the SHAPE, not the payload. (4) It would not have stopped instance 2, which was not a satisfier. CORRECT FIX (architectural, operator decision): defer any walk-performed durable store write until after the reach verdict, or snapshot the prior gap state and restore it on reached=false, mirroring what feature_compose and patch_with_tools already do for files.

SCOPE. goal_execution_paths: 9700 rows, of which 4205 (43% of every learned path) are 'Close substrate gap' goals; 86 use a satisfier:substrateGap_write path, aggregating 21 success / 120 failed / 141 total (85% failure). LIMIT: 120 is failed executions on ONE implicated path shape, not confirmed fabrications, and instance 2 shows other paths also do this, so 120 does not bound the phenomenon either.

PARTIAL MITIGATION LANDED 2026-09-05, commit 3f440bd (substrate-authored, pushed, 0 unpushed): substrate-gap.ts now refuses an incoming summary that is a case-insensitive leading fragment of the stored one. VERIFIED BEHAVIOURALLY, not by verdict — probe gap baseline 429 chars; leading-fragment write left it at 429 (preserved); a genuinely different shorter summary replaced it at 59 (no false positive). This does NOT stop false closures; it stops them from destroying the evidence that would expose them, which is the precondition for measuring this gap at all. Note the dispatch that landed it reported failed/reached=false while the change was correct, deployed and pushed — an inverse verdict, the same class filed as reach-verdict-inverted-on-the-effect-of-a-diff.

FALSIFIER: no gap may transition to closed by a walk that graded reached=false. Re-run by dispatching a closing goal for a gap whose defect is still present and asserting the status is unchanged.

summary:
THE GUARD THAT EXISTS TO STOP A WRITE FROM BLANKING A GAP'S PROBLEM STATEMENT IS ONE COMPARISON SHORT, AND THAT SHORTFALL DESTROYED THREE OPERATOR GAPS TODAY.

THE GUARD. development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts:795 (and again, harmlessly duplicated, at :803):
    if (typeof gap.summary !== "string" || gap.summary.length === 0) gap.summary = existing.summary;
Its own comment states the intent exactly: 'Prevent a close or re-emit that carries no summary from blanking the stored problem statement.' The resolver ALREADY loads the prior record as `existing` and already uses it to preserve created_at, remedy, and the learned failed_attempts counters. The prior state is in hand.

THE SHORTFALL. The condition fires only when the incoming summary is absent, empty, or not a string. It does nothing when the incoming summary is NON-EMPTY BUT COLLAPSED. Every destruction observed today passed a non-empty string and sailed through:
  4781 chars → 11   ('STILL OPEN.')                                             99.8% loss
  4519 chars → 62   ('A FAILED WALK'S SIDE EFFECTS SURVIVE ITS OWN NEGATIVE VERDICT.')  98.6% loss
  3300 chars → 123  ('The gap store accepted a write in which every field was an unrendered template placeholder, and created a real gap from it.')  96.3% loss

THE SIGNATURE IS PRECISE, WHICH MAKES A SAFE RULE POSSIBLE. In all three cases the replacement was a CASE-INSENSITIVE LEADING FRAGMENT of the summary it replaced — not a paraphrase, not a summarisation. That is because the auto-generated closing/edit goal is 'Close substrate gap <id>: <summary, truncated>', and the writer echoes that goal text back as the new summary. So the destroyed content and its replacement stand in a strict prefix relation. A rule of the form 'if the incoming summary is a case-insensitive leading fragment of the existing one, keep the existing' catches all three with a very low false-positive surface — a genuine human or drafter rewrite is essentially never a strict prefix of what it replaces. A blunter length-ratio rule would also work (all three lost >95%) but is cruder and would fire on legitimate deliberate shortening.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE AVAILABLE FIX. Every measurement and falsifier the substrate records about itself lives in this field, because the remedy field is not returned by the substrateGap read projection (see gap-remedy-accepted-on-write-but-never-returned-on-read). The store REPLACES rather than merges, so a collapsing write erases exactly the material by which a false closure could be detected — self-concealing by construction. Fixing this does NOT stop gaps being falsely closed (see autonomous-closure-paraphrases-a-gap-and-closes-it-without-fixing-anything), but it makes every such closure AUDITABLE AFTER THE FACT, which is the precondition for measuring the larger defect at all.

AND IT NEEDS NO COUPLING TO THE WALK. This is the key feasibility finding. The correct fix for the closure defect requires binding a walk's durable writes to its own reach verdict, which is architectural and cross-vessel. This one does not: the resolver is a TRUE CHOKEPOINT — every substrateGap_write passes through it regardless of which walk path called it, and the three observed destructions came through at least two different paths (a bare satisfier and a learned composition activity). A guard here covers all of them, with no verdict plumbing.

SAME CLASS AS THE DAY'S RECURRING PATTERN: a guard that is correct in intent, has the information it needs already loaded, and stops one step short of the case that actually occurs — cf. SATISFIER_FORBIDDEN_FS_WRITE covering filesystem writes but not store writes, and the oracle-label fix applied to the execution id but not the label id one line above.

FALSIFIER: after the change, re-run the three observed collapses as writes against a test gap and assert the stored summary is unchanged; and assert that a normal operator rewrite (not a prefix of the prior text) still replaces the summary as before. Currently the first assertion fails for all three.

summary:
MEASURED by the declaration-drift scan added to schema-assert-drift-scan (commit 8636190), run against the live store and the real migration tree.

Over 217 .surql files, 1,595 DEFINE FIELD declarations, 97 live tables (59 SCHEMAFULL), exactly two declared fields are absent from the live schema:

  execution_traces.org_id     declared in 068-complete-permissions-coverage.surql
  execution_traces.ci_status  declared in 005-ci-integration.surql

Verified by hand: INFO FOR TABLE execution_traces reports 12 fields (account_id, account_id_version, cost_usd, created_at, duration_ms, execution_id, execution_trace, session_context, status, stored_at, template_id, updated_at) and neither flagged field is among them. The table is SCHEMAFULL, so a write to either would be DISCARDED silently — the same mechanism that made cc81c2d inert this morning.

SEVERITY CORRECTED DOWN, P2 -> P3. execution_traces has ZERO ROWS. Nothing writes to it, so no data has been lost and nothing is currently broken. My first draft of this gap claimed tenant-scoping rows might not carry org_id; that was inference and it is not supported — there are no rows. This is LATENT drift of the same class as org_id ON impulse_resolution_metrics (migration 070), which is likewise harmless only while its table is empty. Note the separate, populated activity_execution_traces table (~18k rows) is a DIFFERENT table and is not affected.

The value here is mostly that it demonstrates the detector finds real declared-vs-live divergence: 0 confirmed write-blocking hazards exist anywhere in the store today, and these 2 are the only declaration gaps on any SCHEMAFULL table.

summary:
NARROWED 2026-09-05 — MY ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS TOO STRONG AND IS CORRECTED BELOW. The residual defect is real but smaller than filed.

THE RESIDUAL, TRUE CLAIM. The compose TRACE records `semantic_reason` (400 chars) for a semantic rejection but carries no equivalent for an apply failure — only `apply_failed: true` and `ops_applied: <count>` (development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, trace metadata around lines 6185-6200). So a query over traces can say THAT an apply failed but not WHY, and apply-failure classes cannot be aggregated on the trace surface the learning loop reads. The reason exists at that point: the per-op result type at feature-compose.ts:4525 is `{ path, kind, ok, repaired?, detail?, span? }`, and the full array WITH detail is written to the compose report at line 6139 under PROPOSALS_DIR (default /workspace/proposals).

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I originally wrote that the detail is 'recoverable only by knowing the gap id and reading a file inside the container, which no automated consumer does'. THAT IS FALSE. An automated consumer does read it. My failed dispatch produced the gap `recommit-route-edit-f06d9ed8-anchor_not_found`, whose summary reads: 'compose for gap route-edit-f06d9ed8 repeated already-recorded failure class anchor_not_found: {"error":"no_unique_anchor: refused fs_edit — planned anchor is non-unique and re-derivation found no unique substring (would mislocalize to first occurrence)"}'. So the reason is captured verbatim AND assigned a named failure class (anchor_not_found), AND recognised as REPEATED — the recommit path is tracking recurrence of apply-failure classes. The gap's classification_metadata also carries a failure_lessons array with {at, class, reason, raw_excerpt}. The system is doing more of this than I credited.

SO THE DEFECT IS NARROWER: attribution exists in the GAP store and is class-labelled there; it is absent from the TRACE. That still matters, because the trace is the aggregatable surface the learning loop and audits read, and because only gaps that go through the recommit path get the treatment — an apply failure on a dispatch with no gap lineage leaves nothing. But 'apply failures are unattributed' as a blanket statement is wrong.

THE UNDERLYING BEHAVIOUR WAS CORRECT. The applier detected that the planned anchor was ambiguous, refused rather than mislocalizing to the first occurrence, and rolled back cleanly (ops_applied 0, rolled_back true, no partial state). That is the anchor-relocation failure mode being PREVENTED. The fault in that dispatch was mine: I quoted a NON-UNIQUE line as context in the goal and the drafter anchored on it. Rule learned and worth keeping: never quote a non-unique line in a goal, even as context; anchor by replacing a line unique by construction, and name the line that must NOT be used.

FALSIFIER (unchanged in form): query traces for template_id=feature_compose with metadata.apply_failed=true and group by failure reason. That grouping is impossible today. After a fix every apply_failed trace must carry a non-empty reason and the grouped count must equal the count of apply_failed traces. NOTE when re-checking: the gap store already answers this question for the subset with recommit lineage, so a fix here is about the trace surface and about coverage of dispatches without a gap, not about creating the information.

summary:
THE ESCALATION PATH ROUTES AROUND THE SYSTEM'S OWN INERT-CHANGE REFUSAL. A change feature_compose would reject as having zero behaviour delta lands anyway, because escalation is triggered BY feature_compose's refusal and the lane it escalates to never runs that gate.

THE GATE EXISTS AND IS GOOD. development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts:758 exports detectZeroBehaviorDelta(diff), which flags an added diff whose executable content is inert. Its first branch is exactly the case below: strip comments and strings from the ADDED lines, and if nothing survives while nothing real was REMOVED, return isInert:true with reason 'added lines are comment/whitespace-only - zero behaviour delta'. It is deliberately conservative (any behaviour token anywhere clears it) and its docstring records why each precondition is safe.

IT HAS EXACTLY ONE CALL SITE. grep across development-vessel/src for detectZeroBehaviorDelta( returns a single caller: feature-compose.ts:1999. patch_with_tools calls it ZERO times, along with every other inert check.

SO THE REFUSAL IS ROUTED AROUND. goal-host-vessel escalates to patch_with_tools precisely WHEN feature_compose returns UNFAVORABLE ('EDIT-INTENT ESCALATION - feature_compose verdict=UNFAVORABLE ...; escalating to patch_with_tools'). The escalation target has no semantic judge AND no inert gate. So the pipeline's response to 'this change is inert' can be to land it through a lane that does not ask.

DEMONSTRATED TODAY, NOT INFERRED. Commit a336a75 (development-vessel, 2026-09-05, substrate-authored via mitosis cutover) landed 12 insertions and 0 deletions, and every inserted line is a comment - I read the diff. detectZeroBehaviorDelta on that diff returns isInert:true by its first branch (added code strips to empty, removedCode empty). The dispatch that produced it graded status=completed, reached=TRUE, executionId=patch_with_tools:a336a758. The functional code it was supposed to add had already landed in the prior commit ecc7db5, so a336a75 changed nothing executable. An inert change landed green, through the lane that skips the gate built to catch inert changes.

WHY THIS IS MORE SERIOUS THAN THE ADJACENT FINDINGS. Elsewhere in this system correct judgement is merely UNRECORDED - the land-sweep withholds credit honestly, the applier refuses an ambiguous anchor, the semantic gate rejects a patch on sound reasoning. Those are silent but correct. This is different in kind: the judgement is made, is correct, and is then OVERRIDDEN by the routing. Measured scope: bare 'mitosis-<timestamp>' commits (the patch_with_tools shape) over 30 days are 48 of 192 in development-vessel, 11 of 115 in goal-host-vessel and 29 of 55 in activity-api - 88 of 362, roughly 24% of all autonomous landings, none of which passed the inert gate.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH AN EXISTING FIX. goal-host-vessel already refuses to escalate when feature_compose returns BUSY, reasoning 'So load - not drafting quality - decided whether a change got judged' and choosing to leave the gap open instead. That fix protects the case where NO judgement happened. The case where a judgement DID happen and was NEGATIVE still escalates. The stronger signal is the one that gets overridden.

THE FIX IS SMALL AND REUSES WHAT EXISTS. detectZeroBehaviorDelta is already exported from feature-compose.ts. Call it in patch_with_tools on the staged diff before landing, and refuse the same way feature_compose does. No new judgement needs inventing; the audit trail in production is 14 composes / 2 refusals / 0 false positives for the related inert-literal gate, so the family is proven conservative.

FALSIFIER: construct an edit goal whose only effect is to add comment lines to an existing file, drive it through the escalation lane, and assert it is REFUSED rather than landed. Today it lands and grades reached=true - commit a336a75 is the worked example.

summary: CONTROL PROBE — CLOSED, purpose served. Written to test whether substrateGap_write could still create a row. Result: the identical write at 23:05Z returned action:skipped and wrote nothing (the :754 env-gate outage); the re-run at 23:24Z returned action:created and the row was confirmed present in gaps.json, with the store count moving 2376 -> 2378. This row is the positive half of that before/after pair and is retained only as evidence of it. Safe to delete.

DEFECT: the 'investigate and decompose gap <id>' path does not decompose. It re-emits the parent gap's own body as a new gap, truncated to 400 characters, under a fresh route-edit id.

MEASURED 2026-09-05 on the live gap store: of 50 gaps whose summary begins 'investigate and decompose gap <id>:', all 50 have a resolvable parent. After recursively stripping the decompose prefix from BOTH child and parent (the parent's summary can itself carry one), 33 of 50 (66 percent) have an inner body that is prefix-identical to the parent's inner body, and 5 are byte-identical. The echoed bodies cluster at exactly 399-400 characters, which is the truncation point. CONTROL: the remaining 17 carry materially different text, so the path CAN produce new content and 66 percent is not a classifier artifact. 66 percent is a FLOOR, because parent summaries are themselves overwritten by closure prose over time, so a child that echoed the ORIGINAL parent text now scores as novel.

CONSEQUENCE 1: the attempt counter is laundered. A seal at 8 attempts with 0 lands never fires, because each echo starts a NEW gap id with failed_attempts reset to zero. One observed chain burned 14 attempts across 4 ids, each capped at 4, and was never sealed.

CONSEQUENCE 2: the recorded failure lesson can never reach what causes the failure. Failure lessons ARE recorded and ARE injected into the drafter prompt, but the lesson names a defect that lives in the GOAL TEXT, and the echo copies that goal text forward verbatim. One observed chain records the lesson 'dead-code-only patch: every changed symbol has zero callers and is not an entrypoint, the change cannot execute' while carrying forward the parent instruction telling it not to wire the symbol in. The lesson and the instruction contradict, and the instruction wins on every retry. A learning channel that can only append to a prompt cannot repair a defect that lives in the prompt.

THE REMEDY, single file, single change site: in the gap-write resolver named in edit_site, inside resolveSubstrateGapWrite, refuse to CREATE a decompose-child whose inner body is a prefix of its parent's inner body. The comparison is cheap and needs no new data: that function already loads the existing gap set in order to dedup by class, so the parent row is in hand at the moment of the write. A child that adds no text cannot by construction be a decomposition. This is the same chokepoint and the same shape as the summary-collapse guard already living in that file.

DO NOT retarget this gap at any other vessel. An earlier attempt was localized to a configuration file in a different vessel because this summary previously quoted that path as evidence; every repair attempt against that target failed, first on a type error and then on a correct semantic refusal. The change site is the gap-write resolver and nothing else.
