PRE-REGISTERED COMPOUNDING SCORECARD, with directional predictions fixed before the data, so the loop's own dynamics can falsify them rather than be fitted.

WHY A SCORECARD RATHER THAN A CLAIM. Compounding is not a single event; it is a regime in which evidence accumulates on reused structure faster than uninformed structure is minted. It cannot be asserted from one posterior nudge. It has to be watched as several counters over time, each with a direction that only honest learning would produce.

THE T0 SNAPSHOT, taken 2026-09-06 13:49. The compose arm sits at alpha 53.65, beta 19.22, an implied rate of 73.6 percent. Its real execution rows show six reached-true and twenty four reached-false among the identifier-keyed rows that instrumentation now grades. Across the fleet, one thousand one hundred eighty nine of one thousand five hundred thirty six arms have exactly one execution, seventy seven percent. Fleet-wide grading coverage is twenty one point one percent.

THE FOUR PREDICTIONS, each with its own falsifier.

One, convergence. If grading is honest, the compose implied rate must fall from 73.6 toward the counter-derived low teens, and crucially beta must rise faster than alpha. The concern already visible: between 06:43 and 13:49 today alpha and beta each rose by about one and a half, in lock step, and the implied rate moved only one point. If alpha continues to track beta one-for-one while reached-false rows accumulate, the posterior is being inflated by chain credit as fast as honest negatives arrive, and it will never converge. That equal-movement is the single most likely falsifier of compounding and must be watched directly.

Two, budget. The one-execution arm fraction must fall. It is the graveyard signature: seventy seven percent means minting is spending the grading budget on arms that never get a second observation. If it holds or rises, structure is outrunning evidence and nothing can compound regardless of how good the grading becomes.

Three, coverage. Fleet grading must rise above twenty one percent as the instrumented lanes carry more traffic and the auditors surface more silent ones. If it holds flat, the censored majority is still censored and every rate computed over the fleet remains a rate over a biased sample.

Four, autonomy. The six conservation auditors, currently at one execution each, must be re-selected and re-run without an operator dispatching them, and their violation counts must move as the underlying defects are repaired or worsen. If they are executed only when hand-dispatched, they are operator meters wearing activity clothes, not loop citizens.

WHAT WOULD CONSTITUTE PROOF. Not one counter moving, but the joint motion: implied rate down with beta outpacing alpha, one-execution fraction down, coverage up, auditors self-selecting with responsive violation counts. Any one of these reversing is informative. The point of fixing them now is that the system's behaviour over the coming days decides the verdict, not a story told after the fact.

FALSIFIER FOR THE SCORECARD ITSELF. If alpha and beta move in lock step over a multi-day window while reached-false rows keep landing, compounding is not occurring on the primary arm and the chain-credit inflation must be repaired before any grading fix can matter.

OUTCOME RECORDED 2026-09-07, after the fixes landed. The predictions in this gap now have verdicts and are written back so the store records confirmations as well as failures.

PREDICTION ONE, PRIMARY SIGNAL: PASSED. The reach graded stamp count rose from seven to ten. Each new stamp corresponded to exactly one beta unit.

PREDICTION TWO, BETA RISES: PASSED. Beta moved from nineteen point four eight to twenty three point four eight, an increase of four, while alpha held completely flat at fifty four point three nine. The implied success rate fell from seventy three point six percent to sixty nine point eight percent, the first movement toward the counter derived rate of about twelve percent in twelve hours.

PREDICTION THREE, CREDIT ASYMMETRY: ARMED AND UNFIRED. The concern was that alpha per positive verdict might run about three times beta per negative verdict and stall convergence. Across five successive beta increments alpha did not move at all, so the asymmetry did not materialise on this sample. The check remains armed for the next twenty verdicts and must not be acted on until it fires; touching the delta weighting on an unfired hypothesis would corrupt the evidence just made honest.

THE SPLIT WAS LOAD BEARING. The original conjunctive form of this falsifier, requiring stamps to rise and stranded rows to fall together, would have reported failure four separate times while the fix worked, because stamps rise with new traffic whereas stranded rows only drain if something revisits old executions and nothing does. Splitting the criterion by denominator is what made the confirmation readable.

DELIVERY COVERAGE, MEASURED ON THE CORRECT DENOMINATOR. Restricted to compose rows created after the delivery fix loaded, twenty nine percent now carry a reach tag against a historical baseline of four and a half percent. The aggregate across all rows remains near ninety five percent untagged because eleven hundred historical rows dominate it; reading the aggregate would hide the working fix, which is the same denominator error that let telemetry rows inflate grading coverage by a factor of two point three.

The report-to-gap bridge is the one missing link that keeps the conservation auditors from closing the detect-to-demand loop on their own, and its absence is now measured: three hundred sixteen autonomous auditor runs have produced tens of thousands of findings and zero gaps.

WHAT IS ALREADY WORKING, MEASURED. The six conservation auditors self-select. Boredom picked them from the tagged pool and re-ran them without any operator dispatch: the emission auditor alone has two hundred ninety two autonomous executions, the posterior auditor seventeen, and each run deterministically recomputes its violations. Their execution rows carry a findings_count in metadata; summed, the emission auditor has surfaced over thirty seven thousand findings and the posterior auditor about thirteen hundred. All of this is real, traced, and graded. None of it becomes a gap: a search of the gap store returns zero conservation or invariant gaps, and no vessel contains a consumer of the finding hashes the runs emit. The loop detects and forgets.

TWO DEFECTS, ONE OF THEM URGENT. First and most important, the bridge does not exist. Second, boredom is over-selecting the emission auditor by roughly twenty to one over its siblings and re-emitting the same one hundred twenty nine violations every run, because the auditor has no memory. A naive bridge that filed one gap per finding would therefore write tens of thousands of duplicate gaps and flood the demand ledger, which is the halo-minting failure the substrate is supposed to avoid. The bridge must aggregate.

THE PRESCRIBED SHAPE, AND WHY IT LIVES WHERE IT DOES. The bridge is a development-vessel resolver, because the gap store lives in development-vessel and the write must happen where the data lives. It reads, cross-vessel, the conservation-audit endpoint on activity-api, which is a pure read. For each invariant that reports violations it upserts exactly one aggregated substrateGap whose identifier is stable per invariant, for example conservation-emission-junction-violated, so re-running is idempotent and refreshes counts rather than multiplying rows. The gap summary names the violation count, the worst offenders, and the shared root cause where one exists, so that one hundred twenty nine arms emitting no rows becomes a single gap about a family, not one hundred twenty nine gaps. The output is bounded at six gaps, one per invariant, no matter how many findings the underlying runs produced. The exact emission mechanism to copy already exists in this repo: cost-expectation-scan posts a substrateGap_write impulse per finding with source substrate_detected; the only change is aggregation before the post and a stable per-invariant identifier.

ONCE IT EXISTS. Tag it with the boredom target tag so it self-selects on the same rhythm the auditors already ride, and the loop closes without hands: auditors detect on cadence, the bridge converts detection to demand on cadence, and the demand enters the same drafter path every other gap does. The emission auditor's over-selection also becomes visible as a real gap the moment the bridge runs, which is the selection-imbalance finding filing itself.

FALSIFIER. After the bridge exists and runs once, the gap store should contain between one and six conservation gaps whose source is substrate_detected, and re-running the bridge should not increase that count, only refresh the existing gaps' updated timestamps. If the count grows without bound on re-run, aggregation failed and the bridge is a flooder.

summary:
The compose posterior has stopped consuming its own verdicts, so the one link proven to close this morning is now open. This is the deepest blocker to compounding and the symptom is measured cleanly; the mechanism is a strongly-evidenced hypothesis with an exact verification attached, not yet confirmed.

THE SYMPTOM, PROVEN. Over three and a half hours of a pre-registered scorecard, the feature_compose Thompson posterior held exactly at alpha 53.65, beta 19.22, implied rate 73.6 percent, across eight successive readings. In the same window the identifier-keyed compose rows accrued new reached-false verdicts, from twenty four to thirty two. Real negative evidence is landing on the rows and the posterior is not moving.

THIS IS NOT A DEAD UPDATER. The Thompson update path is alive and moving other arms in the same window. The newly minted emission auditor went from its one-one seed to alpha 1.81, beta 1.19; the mitosis cutover arm carries fractional, shifting values; the metrics row for feature_compose itself is re-written every few minutes with a fresh timestamp. The updater runs and touches the compose row; it simply writes the same alpha and beta each time. The counters on that row do move: total executions climbed from about one thousand sixty to one thousand one hundred sixty and failed from its prior value to one thousand twenty. So the execution counters advance while the Thompson fields stand still, which means the two are updated by different triggers and only the counter trigger is firing for compose.

WHY THIS CONTRADICTS THIS MORNING. Earlier today, immediately after the grading instrumentation went live, beta moved by exactly one on a single reached-false verdict, delivered synchronously by goal-host through its reach-verdict path into the learning sink. That path fires only for goal-host's own in-process edit-intent dispatches. The thirty two reached-false rows now sitting ungraded-into-the-posterior all carry a null dispatcher and null outcome in metadata, which is the signature of rows graded by some path other than goal-host's synchronous delivery. The reach-classify contract is unambiguous that reached-false must penalize beta, so the verdict exists and the rule exists; what is missing is the call that carries these particular verdicts into posterior-update.

THE HYPOTHESIS, AND ITS EXACT TEST. The leading explanation is that autonomous compose runs, dispatched by boredom or the self-development lane rather than by goal-host edit-intent, have their reached field patched onto the row by an asynchronous path that never invokes posterior-update, or invokes it after the row's pre-verdict is no longer ungraded so the double-count guard skips it. Either way the beta penalty is written to the row and never to the posterior. To confirm: take one of the thirty two exec-identifier rows, for example exec_1788699739699_mnf762kwoaf, and establish whether POST /reach was ever called for it and whether posterior-update logged a credit or penalty or a skip for that identifier. If posterior-update logged a skip or was never called, the hypothesis holds and the fix is to route the asynchronous reach patch through posterior-update the same way goal-host's synchronous delivery does. If posterior-update logged a penalty that did not move beta, the defect is downstream in the metrics write and this hypothesis is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST. Every other repair this week routes through this junction. Fixing addressing so verdicts reach the right rows, fixing the emission so refusals and failures become rows, minting auditors that detect imbalance, building the bridge that turns detection into demand: all of it assumes that a verdict on a row eventually moves a posterior. For compose, right now, it does not. Until it does, the compose lane can be graded perfectly and still never learn, and the scorecard's convergence criterion cannot be met no matter how honest the grading becomes.

FALSIFIER. Deliver a reached-false verdict for a fresh compose exec-identifier row through the same asynchronous path these thirty two took, and watch beta. If beta rises, the posterior is consuming verdicts and this gap is closed or was never real. If beta holds while the row shows reached-false, the junction is broken as described.

summary: HORIZON LAYER (derivative instrument, genuinely new): the substrate measures every conservation residual at LEVEL only (violation counts per invariant) via the conservation-audit junctions, residual-shape-discovery, and model-opportunity-scan report resolvers - but NOTHING measures a residual's RATE OF CHANGE. A residual can be nonzero-but-shrinking (self-healing) or small-but-accelerating (about to break); level cannot tell them apart. DESIGN: per conservation invariant, compute the recent-window vs prior-window residual ratio from execution history (client-side date buckets; NEVER combine a datetime comparison with another predicate - SurrealQL silently drops the conjunct) and classify CONVERGING / FLAT / DIVERGING; emit a substrateGap when ratio exceeds a divergence threshold. Fire on divergence-RATE, not level. MEASURED EVIDENCE (this audit): the structure-residual proxy (organic new-arm introductions per day, excluding test/nonexistent probe arms) diverged recent-3-day mean 33.7/day vs prior-3-day 12.7/day = 2.66x over the 38k-row execution window; with probe arms included it is 3.51x (a partially self-inflicted, probe-driven component - the level instruments show none of this because they read a snapshot). NEGATIVE CONTROL / FALSIFIER (both directions REQUIRED): the detector must FIRE on an unplanted diverging residual computed live from execution history (e.g. the organic new-arm rate above, which no operator planted), AND must stay SILENT on a genuinely flat residual - the daily failure-fraction proxy measured slope +0.0012/day (28.8% prior-3 -> 32.6% recent-3, within the 6-82% day-to-day noise band) is the flat negative control it must NOT flag. A detector that fires on a replayed/planted series but not on this organic divergence, or that flags the flat failure-fraction, is falsified. IMPLEMENTATION HINT: extend an already-wired single-file report resolver that already emits a residual/opportunity report (model-opportunity-scan or residual-shape-discovery are live, single-file, already have call sites) to add the per-invariant recent-vs-prior ratio to its report body plus a gap emission on divergence - helper-first / new-file splits are dead code and the semantic gate refuses them, so the derivative computation and its call site must land in the same file in one goal.

summary:
PRE-REGISTERED, before the guard fix lands, so its outcome can falsify rather than be fitted. Two separate predictions, deliberately split because conflating them produces a false negative.

PREDICTION ONE, THE PRIMARY SIGNAL. If widening the reach grading guard works, the count of compose execution rows carrying the reach graded true stamp must rise above seven. That stamp is written inside the branch immediately before credit is applied, so it is a direct witness that the posterior path executed. It needs only new traffic to move.

PREDICTION TWO, DELIBERATELY NOT CONFLATED WITH THE FIRST. The thirty four rows already stranded with a reached false tag and no stamp will only drain if something re-calls the reach endpoint for those old executions. Within a single call the pre-existing tags do not yet carry the verdict, because the mirror writes it afterwards, so a stranded row is rescued only by a second visit from the reach spool retry or a duplicate patch. If nothing revisits them the stranded count stays at thirty four even with the fix working perfectly. A static thirty four is therefore NOT evidence of failure; it is a separate question about whether the spool revisits, and must be reported as such.

PREDICTION THREE, THE CREDIT ASYMMETRY, REGISTERED NOW BECAUSE IT IS THE NEXT LIKELY SURPRISE. Measured on the compose arm: one reached true verdict moved alpha by zero point seven four while one reached false verdict moved beta by zero point two six, roughly three to one per verdict. If that weighting is systematic then an arm whose true to false ratio is about one to six can hold an implied rate near seventy three percent indefinitely even when every verdict is consumed. The check: over the next twenty graded compose verdicts the implied rate must fall. If alpha per true stays about three times beta per false while the implied rate does not fall, the defect is the delta weighting in computeDeltas, not the grading path, and the investigation must move there rather than continuing to hunt for verdicts that are not arriving. Registering this now is what prevents an unfrozen but never converging posterior from costing another day.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THE WHOLE FRAME. If the stamp count rises and the implied rate falls toward the counter derived rate near twelve percent, the ordering defect was the binding constraint and the loop closes. If the stamp count rises and the implied rate does not fall, the binding constraint is the weighting. If the stamp count does not rise at all, the guard was not the mechanism and five refuted hypotheses become six.

OUTCOME RECORDED 2026-09-07, after the fixes landed. The predictions in this gap now have verdicts and are written back so the store records confirmations as well as failures.

PREDICTION ONE, PRIMARY SIGNAL: PASSED. The reach graded stamp count rose from seven to ten. Each new stamp corresponded to exactly one beta unit.

PREDICTION TWO, BETA RISES: PASSED. Beta moved from nineteen point four eight to twenty three point four eight, an increase of four, while alpha held completely flat at fifty four point three nine. The implied success rate fell from seventy three point six percent to sixty nine point eight percent, the first movement toward the counter derived rate of about twelve percent in twelve hours.

PREDICTION THREE, CREDIT ASYMMETRY: ARMED AND UNFIRED. The concern was that alpha per positive verdict might run about three times beta per negative verdict and stall convergence. Across five successive beta increments alpha did not move at all, so the asymmetry did not materialise on this sample. The check remains armed for the next twenty verdicts and must not be acted on until it fires; touching the delta weighting on an unfired hypothesis would corrupt the evidence just made honest.

THE SPLIT WAS LOAD BEARING. The original conjunctive form of this falsifier, requiring stamps to rise and stranded rows to fall together, would have reported failure four separate times while the fix worked, because stamps rise with new traffic whereas stranded rows only drain if something revisits old executions and nothing does. Splitting the criterion by denominator is what made the confirmation readable.

DELIVERY COVERAGE, MEASURED ON THE CORRECT DENOMINATOR. Restricted to compose rows created after the delivery fix loaded, twenty nine percent now carry a reach tag against a historical baseline of four and a half percent. The aggregate across all rows remains near ninety five percent untagged because eleven hundred historical rows dominate it; reading the aggregate would hide the working fix, which is the same denominator error that let telemetry rows inflate grading coverage by a factor of two point three.
The autonomous self-development lane never enters the grading path, resulting in ninety-five percent of the substrate's own code-change executions not being able to move a posterior.
remedy: This gap is closed because the autonomous compose lane is now integrated with the grading path, allowing its code changes to be evaluated and move posteriors.

The falsifier census under-reports measurable gaps: classifyFalsifier in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts stamps falsifier="none" on gaps that carry a Class-1b expected_literal predicate, which the sweep DOES honour.

EVIDENCE. verifyGapConditionAsync (Class 1b) measures a gap when classification_metadata has edit_site + expected_literal, returning absent/present by reading the deployed file under /vessels. classifyFalsifier recognises only hardcoded_url (class1) and evidence_resolve/verify_shape (class2); the string expected_literal does not occur anywhere in substrate-gap.ts. A live gap carrying edit_site + expected_literal="reachId2" was written and read back with both fields intact and falsifier="none".

WHY IT MATTERS. The stamp is the census used to judge which gaps are closable. A gap that IS measurable is counted as unmeasurable, so remediation effort is aimed by a number that is wrong in the pessimistic direction. The Class-1 branch of this same function carries the comment "a census that can lie is worse than no census, because the lie is what gets acted on" -- this is that failure, one class over.

REGION / ANCHOR. Ground on the single line that begins the Class-1 test, which occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file:
  if (usablePredicateString(m["hardcoded_url"])) {
Add a new Class-1b test in the same style immediately BEFORE that line: when usablePredicateString(m["expected_literal"]) is set, return falsifier "class1" with predicate_position "expected_literal" if an edit_site or file_path is also present, and "unresolvable" if it is not -- mirroring exactly how the hardcoded_url branch already treats a predicate with no file to read it in. Change nothing else.

summary:
98.2% of open gaps carry no measurement predicate, so the unaided close lane structurally cannot reach them. The gap store has a working measured-close path -- sweepPendingLandVerifications closes a gap with closed_reason=landed_verified when verifyGapConditionAsync positively MEASURES the condition gone -- and it has produced 50 closes all-time, so the machinery is not broken. What is missing is a PRODUCER: no component ever arms a predicate when a gap is filed.

CENSUS (gaps.json, 3512 rows, 2026-09-07). Predicate coverage over ALL gaps: none 3457, hardcoded_url 42, evidence_resolve/verify_shape 11, expected_literal 2. Over the 778 OPEN gaps: none 764 (98.2%), class2 11, url 3, literal 1. Closure is dominated by expiry, not closure: expired_not_redetected 905 versus landed_verified 50.

CONSEQUENCE, OBSERVED. A gap with no predicate that lands once is stamped disposition=pending_verification and held: the picker then SKIPS it, by design, so a second landing cannot manufacture a false close. Live sweep tally, repeated every 1-2 minutes: checked=25 closed=0 {absent:0, present:2, pending:22, unknown:1}. 22 of 25 are correctly abstaining on an input that cannot be measured. 40 gaps are being skipped as pending out of a 226-gap pick pool. This is not a bug in the sweep -- the sweep is right to abstain -- it is an absent input.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. Something that, at filing time, derives a falsifiable predicate from the gap's own content and writes it into classification_metadata: for a surgical code gap, edit_site plus the expected_literal the fix must introduce (Class 1b, measured against the DEPLOYED file under /vessels, so it also catches a change that landed but never deployed); for a behavioural gap, an evidence_resolve shape (Class 2). classifyFalsifier already LABELS predicates and is explicitly non-mutating by design ("ADD BESIDE, NEVER REWRITE"), so it is the census, not the producer, and should not be made to do this job.

FALSIFIER FOR THIS GAP. Refuted if predicate coverage over open gaps rises above 10% without an operator hand-writing the predicates, or if landed_verified closes come to exceed expired_not_redetected. Confirmed while open-gap predicate coverage stays near 2%.

NOTE ON SCOPE. Filed WITHOUT an edit_site deliberately: the correct home for the producer is a design decision, and naming a file here would route every repair attempt at a path chosen by guess.

CONSEQUENCE MEASURED 2026-09-07 19:00 -- THIS CLOGS THE COMPOSE LANE, NOT JUST THE CENSUS. Because a gap with no predicate can never leave pending_verification, the pending population is permanent and grows, and it keeps winning picks. Over 30 minutes: 19 picks, 16 of them (84%) hit "PENDING verification at pick time -- skipping re-compose" and did no work; only 5 real composes ran; 0 non-attempts. Upstream of that, admission excluded 470 of 751 eligible gaps as no_groundable_target (63%). Real queued work at the same score (route-edit-15c44caa, score 0.84) received ZERO picks in that window. So the missing predicate producer is not only an accounting defect -- it is the reason the cap-1 compose lane idles while real work starves.

Two insertions, both purely additive, no existing line deleted or changed. All anchors below were verified verbatim-unique against the current file.

First insertion. The line

that immediately precedes the verbatim-unique line

    const traceEndpoint = process.env["METABOB_ENDPOINT"] ?? "http://127.0.0.1:8080";

gets one new statement inserted directly ABOVE that `try {` line:

  let emittedExecutionId: string | null = null;

And inside that same try-block, directly after the verbatim-unique line

        console.log(`[feature-compose] trace emission persisted execution_id=${emittedId}`);

insert:

        emittedExecutionId = emittedId;

Second insertion. In the resolver's final return — the object whose body begins with the verbatim-unique line

      ok: effectiveVerdict === "FAVORABLE",

insert one new field directly after that line:

      execution_id: emittedExecutionId,

Both insertions must land together; the value flows from the first to the second, so a draft carrying only one of them does not address this goal.

Why: the trace store already returns the compose run's real exec_* row id when the trace is posted, and the current code reads it into a const named emittedId whose only consumer is the console.log above — the id is captured and then discarded. Because it never reaches the returned featureComposeReport, the caller synthesizes feature_compose:<commit-sha> as the execution id, which matches no row, so no reach verdict can ever address the compose run's actual record: self-development has 5 graded rows in three weeks against 868 ungraded exec_* rows. summary:
The GET /conservation-audit route is registered TWICE in repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts with byte-identical handler bodies (verified by diffing the two blocks: the only difference was a trailing brace from the slice boundary). The framework serves the FIRST registration, so the second is unreachable dead code.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
1. Dead code: roughly 80 lines that can never execute.
2. BLOCKING: every anchor inside the handler now occurs twice, so any surgical edit to this endpoint hits an ambiguous old_string and cannot be applied. Adding a new invariant to this endpoint is impossible until the duplicate is removed.

HOW IT HAPPENED: two separate substrate-authored landings each appended the endpoint (ad41776 for gap route-edit-97c7b422, and 776456c for gap route-edit-c2ed2d92, which also added conservation-residual-trend). Both landed through the gated lane and both were verified only by the endpoint answering HTTP 200.

WHY VERIFICATION MISSED IT: a 200 response is served by the first registration and is therefore IDENTICAL whether the route is registered once or twice. An endpoint returning 200 does not prove there is exactly one of it. The check that would have caught this is a count of registrations for the same method+path, not a request against it.

FIX: remove the second registration of GET /conservation-audit (the later of the two identical blocks), leaving exactly one. Do not alter the surviving handler, and do not touch conservation-audit-emit or conservation-residual-trend, which are distinct routes and are correct.

NOTE: this gap has no literal-presence predicate because the defect is a COUNT (two registrations) rather than the presence or absence of a string, and the existing falsifier classes cannot express a count. The closing check is: exactly one occurrence of the route registration for GET /conservation-audit.

summary:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/compose-workspace.ts, add one line so the push clone's own HEAD advances instead of drifting forever.

Find this exact text:

```
      await git(clone, ["fetch", "origin", "dev"]).catch(() => { /* offline: use last-known origin/dev */ });
```

Replace it with exactly this:

```
      await git(clone, ["fetch", "origin", "dev"]).catch(() => { /* offline: use last-known origin/dev */ });
      await git(clone, ["merge", "--ff-only", "origin/dev"]).catch(() => { /* dirty, detached or diverged: worktrees still pin to origin/dev */ });
```

One inserted line, immediately after the existing fetch. Change nothing else.

Reason: this function fetches origin/dev and adds a per-compose worktree pinned to it, so composes are correctly isolated and fresh. Nothing, however, ever advances the clone's OWN checkout. Measured on the live substrate 2026-09-07 22:52: the push clone at /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/development-vessel sat on a detached HEAD at 4c863ee dated 09-07 00:26 while origin/dev was at 8c93591 dated 21:46 — 29 commits and 21 hours behind — with five modified files in its working tree. substrate-pull-sync runs every ten minutes and reports synced=0 on every run; it does not manage this clone. The lag is unbounded and grows monotonically.

Scope honestly: no push failure was observed during that window, and composes were unaffected because their worktrees pin to a freshly fetched origin/dev rather than to the clone HEAD. The exposure is that the mitosis cutover reads this clone for its drift and freshness checks (it logs 'in the push clone (<sha>) vs staged base <sha>'), so those checks compare against a tree that can be arbitrarily old. merge --ff-only is chosen deliberately over reset --hard: it advances the clone when it cleanly can and refuses harmlessly when the tree is dirty or diverged, so it can never discard staged content.

Verify with bun run lint in repos/development-vessel.

summary:
The autonomous dispatch path never grades anything it does. Every execution dispatched through light-dispatch-vessel is written to the trace store with no reach verdict, ever, so no work the substrate does on its own can move a posterior.

MEASURED (2026-09-08). Of 810 conservation execution rows, exactly 8 carry a non-null `reached` and exactly 8 carry `reach_graded:true` -- and they are the SAME 8 rows, which are precisely the 8 tagged `dispatcher_used:goal-host`. The other 802, all tagged `dispatcher_used:light-dispatch`, are ungraded. Fleet-wide control over the newest 3000 execution rows: light-dispatch 0/1072 graded, goal-host 46/1370, no-dispatcher-tag 44/558. The zeros are real, not a broken query: `reach_graded:true` is findable in the same datasets (90/3000 and 60/2000).

THIS IS NOT A CLASSIFICATION SKIP. POST /v2/activities/execution-traces/reach writes the verdict tag BEFORE it checks whether to grade, so a row that was POSTed and then skipped would still carry a `reached:*` tag. Zero verdict tags across 802 rows means no reach POST arrives at all. Confirmed in the deployed tree: the only callers of `execution-traces/reach` are goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts and development-vessel/src/resolvers/{gap-to-feature,vessel-mitosis-cutover}.ts. light-dispatch-vessel has no call site. boredom-vessel only GETs /executions/<id>/reach to read a verdict for its own bookkeeping.

LIVE PROOF OF THE CONSEQUENCE. Six auditor arms ran 65 new executions in one hour through this path; their posteriors did not move at all, remaining at exactly thompson_alpha=1.8125, thompson_beta=1.1875. That sums to 3.000 = the 1.0/1.0 prior plus exactly 1.0 of evidence -- a single graded update each, which was their one goal-host dispatch at mint time. Everything they have done autonomously since has taught nothing.

FIX. In repos/light-dispatch-vessel/src/index.ts, after the trace is posted at the END of a dispatch, POST the reach verdict for that execution.

REGION / ANCHOR. The bare line `await postTrace(trace);` occurs TWICE in this file and is therefore ambiguous. Ground instead on this exact three-line sequence, which occurs EXACTLY ONCE:

  await postTrace(trace);

  return {

Insert the new code between `await postTrace(trace);` and `return {`. Do not modify the other postTrace call site, and do not touch the top of the file or any import.

THE VERDICT SOURCE -- READ THIS, IT IS THE POINT OF THE CHANGE. Do NOT grade `reached:true` on HTTP 200, and do NOT grade it on `overallStatus === "success"` alone. Either would pump vacuous positive credit into every posterior and destroy the honest signal this gap exists to restore; an activity that exits cleanly while producing a wrapper instead of the asked-for output is exactly the hollow completion the reach gate exists to catch. Grade on SHAPE COVERAGE, which is what the walk's own reach check verifies: the execution reached iff `overallStatus === "success"` AND every output shape declared by the template's tasks appears in `outputShapesProduced`. Both values are already in scope at the anchor: `outputShapesProduced` is the accumulator filled from each successful task result, and the template is `tpl`. Read each task's declared output shapes defensively, since the local task type may not declare that field.

Send the verdict to `${ACTIVITY_API}/v2/activities/execution-traces/reach` as a POST with body {execution_id, reached}, reusing the existing `auth()` helper for headers and the same AbortController timeout pattern as `postTrace`. Name the computed boolean `reachVerdict`.

WHY THIS IS NOT DEAD CODE. It replicates a delivery block already live in this fleet: development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts posts to this same endpoint after a compose, landed in commit c5468ed and currently deployed, and that block has been observed delivering verdicts (HTTP 200 at the receiver, and the compose posterior moved as a result). The call must be fire-and-forget with its errors swallowed so that grading can never fail or slow a dispatch -- that is the established pattern here, not a stub.

PRE-REGISTERED CHECK AFTER THIS LANDS. Alpha-per-execution on the auditor arms must stay well below 1.0. If every execution grades reached:true, the verdict source is vacuous and the change is wrong even though it will look like it worked.

summary:
The oracle corpus goal_verification_labels holds 3,667 verdicts, 1,030 of them authored by a human labeler, accumulated between 2026-07-02 and 2026-09-07. Across the entire live fleet there is exactly ONE read of that table, in repos/activity-api/src/routes/impulses.ts, and it is the read-back endpoint that serves the shape. No learning component reads it. Writers are the impulses route and feature-compose.

So the corpus is write-only with respect to learning: two months of external judgement, including a thousand human verdicts, have never moved an alpha, a beta, or an edge. The documented front door says so itself — provide_feedback records 'into the substrate's oracle corpus (goal_verification_labels) — currently for offline audit, not yet consumed by an automated reach-gate recalibration path'.

Why this matters more than an ordinary missing feature: a closed self-grading loop drifts toward whatever its own instrument rewards and cannot detect the drift from inside. Every flattering-direction failure measured on this substrate on 2026-09-06/07 was caught by an operator control and none by the system: a gap closed citing a real commit whose diff did something else; a semantic gate returning verified:true for a change that did not occur; a falsifier marker taken from an adjacent line that then self-sealed the closure; baseline traffic read as a step change. The stated S1->S2->S3 trajectory removes that operator. This corpus is the only existing channel that could replace them, and nothing consumes it.

WHAT IS NEEDED, and this gap is deliberately not specifying a one-line edit because none is honest here: a consumer that reads goal_verification_labels and turns a verdict into durable learned state. The smallest useful first step is not recalibration but VISIBILITY — a scan that joins labels to the recorded reach verdict for the same execution_id and reports where the human and the system disagree, together with the count and direction of that disagreement. That measurement is a precondition for any recalibration policy, and it is checkable: today the disagreement rate is unknown because nothing has ever compared the two.

Evidence: validation/reports/PREREG_gap_admission_grounding_2026-09-06.md

The compose lane sometimes applies an inserted block TWICE, landing a verbatim duplicate that typechecks and passes every gate.

TWO CONFIRMED INSTANCES ON 2026-09-08, both in changes that otherwise landed correctly:
1. repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts -- GET /conservation-audit was registered twice with byte-identical handler bodies (~80 lines). The framework serves the first, so the second was unreachable dead code, and because every anchor inside the handler then occurred twice, the endpoint became impossible to edit surgically until the duplicate was removed (commit 207c16a, 82 deletions).
2. repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts -- a replacement block landed duplicated at lines 4790-4795 and 4796-4801, identical if/else pairs inside the same enclosing if. Behaviourally harmless here (same condition, same assignment, doubled log line) and tsc exits 0, but redundant. Landed in commit 47f73b7.

WHY NO GATE CATCHES IT. Typecheck passes because a duplicated statement is valid TypeScript. The semantic gate reads the diff and sees the intended change present. A duplicated route registration even answers HTTP 200 identically, because the first registration serves. Verification by exercising the change cannot distinguish one copy from two -- only COUNTING occurrences can.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. Instance 1 shows the real cost: a duplicated block makes its entire interior unaddressable, because every anchor within it becomes ambiguous and every subsequent surgical edit fails with an old_string collision. That converts a cosmetic defect into a permanent blocker on further repair of that region.

WHAT WOULD DETECT THIS WITHOUT AN OPERATOR. After an apply, count occurrences of the inserted text in the resulting file. If a block that should appear once appears twice, the apply is wrong even though the diff looks right and the typecheck is clean. The check is cheap and needs no test infrastructure: it compares a count before and after, on text the composer already has in hand.

Filed as an observation with two verified instances rather than a single-file edit request, because the correct location for the check is in the apply path and that placement is a design decision.

In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, persist the pending-verification verdict that the pick-time check already computes, so the candidate-set exclusion can see it and stop re-picking the same gaps forever.

ANCHOR. This exact line occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file:
  if (_pickCond === 'pending') {

Immediately inside that block, AFTER the existing console.log line that ends with `PENDING verification at pick time — skipping re-compose\`);` and BEFORE the `return {` that follows it, insert exactly this one statement:

    await markPendingVerification(gap, undefined, "pending at pick time: landed once, no measurement predicate — persisted so the candidate filter can exclude it");

Change nothing else. Do not touch the console.log, the return value, the enclosing condition, the comment above it, the top of the file, or any import.

WHY. `_pickCond` is recomputed by verifyGapCondition on every pick. For a gap that has a landed commit naming it and no measurement predicate, that recomputation returns 'pending' every single time, so the pick is discarded. But this branch writes NOTHING back to the gap store, while the picker's candidate-set exclusion (the `skipped_pending` count in the pick log) filters on the STORED `classification_metadata.disposition`. The result is a closed loop with no exit: the picker ranks the gap top, the pick-time check recomputes 'pending' and discards the cycle, nothing is persisted, the exclusion filter stays blind, and the same gap wins the next tick.

MEASURED IMPACT, twice in a row on a quiet box (loadavg ~3, zero compose-cap refusals, so this is not contention): 25 picks / 25 skipped / 0 composes over 40 minutes, then 13 picks / 13 skipped / 0 composes over 30 minutes. In both windows the picks resolved to just FOUR distinct gap ids — route-edit-040f827e, route-edit-c263f498-narrowed, route-edit-0da646c8, route-edit-7b7e0ea0-narrowed — out of 817 open gaps. All four carry `disposition: None` and no `pending_outcome_verification` in the store, which is exactly the symptom: the pick-time check knows they are pending and the store does not. The compose lane has produced zero executions across both windows.

WHY THIS IS SAFE AND NOT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. It does not change what the pick-time check decides, and it does not re-enable composing these gaps — the skip and the returned `pending_verification` report are untouched. It only records the verdict that was already reached, using the same helper the sweep already calls for the identical situation at the `markPendingVerification(g, sha, "pending sweep: single landing, no measurement predicate")` call site. `markPendingVerification` is declared at module scope in this same file and is already awaited at three other call sites, so it is in scope here.

In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, teach the gap picker to recognise a Class-1b measurement predicate, so gaps that CAN measure their way out are no longer treated as unmeasurable and skipped forever.

ANCHOR. This exact line occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file:
      || typeof m.evidence_resolve === 'string' || typeof m.verify_shape === 'string';

ONE OPERATION. Replace that single line with exactly:
      || typeof m.evidence_resolve === 'string' || typeof m.verify_shape === 'string'
      || typeof m.expected_literal === 'string';

Change nothing else. Do not touch the preceding `const hasMeasurablePredicate = typeof m.hardcoded_url === 'string'` line, the enclosing predicate, the top of the file, or any import.

WHY. That expression computes `hasMeasurablePredicate` inside the `isPending` callback the gap picker passes to `chooseFirstActionable`. It enumerates the predicate kinds a gap may carry — `hardcoded_url` (Class 1), `evidence_resolve` and `verify_shape` (Class 2) — but omits `expected_literal`, which is the Class-1b predicate. `verifyGapCondition` in this same file DOES honour `expected_literal`: it evaluates edit_site plus expected_literal against the deployed tree under /vessels with inverse polarity, so the literal being present means the defect is absent. The string `expected_literal` already appears six times in this file, so the concept is known here — it is only missing from this one enumeration.

CONSEQUENCE OF THE OMISSION. A gap that has been armed with a working Class-1b predicate still evaluates `hasMeasurablePredicate === false`, so `isPending` returns true and the picker skips it as unmeasurable. The gap can never be selected, and therefore can never land the change that would let its own predicate measure it resolved. It is a closed loop that arming the predicate was supposed to open.

MEASURED IMPACT. The compose lane has produced ZERO executions across four consecutive 30-minute windows on an idle box (loadavg 3-8, zero compose-cap refusals, so this is not contention). Recent windows: 9 picks / 9 skipped / 0 composes, then 23 picks / 23 skipped / 0 composes. Every pick is discarded by this pending judgement. `chooseFirstActionable` scans at most PENDING_SCAN_MAX = 20 candidates and then deliberately fails open, returning a pending gap that the post-selection guard refuses — so widening what counts as measurable is what actually frees the lane.

THIS IS THE SAME OMISSION IN A SECOND PLACE. `classifyFalsifier` in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/substrate-gap.ts has the identical blind spot and stamps `falsifier:"none"` on gaps carrying `expected_literal`. That was filed separately. Fix only the picker here; do not modify substrate-gap.ts in this change.

summary:
[narrowed from conservation-audit-route-registered-twice-blocks-all-further-edits] The GET /conservation-audit route is registered TWICE in repos/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts with byte-identical handler bodies (verified by diffing the two blocks: the only difference was a trailing brace from the slice boundary). The framework serves the FIRST registration, so the second is unreachable dead code.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
1. Dead code: roughly 80 lines that can never execute.
2. BLOCKING: every anchor inside the handler now occurs twice, so any surgical edit to this endpoint hits an ambiguous old_string and cannot be applied. Adding a new invariant to this endpoint is impossible until the duplicate is removed.

HOW IT HAPPENED: two separate substrate-authored landings each appended the endpoint (ad41776 for gap route-edit-97c7b422, and 776456c for gap route-edit-c2ed2d92, which also added conservation-residual-trend). Both landed through the gated lane and both were verified only by the endpoint answering HTTP 200.

WHY VERIFICATION MISSED IT: a 200 response is served by the first registration and is therefore IDENTICAL whether the route is registered once or twice. An endpoint returning 200 does not prove there is exactly one of it. The check that would have caught this is a count of registrations for the same method+path, not a request against it.

FIX: remove the second registration of GET /conservation-audit (the later of the two identical blocks), leaving exactly one. Do not alter the surviving handler, and do not touch conservation-audit-emit or conservation-residual-trend, which are distinct routes and are correct.

NOTE: this gap has no literal-presence predicate because the defect is a COUNT (two registrations) rather than the presence or absence of a string, and the existing falsifier classes cannot express a count. The closing check is: exactly one occurrence of the route registration for GET /conservation-audit.

summary:
Nothing derives a region anchor for a gap, so the compose drafter is localised by a guess instead of a fact - and the machinery that would consume a real anchor is already built and idle.

THE CONSUMER EXISTS AND WORKS. In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, regionHint is read as String(gapMeta.region ?? "").trim(). When it is non-empty the compose pipeline changes behaviour in four ways: the grounding window is centred on that literal, focusHints is led by it, the op budget is set for a region-named gap (logged as [fc-scope] region-named gap), and the fc-anchor-region veto takes its EXPLICIT-region branch, which is the branch where that guard's premise actually holds. None of this requires new code.

THE PRODUCER DOES NOT EXIST. Measured 2026-09-08 over 3,898 gaps: only 22 (0.6%) carry classification_metadata.region. Of the currently OPEN gaps, 284 have an edit_site but no region. A source comment in feature-compose.ts records the same absence independently: 0 of 402 gaps set metadata.region. Because the field is empty, localisation falls back to regionCandidatesFromText, which mines identifiers out of the gap's prose - a median of 53 candidate identifiers per compose - and centres a ~54KB window on whichever one it finds first. Nothing in the gap says which of those identifiers is the edit target.

CAUSAL EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS THE DOMINANT FAILURE. On 2026-09-08 a dispatch planned an anchor that was unique in the live file at line 988. The mined region located at line 50. The 938-line distance tripped the veto, the edit was refused as anchor_not_from_window, and it escalated to patch_with_tools - whose FIRST action was to search the file for that same anchor, find it, and apply the edit at lines 988-990. That result typechecked and landed as commit 59732fd. The vetoed anchor was correct; the mined region was wrong. Separately, a failure-lesson census over 1,387 recorded lessons: 52% are edit-mechanics classes (anchor_not_found 20.0%, typecheck_dangling_reference 16.1%, syntax_break 13.5%, wrong_location 2.5%) and a further 29.1% are semantic_reject, whose sampled reasons describe a small edit made ADJACENT to the target rather than at it.

WHAT TO BUILD. An activity that, for a gap carrying an edit_site, derives a region literal and writes it to classification_metadata.region. It has two halves and they should be separate so only the uncertain one is graded:
(a) DETERMINISTIC, no learning needed: given a candidate literal, verify it occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the deployed file at edit_site under /vessels, and that it encloses or sits within ANCHOR_REGION_SLACK_LINES (160) of the intended change. Uniqueness and enclosure are grep facts.
(b) STOCHASTIC, and this is the part worth grading: choose WHICH literal to propose, from the gap's own text plus the file. This is a judgement - the drafter currently has ~53 candidates and no signal distinguishing the edit target from identifiers mentioned only as evidence. Minting this half as its own activity gives it a posterior, admits competing variants, and lets the ribosome extract improvements. A behaviour that lives only inside a resolver cannot be graded (law 2).

HONEST LIMIT ON THE EVIDENCE. The observational comparison is weak and should not be read as stronger than it is. Across the 22 gaps that do carry a region, anchor_not_found plus wrong_location account for 16.2% of their failure lessons versus 22.0% for the 3,876 without - directionally favourable but n=22, and those same 22 gaps have a LOWER close rate (36.4% vs 72.3%), most likely selection bias because a region tends to get added to gaps something already struggled with. The case rests on the mechanism and the causal instance above, not on that comparison.

MEASUREMENT PLAN, PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE PRODUCER IS ENABLED. Record the anchor_not_found plus wrong_location share of failure lessons, windowed by each lesson's own at timestamp, for gaps composed WITH a produced region versus WITHOUT, over at least 50 lessons per arm. Compare shares, never cumulative counts: throughput varies several-fold between windows and raw counts rise with volume regardless. Refutation: if the share does not fall for region-armed gaps, the producer is not earning its cost.

The compose failure-lesson channel stores build boilerplate instead of the diagnostic, so the drafter's only runtime teaching channel carries no information about why a verify failed.

MEASURED 2026-09-08. On gaps whose lessons were recorded after 20:30, every verify_failed lesson's `reason` field is exactly 200 characters and every one of them is consumed by the build preamble:
  "== install == == resolve == DRYRUN_EXIT=0  @types/bun@1.3.14  typescript@5.9.3  bun-types@1.3.14 ... [3.00ms] done == typecheck == $ tsc --noEmit src/resolvers/sub"
The string ends mid-path, exactly where the TypeScript error would begin. The accompanying `raw_excerpt` fields measured 479 and 529 characters, also ending mid-error.

WHY THIS MATTERS. feature-compose.ts:2213-2214 renders `raw_excerpt` back to the drafter on a later attempt ("raw verify output (verbatim, from the prior failed attempt)"), and the code's own comment at 6190-6194 states that this is "the one learning loop that actually works" and that feeding it a misleading label "is a law-8 failure (the load-bearing fact is available but wrong at the moment of use) on the only channel with a runtime reader". The same law-8 failure is happening one level down: the label may now be right, but the evidence attached to it is the package list.

WHY IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS SLICE. At feature-compose.ts:3081 the lesson is written as `reason: reason.slice(0, 200), raw_excerpt: reason.slice(0, 1500)`. The 1500-char excerpt would be ample, but the stored excerpts are only ~500 chars, so `failedVerify.output` has ALREADY been truncated before it reaches this line. lessonReason is assembled at 6199-6204 as `failedApply?.detail ?? failedVerify?.output ?? semantic_gate?.reason ?? verdict`, so the cap is upstream of that, in whatever captures verify output. Note this is not a universal cap: a compose report inspected earlier the same day carried a 336KB verify output, so short outputs are a property of this path rather than of verification generally.

TWO INDEPENDENT FIXES, EITHER OF WHICH HELPS.
(a) Preserve the error, not the head. The classifier at feature-compose.ts:3063-3067 already greps `bad.output` for TS1128/TS1005/TS1109/TS1110 and TS2304/TS2552/TS2554/TS2551/TS2345/TS2322, so the error-bearing lines are identifiable at that point. Build the lesson `reason` from the lines matching /error TS\d+|\d+ fail|FAIL|Error:/ rather than from the first 200 characters. A head-slice of a build log is almost never the diagnostic, because build logs put the environment first and the failure last.
(b) Find and raise the upstream truncation so `failedVerify.output` still contains the error by the time the lesson is written.

WHY NOW. verify_failed is the dominant failure class on the gaps that currently localise successfully: among failure lessons recorded on region-armed gaps after 20:30, verify_failed is 57.1% versus a 15.7% historic base rate (n=7, P(>=4)=0.014 against that base). As localisation improves, the next bottleneck is the drafter learning why its applied change failed its tests, and that is exactly the information this channel is currently discarding.

FALSIFIER. Read any verify_failed lesson recorded after this change and confirm its reason or raw_excerpt contains a line matching /error TS\d+/ or a test-failure summary rather than the install/resolve preamble.

In repos/activity-api/src/lib/posterior-update.ts, make one silent skip audible.

Find this exact text:

```
    trace.signature &&
```

Replace it with exactly this:

```
    ((alphaDelta !== 0 || betaDelta !== 0) && !trace.signature
      ? (logger.warn('posterior-update: non-zero delta dropped, execution carries no signature key so no posterior row can be written', { activity_id: activityId, alpha_delta: alphaDelta, beta_delta: betaDelta }), false)
      : true) &&
    trace.signature &&
```

The existing line is preserved unchanged at the end; the new clause only adds a warning and always evaluates to true when it does not fire. No control flow changes. logger, activityId, alphaDelta and betaDelta are all already in scope at this point and are already passed to a logger.warn a few lines below.

Reason: this guard is the only write to context_thompson_scores on the outcome path, and it is gated on trace.signature. When an execution carries no signature the write is skipped, nothing throws, and the caller reports success. Measured on the live substrate 2026-09-08: the feature_compose posterior read alpha 6.918 / beta 2.973, n=64, last_updated_at 2026-09-06T10:42:06 while 19 other posterior rows updated in the same 17-minute window, so the learner was live and this arm alone was frozen. Every feature_compose execution in that window emitted metadata.reached, was tagged reach_graded:true and reached:false, and produced the log line 'late reach verdict graded into posteriors' — three landed fixes composing correctly — and the posterior still did not move. computeDeltas returned a full beta penalty of 1 for those rows, so a correct non-zero delta was computed and then discarded here.

The discard is unobservable from inside: 5,546 claimed gradings in 24 hours produced zero applyOutcomeToPosteriors failure warnings, because the function does not fail, it declines. Worse, the caller stamps reach_graded:true on the authoritative row before the credit is applied as a double-grade guard, so every row whose write is skipped here is permanently marked graded and can never be re-credited. This is silent, irreversible loss of learning signal.

The instance that exposed it is a regression: 28 of 994 feature_compose executions carried a signature before 2026-09-06T10:42, and 0 of 572 after. Restoring that emission is separate work. This change is the class-level fix — it makes any arm losing its signature key announce itself instead of silently reporting full success, which is the only reason this took an operator reading the posterior row rather than the log to find.

Verify with bun run lint in repos/activity-api.

summary:
93% of gap closures record no closed_reason, so law 7's gap triple cannot be measured and bookkeeping is indistinguishable from work.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 over the full gap store. Of all closed gaps, closed_reason is None on 1,744 rows. Breaking down what those None-reason closures actually are:
  auto_draft_decision:*        1,630  (93%)
  other                           97
  real gap (has an edit_site)     55  (3%)
  uninterpolated placeholder       2

CONSEQUENCE, OBSERVED DIRECTLY. Any aggregate that groups closures by day reads as though self-development output grew roughly twentyfold over the week: close-on-land closures went from ~1-6/day at the start of September to 81, 117 and 135/day on 09-05 through 09-07. Split by what the closed rows ARE, that surge is almost entirely auto_draft_decision bookkeeping - 124 of 135 on 09-07, 62 of 64 on 09-08 - while closures of gaps that carry an edit_site run 0-6 per day and are FLAT. An operator measuring progress from the closure stream will conclude the substrate is compounding when the underlying work rate has not changed. This is not hypothetical: it happened during this analysis and was caught only by sampling closed rows and reading their ids.

WHY IT MATTERS TO LAW 7. The gap triple is close rate, close latency, and durability. Two of the three are computed off the closure stream. With 93% of closures carrying no reason, close rate cannot distinguish a landed fix from a decision record being tidied up, and median close latency is dominated by whichever population is larger rather than by how fast real gaps get fixed. The law prescribes measuring progress this way and the data cannot currently support it.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. Every close should record why. The paths that close a gap already know: close-on-land knows it saw a genuine land signal, the pending-verify sweep knows it measured the condition absent (it already writes landed_verified), and expiry knows it expired (it already writes expired_not_redetected). The gap is the close-on-land path and whatever closes auto_draft_decision rows, which write nothing. Giving those two a reason - even a coarse one such as landed_on_origin and decision_record_settled - makes the triple computable and separates work from housekeeping in every downstream aggregate.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT FOUND ALONGSIDE. Two gaps exist whose id contains an uninterpolated template placeholder, including one whose entire id is the literal {{dispatch_id}}. A placeholder reached the gap store as a durable record and was then closed, which means at least one gap-creating path emits its template rather than its value.

FALSIFIER. Recompute the closed_reason census. The defect is resolved when the share of closed gaps with closed_reason None falls well below 93%, and when close-on-land closures of gaps carrying an edit_site can be counted separately from decision-record closures without reading gap ids.

summary:
Gaps that arrive carrying a concrete proposed change land 3x more often than gaps that only describe the defect - and nothing in the substrate turns the second kind into the first.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 across all 995 open-or-closed gaps carrying an edit_site:
  summary CONTAINS a concrete proposed change : 102 gaps, 29 landed = 28.4%
  summary only DESCRIBES the defect           : 893 gaps, 86 landed =  9.6%
  Fisher exact two-sided p = 5.75e-07
"Concrete proposed change" means the summary contains the edit itself - an indented multi-line code block, or an explicit instruction to insert or replace a named verbatim block - rather than prose describing what is wrong.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT TARGET. The failure-lesson census over 1,387 lessons puts 52% in edit-mechanics classes and a further 29% in semantic_reject, whose sampled reasons are consistently of the form "the patch does not change the behavior related to the gap, it only modifies logging output" - the drafter making a token edit because it does not know what change is actually required. Work already done on LOCALISATION (deriving a verified-unique region anchor for 145 gaps, and ranking a verified region first among locators) moved failures downstream from anchor_not_found to verify_failed but did not raise reach, and its randomised control is currently showing no effect. Localisation answers WHERE to edit. This gap is about WHAT to edit, and the association is an order of magnitude stronger.

THE CONFOUND, STATED PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME ONE THAT REFUTED THE LOCALISATION WORK. Gaps containing a concrete change were written by someone who already understood the fix. So this measurement may be reporting "gaps written by someone who knew the answer land more often", which is selection bias, not a causal effect of carrying the change. An identical-looking observational result on region anchors (armed 6.9% vs unarmed 1.9%, p=0.0022) is being dismantled by its own randomised control, where the region-stripped arm lands at the same rate as the armed arm. This finding must NOT be acted on as causal until it survives the same test.

THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT. Take gaps that carry an edit_site and only DESCRIBE the defect. Randomise into two arms. For the treatment arm, have an activity draft a concrete proposed change into the summary at filing time - the actual edit, verbatim, anchored on a literal verified to occur exactly once in the deployed file. Leave the control arm untouched. Measure the fraction of each arm that acquires a landed sha or closes, attributed BY GAP ID and never by log adjacency. Compare with Fisher exact. Refutation: if control >= treatment, carrying the change does not cause landing and the association was selection bias.

WHAT TO BUILD IF IT SURVIVES. An activity that consumes a gap with an edit_site and emits a proposed change - which is the stochastic, gradable half of gap authoring, and belongs as its own activity with its own posterior under law 2 rather than buried inside a resolver. It should be minted from a reached execution rather than declared (law 4). Note the deterministic half is already solved and reusable: verifying a literal occurs exactly once in the deployed file under /vessels is a grep, and that machinery exists.

FALSIFIER FOR THIS GAP AS WRITTEN. Recompute the two land rates. The claim is refuted if the concrete-change cohort does not land at a materially higher rate, or if a randomised trial shows no difference.

summary:
The substrate's own gap-narrowing loop is measurably inert: 259 narrowing operations produced a 0.4 percentage-point change in landing rate.

MEASURED 2026-09-08, PAIRED WITHIN-GAP. For every gap with a corresponding -narrowed variant (259 pairs), comparing the original against the narrowed version of the SAME gap:
  summary contains a concrete proposed change : parent 5%  -> narrowed 8%
  landed (acquired a sha, or closed landed_verified) : parent 7.3% (19/259) -> narrowed 7.7% (20/259)

This is a paired design on the same underlying gap before and after the substrate reprocessed it, so it is free of the selection bias that confounds cross-sectional gap comparisons - notably the confound that dissolved a region-anchor result earlier the same day, where an apparently significant 6.9% vs 1.9% difference turned out to reflect which gaps were well-specified rather than any effect of the intervention.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Narrowing is the substrate's mechanism for improving its own inputs: taking a gap it could not act on and reworking it into something it can. The architecture expects exactly this kind of self-improvement of the work queue. Measured over 259 attempts, it does not produce one. A loop that reprocesses gaps without making them more actionable consumes compose capacity - each narrowed gap is another entry competing for a cap-1 lane - while returning nothing.

THE TWO NUMBERS ARE CONSISTENT WITH EACH OTHER, AND THAT IS THE LEAD. Narrowing barely raises concreteness (5% to 8%) and correspondingly barely raises landing (7.3% to 7.7%). Separately measured across 995 gaps carrying an edit_site, gaps whose summary contains a concrete proposed change land at 28.4% versus 9.6% for gaps that only describe the defect, and that gap survives within-file matching (26.0% vs 8.1% across files containing both kinds, holding directionally in 5 of 6 files). If concreteness is the operative variable, then narrowing fails precisely because it does not supply it: it rewords the description rather than proposing the change.

WHAT TO CHANGE. Narrowing should be judged on whether its output contains a concrete proposed edit - the actual change, anchored on a literal verified to occur exactly once in the deployed file - not on whether the description got shorter or more specific in prose. A narrowed gap that still only describes a defect has not been improved in the dimension that predicts landing.

FALSIFIER. Recompute the paired comparison. The defect is resolved when narrowed gaps land at a materially higher rate than their parents, or when the share of narrowed summaries carrying a concrete proposed change rises well above the current 8%.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND IN CODE (repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, the chronic-failure narrowing branch). At the moment the narrowed child is created it does exactly two things:
  childMeta = { ...meta, failed_attempts: 0, parent_gap_id: parentId, narrowed_at: ... }
  summary   = `[narrowed from ${parentId}] ${parentSummary}`
The summary is the PARENT'S text with a prefix prepended. There is no narrowing step - nothing shortens the description, extracts the failing statement, or proposes a change. The comment directly above the branch nevertheless states "The child carries a tighter description", which the code does not implement. That comment is the specification this code fails to meet.

SO THE ONE RELIABLE EFFECT OF NARROWING IS RESETTING THE FAILURE COUNTER. The code says so itself: failed_attempts is set to 0 "so it re-enters the dispatch queue at normal priority rather than being culled by the landabilityScore filter". That filter exists to deprioritise gaps the substrate has repeatedly failed to land. Narrowing therefore launders chronic failure back into the queue at full priority without changing anything about why the gap kept failing.

CONSISTENT WITH THE MEASUREMENT. 259 narrowing operations, landing 7.3% -> 7.7%, concreteness 5% -> 8%. If the description is carried across unchanged, no landing improvement is expected, and none is observed.

MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY. Comparing stored summaries today, only 82 of 259 narrowed children are byte-identical to their parent after stripping the prefix; 177 differ, and at least one child is LONGER than its parent (151 chars vs 347). So summaries evolve after creation via other write paths, and the verbatim-copy claim is established from the CREATION code, not from the current stored state. The claim that narrowing itself supplies no narrowing rests on reading that branch.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, EACH TESTABLE.
(a) Make narrowing narrow. The child summary should carry the specific failing statement or a concrete proposed change - the actual edit, anchored on a literal verified to occur exactly once in the deployed file - rather than the parent's prose. This is the same capability described in the separately filed gap about nothing turning a described defect into a concrete proposed change, and the two should probably be solved together.
(b) Stop resetting failed_attempts, or carry a decayed value rather than zero, so a chronically-failing gap does not return to full priority merely by acquiring a new id. This is a selection-policy change and should be measured before and after: watch whether pick cycles spent on repeatedly-failing gap families fall without starving gaps that were narrowed for good reason.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE LOOP. The architecture expects the substrate to improve its own work queue over time. Narrowing is that mechanism. Measured over 259 attempts it returns nothing while consuming capacity in a cap-1 lane, and it actively defeats the landability filter that would otherwise stop the loop churning on gaps it cannot land.

In scripts/substrate/configure-local.sh, the client config written at bring-up names a model that no longer exists.

Find this exact text:


Reason: claude-sonnet-4-20250514 was deprecated 2026-04-14 and RETIRED 2026-06-15 on the Claude API; requests naming a retired model fail. Anthropic's published replacement for this exact id is claude-sonnet-4-6, which is active with a retirement date no sooner than 2027-02-17. This script is the bring-up path that writes the client config on a fresh deployment, so every new substrate is currently configured with a dead model id.

It does not fail today only because llm-resolver-vessel carries a RETIRED_MODEL_ALIASES table that remaps this one id at call time. That table has exactly one entry, and it is in a different repository from the script that creates the dependency on it. The bootstrap tier is supposed to be the layer that works before anything else exists; here it emits a value that is only valid because a downstream vessel happens to patch it. Naming the live model directly removes the coupling and leaves the alias table as a genuine compatibility shim for old callers rather than as load-bearing infrastructure for the installer.

This is a location-independence defect: the running substrate is healthy because its config predates the retirement and its resolver patches the id, but a deployment brought up today inherits a config whose only protection is a single hardcoded alias.

One line becomes one line; this is a verbatim revert of the change applied by commit 3d648ad (gap route-edit-04925ca8), deployed 2026-09-06 at 10:42:33.

Reason, measured on the live substrate 2026-09-09: that commit made this trace reuse the engine's exec_-prefixed execution_id. But a thin execution row under that exact id already exists by the time this rich trace arrives — activity-api's authoritative store is an INSERT, a duplicate id surfaces as 'already exists', and the handler maps it to an idempotent 200. The sender sees success; the rich trace, the only record that carries input shapes from which execution-traces derives the v1 state-space signature, is silently discarded. Downstream, the only write to context_thompson_scores on the outcome path is guarded on trace.signature, so the discard makes the arm ungradable.

The regression is bracketed to 71 seconds around that deploy: 28 of 994 feature_compose executions carried a signature before 2026-09-06T10:42:05, and 0 of 572 after 10:43:16. The last signed row is execution:feature_compose:3d648ad7b678b187a8784482ed93e476f02bddc3 — the execution that landed the regressing commit was the last one ever graded, and the feature_compose posterior has been frozen at alpha 6.918 / beta 2.973 since 10:42:06 while hundreds of other posterior rows kept updating. Restoring the dedicated id namespace makes the rich trace INSERT land again, which restores signature derivation at ingest and re-opens the keyed posterior write.

The intent behind the original change — joining the reach verdict to the engine's execution record — is now served by a different, landed mechanism: feature-compose emits metadata.reached on the thin row and the executions route grades it (2f01007 plus the emitter, both deployed 2026-09-08). The id unification is therefore no longer load-bearing, and what it actually does today is delete the learning signal it was meant to improve.

In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts there is a landed but INERT block that tries to record a failure outcome against the compose lessons that preceded a failure. It never works: it calls a non-existent endpoint path, sends a wrong auth header, sends a wrongly-shaped body, and mis-types the response — and because it is fire-and-forget, all four fail in silence. Repair it in place by delegating to the resolver that already implements this correctly.

Anchor A — this line occurs exactly once and is inside the broken block:

                await fetch(`${CONCEPT_DB_ENDPOINT}/usage/${concept.id}/fail`, {

Anchor B — this line occurs exactly once, a few lines above it:

            interface ConceptRow { id?: string; }

Replace the broken block so that it does exactly two things.

FIRST, look up the lesson concept ids using the SAME call this file already makes when it recalls lessons — these literals are correct and must be copied exactly, not reconstructed:

  - URL:     `${DISCOVERY_ENDPOINT}/resolve`
  - method:  POST
  - headers: Content-Type application/json, plus an Authorization header whose value is `ApiKey ${apiKey}` built from process.env["METABOB_API_KEY"], set only when that env var is present
  - body:    JSON.stringify({ pointer: { type: "conceptSearch", source_type: "compose_lesson", query: cls, limit: 8 } })

  The response body is shaped { content?: Array<{ content?: string; id?: string }> } — note it is an OBJECT with a content array, NOT a bare array. Read the id off each row in that content array and keep the ones that are present.

SECOND, credit those ids by calling the existing resolver IN-PROCESS rather than re-implementing its HTTP:

  await resolveCreditPrimedConcepts({ type: "credit_primed_concepts", conceptIds: ids, outcome: "failure" });

For that call to compile you must also add this import alongside the other sibling-resolver imports near the top of the file:

  import { resolveCreditPrimedConcepts } from "./credit-primed-concepts.js";

Keep the whole thing best-effort: it must remain wrapped so any error or timeout is swallowed and can never fail or delay the compose. Do not add module-level variables. Do not change composeLessonsBlock. Do not change any other line in the file.

Verified by hand before dispatch: invoking credit_primed_concepts with conceptIds and outcome "failure" moved times_failed from 0 to 1 on a real concept, returning {"credited":1,"errors":0}. That call is known-good; the HTTP the current block performs is known-bad.

On 2026-09-09 the host rebooted; METABOB_API_KEY was absent from /workspace/.substrate-secrets (silently dropped between the 04:42 and 06:53 rewrites on 2026-09-07: .prev is 1099 bytes vs the operator backup's 1276), gen-env minted a fresh key against an already-initialized identity keyspace, every vessel registration 401d, and the discovery registry sat EMPTY while all units reported healthy. The identity-seeder could not self-heal because its login credential IS the regenerated key, and after operator restore it reported key-unchanged/no-restarts-needed even though running processes still held the stale minted key frozen in their env. Fixes in order of leverage: (1) gen-env must refuse to mint a replacement for an auth-critical persisted secret when the identity volume shows an initialized org, failing loudly and naming the backups (minting converts a recoverable outage into a lockout); (2) the writer that rewrites .substrate-secrets must never drop lines it does not understand (the 09-07 silent shrink is the root cause, writer unidentified); (3) the seeder no-restarts-needed check must probe what running consumers actually hold, not whether the file changed during its own run. Working recovery recipe: restore the key from .substrate-secrets.bak-2026-09-07-operator into secrets and /etc/substrate/env, re-run identity-seeder, restart discovery first then the fleet.

summary: The substrate modifies feature-compose.ts - the component that performs all code modification - and nothing executes the result, so regressions accumulate silently in the exact capability needed to detect and repair them. MEASURED: 41 substrate-authored commits to feature-compose.ts across 09-06 and 09-07, after which the composer's core function degraded roughly threefold. The anchor-failure rate (executions with apply_failed AND ops_applied==0) went 3.3% on 09-04 when the file received ZERO commits, to 12.0% on 09-06 (19 commits), 19.0% on 09-07 (22 commits), peaking at 34.4% on 09-08. File growth does not explain it: 3.3% at 6136 lines vs 34.4% at 6401 lines, a 4 percent size difference against a tenfold rate change. One regression inside that burst is CONFIRMED: commit f0cfb91 inverted a single boolean, disabling the blind-edit anchor repair for two days; it passed typecheck, the semantic gate and mitosis cutover. Restoring it (bac7d00) returned the rate to 16.8% over 184 executions, p < 1e-6 against 09-08, indistinguishable from the 19.0% pre-inversion level. ROOT CAUSE: the pipeline logs its own blind spot - TARGET HAS NO TEST FILE: every gate below this point READS the diff; only a test RUNS it - and post-land suites report ran=false. Self-modification without execution-level verification is negative drift. PROPOSED CHANGE: gate a change to any resolver on the self-development path (feature-compose.ts, gap-to-feature.ts, vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts) on EXECUTING a fixed corpus of compose tasks against the modified composer, not merely typecheck plus semantic review; failing that, record the anchor-failure rate per composer commit so a regression is attributable rather than found days later by an operator.

PER-DAY: commits to src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts vs anchor-failure rate (apply_failed AND ops_applied==0), denominators in parens: 09-02 2c 3.3% (30); 09-03 1c 3.8% (106); 09-04 ZERO commits 3.3% (91); 09-05 5c 10.3% (233); 09-06 19c 12.0% (242); 09-07 22c 19.0% (200); 09-08 3c 34.4% (270). All 46 commits authored Substrate Autonomous. SIZE CONTROL: 6136 lines at 3.3% vs 6401 at 34.4% - 4% growth cannot cause a tenfold change. CONFIRMED REGRESSION: git show f0cfb91 is a one-line diff, !r.ok -> r.ok. POWERED FIX RESULT: 31/184 = 16.8% post-fix vs 93/270 = 34.4% on 09-08, p < 1e-6. NOT ESTABLISHED: causal share of any other commit; hourly attribution failed (n per hour 2-14, and the elevation already appears at 09-07 22:00 before all three boundary commits).
